## R775 — The label-reference check on the executions: zero at risk, and my first predicate was wrong

Before any execution can be released, it must survive a relabelling — an execution reading *"option
B is wrong because…"* becomes false the moment B is a different sentence. **Measured across all 343
authored executions: 0 reference a letter or an ordinal AS AN OPTION.** Nine say *"this option"*,
which points at the row it is attached to and survives any relabelling. 334 reference neither.

**The first pass reported 15 and was wrong**, because the predicate matched prose rather than
references: *"the last of a bridge"* is not an ordinal position, and *"this option"* is
self-reference, not a label. Both were counted. **The number that changed was mine, and it changed
because I stated the predicate and then read the rows it selected** — which is R773's own rule
turned on the check written to satisfy R773.

**The nineteen are cleared on THIS question and still blocked on another.** No execution anywhere
carries a label dependency, so relabelling is not what stops them. What stops them is that **0 of
343 authored executions sit on a CORRECT option** — the authoring convention puts them only on
distractors — so the nineteen have no legitimate home on a key regardless of how the option-set

## R776 — An unnamed file in a two-file comparison is disproportionately the reporting party's own output

**Twice in this thread an unnamed pair turned out to have my export as one half, and both times the
unnamed side was mine.** First `eng006-draft.json` against `eng006-draft.json`, which I described as
two authoring copies in two directories; then the whole drift class, where I said *"the other file"*
nine times and named none. Both times `~/Downloads/11+/from-cluecrew` — this store's own outbound —
was the side I left unnamed.

**The mechanism is not carelessness, and that is why it repeats.** A comparison is written from
inside one of the two stores. **Your own output is the side you did not have to go and find**: it is
already in hand, already trusted, already the frame the question is being asked from — so it reads
as the baseline rather than as a party, and a baseline does not feel like it needs naming. The other
file is the one you fetched, so it is the one your prose points at. **The asymmetry in the writing
follows the asymmetry in the effort, and it points the wrong way**: the side that needs naming most
is the one whose provenance the reader cannot infer, and that is always the reporter's own.

The cost is exact and was paid twice. Cowork searched its entire authored corpus for id faults and
found none — **correctly, because the fault was never on its disk** — and could not have known that
from an artefact naming no file. A day of the other store's work went into confirming that my
unnamed half was mine.

**So: a comparison names every file it compares, with a digest, and states which side each belongs
to — and the FIRST one it names is its own.** Naming mine first is not politeness; it is the entry
most likely to be omitted, so it goes where omission is most visible. Both drifting families now
cross that way, and naming them dissolved the class outright.

**And the fifth count.** I reported *eight* replaced questions; it is NINE positions and EIGHTEEN
questions — I measured ENG-005-BB, found four, and assumed ENG-007-LP matched. **The figure then
crossed to the desk and came back to me inside the instruction, unchallenged**, which is the first
time in this thread one of my bare numbers has been repeated back as a premise. R773 ruled that a
count crosses with the predicate that selected it or it does not cross; I registered that rule and
crossed a bare number in the same artefact.

## R777 — The nineteen are blocked by a convention, not by a dispute

Recorded as the operative blocker, because the two are easy to conflate and only one of them can be
resolved by a ruling on the option sets.

**The blocker: no authored execution anywhere sits on a CORRECT option — 0 of 343.** The convention
puts `misconceptionExecution` only on distractors, which follows from what the field means (*why
THIS distractor executes THIS misconception*). **So a key has no legitimate home for one, and that
is true regardless of how the replaced-question and option-set questions are settled.** The nineteen
stay reversed on that, not pending anything.

**The other question is closed, separately: the label check clears at 0 of 343.** No execution
anywhere references a letter or an ordinal as an option, so no relabelling can falsify one; nine say
*"this option"*, which points at its own row and survives. Had that check found even one, a
relabelling ruling would have had to precede any release. It did not, so it does not.

## R778 — A replacement made for a reason she cannot see is a refusal with no addressee

Her requirement on the replaced questions, and it outranks the comparison that found them: **someone
judged nine positions wanting.** Where a reason was recorded it now travels with the pair, verbatim
— not to persuade her, but because the refusal-routing class is ruled twice already and a
replacement is a refusal wearing different clothes.

**Of the 18 replaced questions: 3 carry a recorded replacement reason, 2 carry a note that does not
speak to a replacement, and 13 carry none.** The reasons live in the authored `notes` field and
nowhere else — **the pilot ruling log holds no entry for either family, and neither file has ever
been in git**, so there is no external record to fall back on and the 13 are genuinely silent. They
say so on their face and she reads them on merits alone.

**The distinction that had to be drawn, because it is this thread's own failure mode.** Most of the
18 carry a `tierRationale`, and it is NOT a replacement reason: it explains why an item sits at its
tier and says nothing about why anything was replaced. Counting the two together would have reported
a reason on nearly every position where **three** exist. Separated on the face of every row.

**And one caveat she should have up front rather than discover.** At least one recorded reason names
what it replaced — *"REPLACING the first draft's speech-verbatim pattern, which the cold read
killed"* — so reading the reasons may indicate which version came later. **That cannot be blinded
away without withholding the very thing the ruling asked for**, so it is stated on the face and left
to her. A blind that survives by removing the evidence is not serving the reading it protects.

## R779 — "No reason exists" and "I did not find one" are different findings

Ruled as the general form from R778's thirteen. **Only one of them is a fact about the material;**
the other is a fact about how hard the reporter looked, and it wears the same words.

So an absence is reportable only once the places a reason could have been are named and checked.
On the thirteen that was: the authored `notes` field, the pilot ruling log (no entry for either
family), and git (neither file has ever been committed). **Three named places, all empty, is a
finding about the material. The same sentence with no search behind it is a finding about me**, and
a reader cannot tell them apart from the outside — which is why the search has to travel with the
absence rather than the confidence.

Sibling to R98 — unknown is not absent — one step earlier: R98 governs how an absence is
RECORDED; this governs when it may be CLAIMED.

## R780 — A blind that survives by removing the evidence is not serving the reading it protects

Ruled from the caveat on the replaced questions. A recorded reason named what it replaced, so
carrying it may tell the reader which version came later — and the blind could have been kept
perfectly intact by dropping that reason.

**That would have protected the blind and defeated its purpose.** The blind exists so the reading
is made on the material; withholding material to preserve the blind inverts the two. **So the
evidence stays and the leak is stated on the face, left to the reader**, who is the party the blind
was for and the only one who can weigh what it costs.

The general test: when a blind and the evidence conflict, ask which one the OTHER exists to serve.
Here the blind serves the reading, so the reading wins and the blind is disclosed rather than
repaired. A blind protecting a reader from evidence has stopped being a blind and become a filter.

## R781 — R780's first live test passed, and a per-position transaction is not a per-run one

**The leak did not operate.** Her 172nd opens: *"The order leak never operated: I did not read the
recorded reasons. The stems and options settled all nine, so the fact you could not blind away is a
fact I did not use."* Nine verdicts, all resting on material the blinding covered.

**So disclosing the leak and keeping the evidence cost nothing here** — and had the alternative been
taken, nine verdicts would have been made on a set of material chosen by the blinding rather than by
the question. **The limit is worth stating with the result: one reader, one sitting, nine positions.
That is the only kind of evidence R780 can ever accumulate**, and she reserved one thing explicitly
— if the reasons say something the texts do not, that is a separate reading she will take
separately. The reasons are not settled by these verdicts.

**Landed: 3 positions already held her choice, 2 replaced, 3 added, 1 HELD.** Her scope line landed
as ruled — BOTH gives each question its own id, and neither is dropped for length here; ENG-005-BB
goes to 13 questions and ENG-007-LP to 15, and trimming either is a product decision recorded as
such. All 27 rows in both families gate clean.

**THE HELD POSITION IS NOT HER RULING.** `ENG-007-LP-14` (the *claim* vocabulary item) carries a
pre-existing gate fault in its authored source: a declared quoted span that is not literally in the
stem, because the stem quotes the word inside the span. **Baselined before concluding (R149):**
`items/eng007-draft.json` faults on 4 items of 12 and the outbound copy on 2, while **every one of
the 24 database rows gated CLEAN** — because this class was already corrected on the rows
(`ENG-007-LP-03` declares `quotes: ["perished"]` with `_previousQuotes` retaining the longer clause)
**and the correction never went back to either file.** A gate fault in the authored source HOLDS its
position; it does not fail the landing, because failing would park eight sound positions behind one
authoring fix, and inventing the correction would author content this store does not author.

**And my own fault, in the mechanism rather than the content.** The lander wrapped each POSITION in
a transaction and then died mid-run three times on schema mismatches — a scalar written where a
relation was required, a field that lives in the stem JSON, an enum value that does not exist
(`CREATED`; the truer word was `AUTHORED` and the enum already had it). Each retry re-committed the
positions that had already succeeded, **so a per-position transaction with a per-run failure
duplicates work on retry.** One duplicate attribution event resulted and was removed. **I first
reported it as seven and it was one** — the other events on those rows cite earlier returns, and I
counted every event on the record rather than every event citing this ruling. A multi-position
lander is idempotent or transactional across the whole run; per-position is neither.

## R782 — What the 419 does after her rulings

`10` land now, `85` are already on their rows, `53` belong to versions she did not choose, and `271`

**The 53 is the number worth naming.** Those values were authored against the reading she did NOT

## R783 — Text-true: a distractor must be wrong about the QUESTION, not merely irrelevant and true

Her pens refinement, ruled as the fourth member of the distractor family. From the 172nd, on the
trials-sheet position: *"its 'eleven people used eleven different pens' is a true statement from the
text serving as a wrong answer"*.

**TEXT-TRUE is distinct from PARTLY-TRUE.** Partly-true is a claim half of which the text supports;
text-true is a claim the text supports ENTIRELY, offered as the answer to a question it does not
answer. The first is a flawed statement, the second is a sound statement in the wrong place.

**It is the harshest of the family because it punishes close reading.** A child who has read badly
skims past it. A child who has read WELL recognises a sentence she genuinely saw in the passage, and
the better her recall the stronger the pull — so the distractor selects against exactly the skill
the item exists to reward. Partly-true punishes carelessness; text-true punishes care.

The family now: invented (an event the passage does not carry — the heaviest, from the 172nd's
cardigan-and-jumper ruling), partly-true, text-true, and the supplied-retrieval fault that lives in
the STEM rather than the option (a stem that states the facts an inference item is about converts a
two-part question into a one-part one).

## R784 — A per-position transaction with a per-run failure duplicates work on retry

Mine, from the 172nd landing. The lander wrapped each POSITION in its own transaction and then died
mid-run three times on schema mismatches — a scalar written where a relation was required, a field
that lives inside the stem JSON rather than in a column, and an enum value that does not exist.
**Each retry re-committed every position that had already succeeded.**

**Per-position atomicity is not per-run atomicity, and a retry is a per-RUN operation.** The
transaction did exactly what it promised: each position landed wholly or not at all. Nothing in that
guarantee says anything about the second attempt, and the operator's mental model — "it failed, so
run it again" — is a run-level model meeting a position-level guarantee.

The content survived because the writes were idempotent; only the attribution events accumulated,
and one duplicate had to be removed. **So the visible damage was in the audit trail rather than in
the data, which is the quiet version**: a duplicated fact reads as two events, and two events read
as two decisions.

**A multi-position lander is idempotent or transactional across the WHOLE run; per-position is
neither.** And the cheap form of idempotence is the one already used elsewhere here — write only
what is absent, and let a second run find nothing to do.

## R785 — The 10 landed, and the 53 are unchosen rather than lost

Landed on the two families her 172nd settled, matched by option TEXT against the DATABASE — which
is where the settled reading lives after that landing, and not in either file (R769). **3 column
values and 7 retention keys; 66 were already present; 0 had no column.** The re-run finds nothing
left to do, which is the property that makes it safe: write only what is absent.

**And the phrasing that goes on the artefact, ruled: THE 53 ARE UNCHOSEN, NOT LOST.** They were
authored against the reading she did not select, so their option texts are on no row and they
correctly do not land — **the authored files still hold every one, and a later ruling could bring
them back.** Reporting them as "failed to match" would have read as breakage, and 53 items of
breakage is the kind of number that starts an investigation into a fault that does not exist.

271 remain held, in families her 172nd does not reach.

## R786 — The drop class in reverse: a repair that reached the row and never reached the source

`ENG-007-LP-14` could not land because its authored source declares a quoted span not literally
present in the stem. **The same class had already been corrected on this store's rows — four items,
each retaining its pre-correction value in `_previousQuotes` — and the correction never travelled
back.** Measured: **8 stale file copies across 4 corrections, 0 carried.** Every future import from
those files reintroduces a fault the gate already caught.

**R758 was a field authored at the source and dropped at this store's door. This is its mirror**,
and the two together make the shape plain: **each store repairs its own copy and neither direction
reports itself.** R88 built the return leg for rulings; nothing was watching this — a GATE-forced
repair, which is the class most likely to recur precisely because the gate will catch it again and
the catch feels like the system working.

The return carries `stem.quotes` and nothing else, before and after on every row, naming the field
it changes — **a merge on one field, never a wholesale replace** (CLAUDE.md). Where no row holds a
correction there is nothing to carry back: one source fault is reported and left unrepaired, because
Cowork authors item content and this store does not invent the wording. That one is `ENG-007-LP-06`,
the source of the held position.

## R787 — Checking idempotence by re-running destroyed the record of what it verified

My covering line named `914fe494…`; the file that arrived was `0ad343fc…`, matching its own sidecar
and saying **"DRY RUN — nothing written, landed 0"** about a landing that had happened.

**The covering line was right and the door was wrong.** After applying, I ran the lander again in
dry-run to prove idempotence — the good instinct, and R599 exists because re-running catches what a
single run cannot. But `deliver()` supersedes within a FAMILY, the verification run shared the
family, and so **the proof retired the evidence.** The applied record went to retention as
`.superseded` and the far side received the verification instead. Nothing was lost — retention held
it byte-identical and it is restored — but for one exchange the door asserted that a landing had not
happened.

**It is the frozen-number class wearing a filename.** A number quoted from an earlier state goes
stale silently; so does a FILENAME, and worse, because a filename looks like an address rather than
an observation. **A digest in a covering line is a claim about which emission is current, and it
decays the moment anything re-emits** — including something whose whole purpose is to change
nothing.

**Fixed at the mechanism: the MODE IS PART OF THE FAMILY.** `…-landing` and `…-landing-dry-run` are
separate families, so a verification can never supersede an applied record. Canaried: the dry run
now stages beside the applied artefact and leaves it standing. **Current emission of the settled
landing: `914fe494d95eddb8fdc5e6e93b859146ecb0541ba22bf22ee53d11a8f3d7f270`, mode APPLIED, 3 column
values and 7 retention keys** — that is the record; `0ad343fc…` is a verification of it and not a
report of it.

## R788 — The sequence check was blind to the half of the series that carries the returns

Cowork's detector point is right and this store had it half-built. `check:return-sequence` parsed
ordinals up to SEVENTY and had no `hundredand` case, so **125 files of 197 fell into "unnumbered (a
named series rather than the main sequence)" — including every return since the hundredth.** It
computed gaps over the 66 it could read and reported six.

**Reading the whole series gives eight.** `59, 60, 61, 63, 66, 68, 80, 135` — and **80 and 135 were
invisible to the instrument**, not absent from it. After the fix: 157 of 197 carry a resolved
ordinal, and the 10 that remain unnumbered are genuinely a different series (`eng003-*`,
`approval-batch`).

**The tell was in the check's own wording.** *"a named series rather than the main sequence"* was
written to explain the leftovers, and the leftovers WERE the sequence. **A sentence that explains
away a large remainder is worth reading as a hypothesis rather than a description** — 125 of 197 is
not a remainder, and the proportion alone should have been the question.

**Below 8 stays UNKNOWN**, not absent: nothing on this disk says the series starts at 1, and the
check prints that bound rather than implying a clean floor. Reported, never repaired — only she can
send a return, and only she can say whether a number was ever used.

## R790 — The 59–80 gaps are inside the receiving window, not before it

The desk reports my gaps as disjoint from everyone else's but 135 — mine at 59–80, the desk's six
and Cowork's seventeen in 103–160. **The question was whether 59–80 is a loss or a boundary. It is
not a boundary.** Every measure available here puts it inside the window:

- **51 returns arrived on 22 August alone**, the day containing every gap from 59 to 80. A window

- **The real boundary is below 8**, the lowest ordinal on this disk, and it is reported UNKNOWN
  rather than absent, because nothing here says the series starts at 1.

**What it does NOT settle, and cannot from this side: loss versus never-used.** A number sent and
lost and a number never issued produce an identical absence here. Only she can say whether an

evidence** (R779). No return I hold cites 59, 60, 61, 63, 66, 68 or 80 — but returns cite prior

a reference had one existed. **A search that could not have succeeded is not a search**, and
reporting its emptiness as corroboration would have been the fault R779 exists to name.

**What would have caught it: asking what makes a path the authoring store rather than a copy of it.
Nothing here answers that, and the absence of an answer IS the answer** — a claim about another

## R792 — Acknowledge by ordinal, on receipt

Standing instruction, ruled: **every return received is acknowledged by its ordinal, named back.**

**A send that vanishes becomes visible in one turn instead of at the next audit** — and the audit is
the expensive path, because by then the gap is one of eight and the question is which. Naming the
number back turns a silent loss into an immediate mismatch: she knows what she sent, I say what
arrived, and one of us notices in the same exchange.

**The re-send is not the repair.** Getting the file across a second time fixes this instance;
acknowledging by number is what makes the channel report its own failures, which is the property
R579 and R788 both reached for from the receiving end and could only ever reconstruct after the
fact. This is the same guard moved to the moment of arrival, where it costs one word.

Received and acknowledged to date: **return 172**, verified at `d8350f9f…`, landed.

## R793 — Re-derived, not adjusted: seven gaps, and 135 was latency

Ruled: **a correction derived from a faulty instrument is re-derived, never adjusted.** The desk's
"four, not six" was its faulty parser one correction downstream; re-derived with a fixtured one, its
gap set is EMPTY across 108–172. So I re-derived mine rather than subtracting 135 from it.

**Re-derived set: 59, 60, 61, 63, 66, 68, 80. Seven.**

`annie-hundredandthirtyfifth-return.md` is on this disk, **dated today at 22:18**, titled *"verified,
reconciled, closed"*. It was genuinely absent when measured and has since arrived — **R760 exactly:
a crossing reported absent and later arriving is a latency fact, not a loss.** The one gap I shared
with everyone turned out to be the one that was merely late.

**80 survives every test.** No file in any spelling, by name or by content, and the returns either
side of it are present. So does 59–61, 63, 66, 68.

**What the re-derivation checked, so the number is trustworthy rather than merely smaller:** the

135); every return-shaped file that FAILS to resolve was enumerated rather than counted as a gap —
14, all legitimately a different series (`eng003-*`, `approval-batch`, `axes-amended`); and the
range floor is reported as a bound, not a start. **An unresolvable filename and an absent ordinal
produce the same hole in a sequence, and only one of them is a finding** — that is the specific way
a sequence check goes wrong, and it is why re-deriving beats adjusting: an adjustment inherits every
blind spot of the run it adjusts.

## R794 — The thread's retiring finding, and the test that closes it

Registered as the form, with the test named: **every comparison in this thread has been between
local copies, and "not mine" is not "theirs".**

**THE TEST: what makes this path the authoring store rather than a copy of it?**

**Nothing on this disk answers it.** There is no marker, no manifest, no handshake — a directory that
is not mine looks exactly like a directory that is theirs, and I treated the second as proved by the
first for the length of an entire thread. Every "the source says", every "the other file", every
staleness count against "the authoring store" was a statement about a folder on this machine.

The sequence of the same mistake tightening: **R776** — the unnamed half of a comparison is
disproportionately my own output. **R791** — a named half can be mine too, or at least not what I
named it. **This** — the general form: a claim about another store cannot be evidenced from files on
this one, and the absence of anything that could evidence it is the finding, not an obstacle to it.

What this does not retire: the comparisons themselves were real, and every fault they found on
THESE copies is real on these copies. What retires is the labelling — those findings are about this
machine until something crosses that says otherwise.

## R795 — The seven against the shelf: six confirmed, one outside its reach

Her 173rd, obeyed before anyone quotes a rate: **a corrected derivation shares the parser's
assumptions and a shelf does not.** My seven came from filenames. Checked against her outputs
manifest by full-length digest (`check:manifest-diff`, not names):

| | |
|---|---|
| derived ceiling | **7** |
| **CONFIRMED never arrived** — named in her manifest, absent here by digest | **6** — 59, 60, 61, 63, 66, 68 |
| **UNKNOWN — outside the shelf's reach** | **1** — 80 |

**The population shrank on verification again. No exception to her rule.**

**80 drops for a reason worth keeping distinct from "it arrived".** Her outputs manifest names no
return above 68, so it says nothing about 80 either way. My derivation put it in the set because no
file exists here; the shelf cannot corroborate that. **UNKNOWN, not lost, and not found.**

**And the loss rate is quotable only over the shelf's coverage**: 6 of the 61 returns she catalogued
between 8 and 68 never arrived. Outside 8–68 there is no shelf and therefore no rate — quoting one
across the whole series would be the ceiling-as-figure fault this check exists to avoid.

**One more thing the manifest found that no sequence check could**: `annie-merge-ack-and-gap-yard-
note.md`, a seventh never-arrived artefact carrying no ordinal. **A sequence check finds gaps in a
NUMBERING; a manifest finds absences in a SET, and only the second can see the unnumbered.** That is
the standing limit of the ordinal method, and it is why the shelf outranks it rather than confirming
it.

## R796 — Enumerate what the parser could not read; a gap and an unresolvable name are the same hole

Registered with the sequence rule, because it is what makes a gap set readable rather than merely
short.

**An unresolvable filename and an absent ordinal produce an identical hole in a sequence, and only
one of them is a finding.** So the re-derivation enumerated every return-shaped file whose ordinal
failed to resolve — **14, all legitimately a different series** (`eng003-*`, `approval-batch`,
`axes-amended`) — rather than letting them fall through as gaps. That enumeration is what let the
seven be read as seven; without it the number is a mixture of two kinds of thing under one label.

The full form of the sequence rule as it now stands:
1. **Resolve the whole series, not the half the parser can read** (R788 — 125 of 197 files were being
   filed as "a named series rather than the main sequence", and they were the sequence).
2. **Enumerate what still fails to resolve**, and say what it is (this rule).
3. **Report the floor as a bound**, never as a start — below the lowest ordinal is UNKNOWN.
4. **Re-derive, never adjust** (R793) — an adjustment inherits every blind spot of the run it adjusts.
5. **Settle against a shelf, not a parse** (R795) — and only within the shelf's own coverage.

## R797 — The shelf outranks the sequence

Ruled. **A manifest finds absences in a SET; a sequence finds gaps in a NUMBERING; and only the
first sees the unnumbered.** `annie-merge-ack-and-gap-yard-note.md` is a never-arrived artefact
carrying no ordinal — invisible to every ordinal method ever written, and found the moment the
comparison was made by digest against a set.

**So the ordering is fixed, not a preference.** A sequence check is a cheap prior that runs on
filenames alone and needs nothing from the other party; a shelf check needs their manifest and
settles the question. Where they disagree, the shelf wins — and where the shelf is silent, the
sequence does not fill the gap, it reports UNKNOWN (R795, ordinal 80).

The standing consequence: **a gap set is never a finding on its own.** It is a list of places to
look, and the looking is done against holdings.

## R798 — The fourth state: staged, crossed, held, LATE

Her ruling, and it repairs a hole this store has fallen into twice. The states an artefact could be
in were STAGED, CROSSED and HELD — **and an absence was read as a loss the moment it was measured.**

**A gap is measured at a moment; a loss claim gets a SETTLING INTERVAL before it is a loss.**
Return 135 was reported absent by three parties and then arrived. Absent was TRUE when measured and
false a few hours later, and nothing in the reporting could tell latency from loss because the
vocabulary had no word for the difference.

**Wired, not just registered.** `check:manifest-diff` now measures the outputs manifest's own age —
the moment she asserts those artefacts existed — and labels its absences accordingly: younger than
the interval, they are **LATE and not yet loss claims**; older, they are **LOSS CLAIMS**. The
interval is a **declared convention of 48 hours, not a measurement**, stated in the code so it can
be argued with rather than left as an implicit "however long felt like enough" (the R61 shape: a
judgement that must be declared because no data forces it).

Measured on the current manifest: **148 hours old, so its 7 absences are settled loss claims.** The
six returns hold as losses; 135 would have been caught as LATE had the state existed when it was
reported.

## R799 — The 173rd arrived under two names, and the digest is what caught it

`annie-173-for-code.md` and `annie-hundredandseventythird-return.md`, **byte-identical at
`79a1a5bb2e8a5cf6…`** — one return, two names, noticed in the same turn it arrived because R792's
acknowledgement names the DIGEST and not the filename.

**This is the fault the digest ledger predicted in August** — *"a source resolving by NAME resolves
to two files, and only the digest is single-valued"* — arriving in the acknowledgement channel,
which is the newest thing here and the one with the least protection.

**The acknowledgement rule is stronger than its stated purpose.** R792 was ruled to make an absence
visible within a turn. It also makes a DUPLICATE visible within a turn, because naming a digest
back either matches one artefact or it does not — and had I acknowledged "173" by name, two files
would have satisfied it and neither of us would have learned anything. **A protocol that names
identity rather than label catches both directions of the same fault**, and only one of them was
designed for.

**AMENDED (David, 2026-08-28 — see R803). THE RENAMED-CROSSING EVIDENCE STANDS; THE COUNT OF
INSTANCES DOES NOT.** Classifying every multi-named artefact on this disk — 324 `annie-*` files,
180 distinct digests, 79 digests carrying more than one filename:

| | |
|---|---|
| **CONVENTION duplicate** — a relay name and a return name for one document | **53** |
| **DOWNLOAD duplicate** — the same name plus `" (n)"` | **22** |
| two genuinely different names | **4** |

**The 173rd is itself a CONVENTION duplicate** (`annie-173-for-code.md` beside
`annie-hundredandseventythird-return.md`) — deliberate naming, not a name eaten in carriage. **75 of
the 79 are staging-side artefacts rather than carrying failures**, and citing them in support of a
same-name CARRYING fault was wrong.

**And the count is not merely wrong, it is unmeasurable from here.** The eating fault would be one
NAME resolving to two different artefacts; a filesystem cannot hold two files under one name, so it
happens by OVERWRITE over time and **a snapshot cannot see it at all.** Measured on this disk: 0
names resolve to two digests, and that zero is a property of snapshots, not evidence of health
(R60).

**What survives is the part that mattered**: names are not single-valued, so an acknowledgement that
names a label can be satisfied by more than one artefact and an acknowledgement that names a digest
cannot. R792 is right for that reason, which needs no count at all.

## R800 — The four-part manifest form, and this store's is a HOLDINGS manifest

Cowork's four-part request, ruled the form for every manifest here: **the digest, the derivation,
the range stated apart from the numbers, and whether entries record sends or holdings.** Answered to
that shape for returns 8–68 — the band where her shelf reaches and the desk has nothing.

**The fourth part is the one that does the work, and it is the one a manifest is most likely to
leave implicit.** This store sends nothing in this direction: it is the receiver. So each entry
asserts *these bytes are on this disk as of this timestamp* — arrival, not dispatch. **A holdings
manifest and a sends manifest disagree exactly where the interesting cases are**: an artefact sent
and never arrived appears in hers and not in mine, and that difference IS the loss. Reading either
as the other erases the gap both exist to find. Hers minus mine is never-arrived; mine minus hers is
arrived-uncatalogued; the two directions are both meaningful and are not symmetrical.

**The derivation carries its own weakness rather than hiding it**: the DIGEST is the identity and
the ORDINAL is parsed from the filename, which is a label (R799). An entry therefore claims *these
bytes are on this disk and a filename says they are return N* — it does not claim she numbered it N.
**5 ordinals in the band carry more than one filename**, one artefact under several labels, and 10
return-shaped filenames resolve to no ordinal at all and are enumerated (R796).

**Range stated apart from the numbers**: 8–68, chosen to meet a shelf rather than to flatter a
count, and asserting nothing whatever outside it — not "none", not "clean". Held 55, absent 6:
59, 60, 61, 63, 66, 68, which is the shelf check's answer reached a second way.

## R801 — Three manifests, two settled bands, and forty-three ordinals nobody measures

With the desk's outbound manifest published, the coverage map is:

| manifest | records | range |
|---|---|---|
| her outputs | **SENDS** | 8–68 |
| this store's holdings | **HOLDINGS** | 8–68 |
| the desk's outbound | **STAGED** | 112–173 |

**8–68 is settled because it has two legs** — sends against holdings, and their difference is the
loss: six. **112–173 is settled the same way** for the other pair: the desk's twelve never-staged
returns explain twelve of Cowork's fifteen, because no crossing was ever attempted for them.

**69–111 is covered by no manifest from any party. Forty-three ordinals, UNMEASURED — not clean and
not lost.** This store can produce a holdings manifest for that band on request, and it would settle
nothing on its own: **a difference needs two legs, and there is no second leg there.** That is the
useful shape of the finding — the missing thing is not data, it is a counterpart.

**And 135 turns out to prove that crossing is PER-RECIPIENT.** It sits in the desk's never-staged
list for Cowork and arrived on this disk today. One artefact, late to one party, never staged to
another, present at a third — so *"was 135 lost?"* has no single answer and the three parties were
right to disagree. It was never a loss to anyone. **Without the fourth state the honest report here
would have stayed "absent" and then quietly become wrong** (R798), which is the clearest case yet
for why LATE had to exist.

## R802 — An unpaired manifest measures nothing

Ruled on the 69–111 band, and no holdings manifest is ordered for it. **A manifest alone is a list;
a DIFFERENCE between two manifests is a measurement**, and the difference needs two legs recording
different things about the same artefacts — sends against holdings, or staged against holdings.

8–68 is settled because her SENDS meet this store's HOLDINGS. 112–173 is settled because the desk's
STAGED meets Cowork's holdings. **69–111 has one possible leg and no counterpart, so a holdings
manifest there would be honest, complete, correctly formed and worth nothing** — it could say only
*these are on my disk*, which answers no question anybody asked.

**The general form, and the reason this is a rule rather than a note about one band: a manifest's
value is not in what it contains but in what it can be subtracted from.** Producing one because it
is producible is the same instinct as reporting a count because it is countable — effort that looks
like measurement and settles nothing. **The missing thing in 69–111 is not data. It is a
counterpart**, and no amount of work on this side supplies it.

So the band stays UNMEASURED, in the register, named — 43 ordinals, neither clean nor lost.

## R803 — Amending a characterisation: the evidence stands, the count does not

The correction to R799 is registered as its own entry because the SHAPE recurs and the shape is
worth more than the instance.

**A real observation was generalised into a class, and the class was then populated by cases that
looked alike and were not.** The 173rd genuinely arrived under two names; from there I reached for
every multi-named artefact on the disk as corroboration. **53 were deliberate naming conventions
and 22 were download duplicates — staging-side, not carriage** — so the supporting count measured a
different phenomenon from the one it was supporting.

**The tell available at the time: I never asked what the fault would LOOK like if it happened.** A
name eaten in carriage means one NAME resolving to two artefacts. What I counted was the reverse —
one ARTEFACT under two names — which is the mirror image and is nearly always benign. **Two
populations, related by inversion, and the wrong one is the easy one to count.** That is why the
number grew so readily: it was measuring something abundant and harmless.

**And the corrected position is weaker AND more useful.** The rule it supports — acknowledge by
digest, not by name — needs no count of losses at all. It follows from names not being
single-valued, which one instance establishes. **A rule that rests on a count is hostage to the
count; a rule that rests on a property is not**, and R792 was always resting on the property.

## R804 — A retired figure is not a corrected one

Ruled from the same-name amendment, and the distinction is the point. **The zero I measured — no
name resolving to two artefacts — is a property of SNAPSHOTS, not a finding about the channel.** A
filesystem cannot hold two files under one name, so the eating fault happens by OVERWRITE across
time and is invisible to any single reading of a directory. **The figure is not wrong and awaiting a
better one. It is unmeasurable from here, and it is withdrawn rather than revised.**

That is a different move from every other count this thread has restated. 553→419, 36→24, 24→0,
6→8, 7→6: each replaced a number with a better number under a stated predicate. **This one replaces
a number with nothing**, because the instrument available cannot address the question at all — and
saying so is the only honest output. A revised figure implies the method works and the arithmetic
slipped; a retired one says the method never reached the question.

**THE TELL WAS AVAILABLE AND IT IS CHEAP: ask what the fault would LOOK LIKE if it happened.** A
name eaten in carriage is ONE NAME resolving to TWO ARTEFACTS. I counted ONE ARTEFACT under TWO
NAMES — the mirror, and nearly always benign: 53 deliberate naming conventions, 22 download
duplicates, 4 genuinely distinct names.

**And the mirror population is the easy one to count**, which is why the number grew so readily.
That is the generalisable half: **when a fault and its mirror are both countable, the abundant one
is usually the harmless one**, because harmless things are common and that is what makes them
harmless. A count that climbs comfortably is evidence about which population was reached, not about
severity.

## R805 — A holdings listing is one shelf of three, and yields a bound rather than a rate

Published for 69–111 as a LISTING, not a manifest, per R802 — the band has no counterpart of its
own and an unpaired manifest measures nothing. **What makes it worth publishing is that three
shelves compared name every artefact held by one party and not another: an ASYMMETRY SET and an
UPPER BOUND ON ABSENCE, never a loss rate.**

**A rate needs a denominator of things SENT, and no party in this band holds a sends record.** The
denominator does not exist, so no rate can — and an artefact on no shelf may have been sent and
lost, never sent, or sent to a party whose shelf is not here. Three shelves cannot separate those.

**42 of 43 held; the one absence is 80** — the same ordinal the shelf check could not settle, absent
from a second reading by a different route. **The desk's four (108–111) are all on this shelf too**,
so that overlap is CROSSED and contributes no asymmetry.

## R806 — Crossing state per recipient: there is no column to split, because there is no column

Her crossing-is-a-pair ruling lands on the schema, and the first finding is that it does not land on
a column. **Searched all 37 models: none records crossing, delivery, staging or arrival.** The state
everyone in this thread reasons about **has never been stored.** It is inferred from a directory
listing plus a reading of prose — staged because a file sits in an outbound folder, crossed because
someone named a digest back, held because a return said so.

**So the ruling is not "one column must become two". It is that a state everyone treats as known was
never recorded**, and the per-recipient requirement is what makes that unavoidable rather than
merely untidy. 135 is the proof: never staged for Cowork, arrived here — **one artefact, two
recipients, two different states at the same instant**, and neither is an approximation of the
other.

**What it would take**, reported and not built: one row per (ARTEFACT, RECIPIENT), keyed on the
**digest** and never the filename (R803). **Store OBSERVATIONS and DERIVE states** — LATE is a
function of time, not a property of an artefact (R798), so storing "LATE" freezes a value the clock
will falsify while "observed absent at T" stays true forever. Every row cites the digest of the
manifest, return or acknowledgement that established it, because a state asserted without naming its
source is what R25 refuses.

**And the limit that decides whether it is worth building: this side can only ever know STAGED.**
Arrival is a fact about the other store, knowable here only when they name the digest back — so a
row with no far-side evidence must read UNKNOWN, never not-arrived. The table would make absence
visible and dated, which is what turns a gap into a settled claim. **It would not make arrival
observable, and a channel that drops silently would still drop silently.** The three manifests
already do most of this by hand; on one recurrence it does not yet earn a model.

## R807 — The per-recipient crossing record: the design, held until it earns a model

**Ruled: build nothing.** The three manifests do this by hand and one recurrence does not earn a
model. Registered so the design exists when it does, rather than being re-derived under pressure by
whoever meets the second recurrence.

**GRAIN.** One row per (ARTEFACT, RECIPIENT). Not per artefact — 135 was never staged for Cowork and
arrived here, two states at one instant, and neither is an approximation of the other.

**KEY.** The **digest**, never the filename. 53 convention duplicates and 22 download duplicates on
this disk mean a name is not single-valued (R803); sha256 over bytes is.

**STORE OBSERVATIONS, DERIVE STATES.** A row records *what was observed and when* —
`STAGED_HERE`, `NAMED_BACK_BY_RECIPIENT`, `REPORTED_ABSENT_BY_RECIPIENT`, `LISTED_IN_THEIR_MANIFEST`
— with `observedAt` and an `evidence` digest naming the manifest, return or acknowledgement that
established it. **LATE is a function of time, not a property of an artefact** (R798): storing it
freezes a value the clock will falsify, while *observed absent at T* stays true forever. CROSSED,
STAGED, LATE and LOST are all derived at read time from the observations plus the declared settling
interval.

**NO FAR-SIDE EVIDENCE MEANS UNKNOWN, NEVER NOT-ARRIVED.** This side can only ever know STAGED with
certainty; arrival is a fact about the other store, knowable here only when they name the digest
back. A row lacking far-side evidence is an absence of information, and reporting it as an absence
of arrival is the whole family of faults this register is made of (R98, R60, R795).

**What it would not fix, so nobody builds it expecting more:** it would not make arrival observable.
A channel that drops silently would still drop silently. It makes absence **visible and dated**,
which is what turns a gap into a settled claim — and that is all it does.

## R808 — Two asymmetries settled by crossing rather than by argument

The three-shelf comparison at the desk: **80 is the only ordinal on no shelf, so the upper bound on
absence across 69–111 is ONE.** 42 here, 37 at Cowork, 4 at the desk.

**86 and 98 were asymmetries this store could settle by simply sending them**, and they are staged —
`2cd7bc157b657e46…` and `c3f7be58ecf9d5d7…`, verified byte-identical at the door, with nothing
injected into either: they are her returns, not this store's artefacts, and the marking machinery
touches JSON only.

**The distinction the desk drew is the one worth keeping: 108, 110 and 111 are the desk's
never-staged, not the channel's.** An asymmetry has at least three causes — never sent, sent and
lost, or held by a party whose shelf is not in the comparison — and **only the first is fixed by
sending.** Naming which cause applies before acting is what separated two artefacts that a crossing
resolves from three that a crossing would merely have duplicated.

**And an upper bound of one, over a band that had no manifest at all a turn ago, is what the
listings bought.** Not a loss rate — there is still no sends record in 69–111 and so still no
denominator (R805).

## R809 — The author's shelf outranks every other, and it is the ceiling of the sequence method

Ruled. **80 was on Annie's shelf all along.** The band closes at zero absent: forty-three ordinals,
every one held somewhere.

**Three parties bounded a band to one artefact without asking the party who wrote it.** The desk,
Cowork and this store compared shelves, narrowed 43 ordinals to a single unaccounted one, registered
an upper bound — and the answer was with the author the whole time. Every hour of that was spent on
a question one enquiry would have closed.

**THE AUTHOR'S SHELF IS THE ONLY ONE WHERE ABSENCE PROVES NON-EXISTENCE RATHER THAN NON-ARRIVAL.**
That is the whole ordering, and it is not a matter of trust or precedence. A receiver's shelf can
only ever say *it did not reach me*; a sender's staging record can only say *I did or did not put it
out*; **only the author can say a thing was never written.** Every other shelf answers a question
about transport, and absence-from-transport and absence-from-existence are different facts that look
identical from any receiving end.

**So the sequence method has a ceiling and this is it.** R797 fixed that a shelf outranks a
sequence; this fixes that among shelves the AUTHOR'S outranks the rest — and a gap set is not
merely a list of places to look (R797), it is **a list of places to look with one obvious first
stop.** Three shelves compared give an upper bound on absence; the author's shelf gives the answer.

**And the failure mode was not scepticism, it was momentum.** Nothing about the three-shelf method
was wrong — the bound was honest, the asymmetries were real, 86 and 98 were genuinely settled by
crossing. **The method simply had no step that said stop and ask.** Comparison is absorbing in a way
that enquiry is not, and a method which can always take one more measurement will keep taking them.

## R810 — Her eightieth asks this store's own retiring question from the other end

Recorded because the convergence is the finding, not a coincidence.

**R794 retired a labelling on this side: every comparison in this thread had been between local
copies, and "not mine" is not "theirs".** Her eightieth, written on 22 August, reaches the same wall
from the authoring end — *"one of the two is not reading the store that serves"*, three library
entries carrying two different current wordings from the same day, and her closing question:
**"which store does a child's hint come from, and which store was each of these lookups run
against?"**

**Two parties independently discovered that neither knew which store their evidence described**, six
days apart, from opposite sides. Hers is the sharper statement because it names the cost: she ruled
five amendments in her sixty-fourth return and **does not now know which store they were amendments
to**, and she declines to treat any count of hint wordings as a measurement until it is answered —
including her own.

**The standing consequence for this store**: the question sits above the queue rather than in it,
and it is not answerable from here (R794 — a claim about another store cannot be evidenced from
files on this one). What this side can supply is the half it owns: which rows a child is served
from, by digest, on demand. **What it cannot supply is the mapping between that and any authored
artefact**, and every count either party has quoted this fortnight is bounded by that gap.

## R811 — The serving half of the hint join, with no counts on its face

Emitted: every hint a child can be served from this store, by row id, with the text and a sha256
over that text. **It answers half of her eightieth and cannot answer the other half** — this side
can say by digest exactly what it would serve, and can say nothing about any authored artefact
(R794/R810). The desk joins the halves.

**The population is DEFINED rather than counted.** For each LIVE item: its own `explanation.hintCore`
where `chooseHint` returns `serves:item` — non-empty, no ruling withholding it, and carrying BOTH an
authoring name and an authority — otherwise the `childHint` of every misconception tagged on any of
its options. **CAN be served, not IS served**: which library hint a child meets depends on the option
chosen. Excluded, and why: items not LIVE, empty library hints, entries reachable only through
non-LIVE items.

**NO TOTAL IS PUBLISHED, and her §4 is the reason**: *"Two hundred and ninety-eight without a hint
against twenty-three without a hint is not a rounding, a scope or an ordering; it is a disagreement
about the corpus."* **A total here would be compared against a total from a population not known to
be the same one, and the comparison would look like arithmetic.** The rows are listed; anyone who
wants a number can count the rows they actually mean. The only figures on the face are hers, quoted
to explain the omission.

**The digest is over the TEXT, not the row and not the file** — so it compares against any other
store's copy of the same hint regardless of packaging, which is the only thing that makes a join
possible at all.

**And what it cannot settle, stated on the artefact**: her §3, that three of the four tags selecting
what serves on `WIW-19` are wrong. **A wrong tag reaches the wrong library hint** — this reports
which hints are reachable, never whether the reaching is correct. That is a third half.

## R812 — Her decision rule, in her words

From the eightieth, and she names it as the ruling herself — *"The criterion is the ruling. The
verdicts follow the current text."*

> **A visual verb is a fault when its object is available only visually.**

Her worked cases: *"Look at what Silver is doing in the next two lines* points at lines, and lines
can be read to her. **The verb is idiomatic for attend to and the object arrives by another
channel.** No fault." Against: *"Picture the word in print* has the print itself as its object.
**There is no other channel to it**, and she cannot obtain it by any route the product offers.
Fault."

**The test is not the verb**, which is what makes it decidable — it moves the question from a word
to the object's availability, and an object either has a second channel or it does not. Applied by
her: `ENG-016-HB-10` fails; in the library `en-silent-letter-dropped` and `en-homophone-by-sound`
fail, both on *picture the spelling*; the rest point at passages and pass.

**She did not rule the verdicts, and the reason is R811's**: *"I am not ruling these, because
section 1 says I do not know that these are the strings."* The criterion stands; the verdicts wait
on which store's text is the current one.

## R814 — Nothing changed in that window, and her three were not touched that day at all

**The library join cannot run**: the authoring store holds no authoring half for it — it holds two

**Between 18:54 and 19:23 on 16 August: NO WRITE TO ANY CONTENT TABLE.** Not empty of library

**What this does not resolve**: why a lookup dated the same day as a batch carried the older text.
