## R817 — A settling fault, not a store disagreement

Ruled. Her §1 compared library batches stamped `2026-08-22T18:17` against a lookup, and found two
current wordings. **`en-homophone-by-sound` was written again at 20:58:45 that same evening — two
hours and forty-one minutes AFTER the stamp.** The batch is not wrong and the row is not wrong:
**the batch was taken while the store was still being written to.**

**This is the fourth state (R798) applied to EXPORT rather than to ARRIVAL.** LATE was ruled for an
artefact that has not yet crossed; this is its sibling one step earlier — **an artefact exported
before the writing settled is stale by construction, and it does not become stale, it is BORN
stale.** Nothing detects it, because every discipline this store has aims at the crossing: digests,
manifests, acknowledgement. **All of them attest that the bytes that left are the bytes that
arrived, and none of them attests that the bytes that left were the current ones.**

**Why it presents as a store disagreement, which is the part worth remembering.** Two artefacts of
the same date carrying different text looks exactly like two stores holding different text. **The
date is what disguises it** — same day reads as same state, and it is not: 18:17 and 20:58 are the
same date and different stores-in-time. Her eightieth reached for the two-store explanation for
that reason, and so did I.

**The general form: an export's stamp is the moment it was TAKEN, never the moment its contents were
LAST TRUE.** Where those differ, the second is what a reader needs, and no artefact this store emits
carries it. Registered rather than built — the fix is a high-water mark on the source (the latest
write time of anything in the export), and it is not owed until something turns on it a second time.

## R818 — An export's stamp is when it was TAKEN, never when its contents were last true

Her ruling and mine, registered together because neither is complete alone.

**Hers: every batch carries the moment it was cut, and every comparison states both moments or is
not a comparison.** **Mine: an export's stamp is the moment it was TAKEN, never the moment its
contents were LAST TRUE.** The first is the mechanism; the second is why the mechanism is needed —
a single stamp is read as *the state at this time*, and it means only *the state I happened to
copy at this time*.

**Two moments, and they are different questions.** WHEN CUT bounds what could possibly be in the
artefact. WHEN LAST TRUE says whether anything has moved since — and where the source is still being
written to, the second is already in the past when the file is written. `en-homophone-by-sound` at
20:58:45 against an 18:17 stamp is the measured instance (R817).

**"or is not a comparison" is the load-bearing half.** Two artefacts with one moment each cannot be
compared at all: a difference between them may be a disagreement, or may be the interval, and
nothing in either file distinguishes those. **A comparison of two single-stamped artefacts produces
a result that looks like a finding and is an unknown wearing one** — which is what happened to her
eightieth, and to me reading it.

## R819 — BORN STALE: the fifth state, and why every discipline here misses it

STAGED, CROSSED, HELD, LATE (R798) — and now **BORN STALE**: an artefact exported before the writing
settled. **It does not become stale; it is stale at the moment it is written**, and no subsequent
event makes it so.

**Why it evades everything this store has built: every discipline here aims at the crossing.**
Digests, sidecars, manifests, the acknowledgement protocol, the settling interval — **all of them
attest that the bytes that left are the bytes that arrived. None of them attests that the bytes that
left were the current ones.** The whole apparatus watches one hop and is silent about the moment
before it.

**And it is invisible in exactly the way the other four are not.** LATE resolves itself — the
artefact arrives and the state changes. BORN STALE never resolves: **the file is internally
consistent, its digest verifies, its sidecar matches, it crosses cleanly and is wrong.** Every check
passes because every check is asking a different question.

**The distinguishing evidence is not in the artefact and cannot be** — it is the source's write
history, which is why R814 could answer a question no artefact could. The fix is a high-water mark:
the latest write time of anything in the export, carried beside the stamp. Registered, not built.

## R820 — The five are held on a question this store cannot answer

Her ruling: **a source that cannot receive corrections reintroduces every amendment on its next
export.** So the five carry-backs wait, and **if no receive path exists, the path is the work** —
sending them into a store that cannot absorb them would produce the appearance of a repair and the
certainty of a recurrence.

**What this store can contribute is the shape of its own evidence, and it is a null.** Two
carry-backs have been attempted from here: the `stem.quotes` corrections (R786) and these five
hint amendments (R816). The first closed as a no-op — the authoring store already held all four —
**and that is not evidence it received them; it is evidence it had them independently.** So: **this
store has never observed a correction it sent being absorbed at the source.** Not once.

**That null is indistinguishable from a path that works silently**, which is the whole difficulty
and the reason the question is not answerable from here (R794). What would settle it is one
observation crossing back — an artefact from the authoring store carrying text this store sent, by
digest.

**And it reframes the reverse-drop class rather than adding to it.** R786 and R816 read as two
incidents of a repair failing to travel. **If there is no receive path they are not incidents at
all — they are the same structural absence observed twice**, and counting them as recurrences
overstates the evidence for a process fault while understating the case for building the path.

## R821 — Her 176th: WIW-22 takes the authored text, and the replacedSha256 was checked not trusted

Four of her five rewrites keep the serving text; **`ENG-001-WIW-22` takes the authored one**, on her
reason: *"the authored 'list the human things and the animal things, what do you notice' asks for
the same work without doing it for her, and listing is own-paper working, which the rough-paper rule
allows. This row should change, and it is the one place the authored text holds something the
serving text lost."*

**Her `replacedSha256` was VERIFIED against the row before anything was written** — her own rule
(R164): a hash in that field asserts the row's actual prior bytes, so it is checked rather than
accepted. `31d65592…` matched. **A mismatch would have been a stop, not a warning**, because it
would mean one of us was describing a different row — and landing an amendment against a row that
is not the one she read is the fault the field exists to prevent.

Landed with the gate clean, the prior text retained on the row as `_previousHintCore` with its
digest and rule, and one attribution event. **The retained bytes are the actual prior text, not a
reconstruction** (R164 again — a reconstruction may never occupy that field).

**And the carry-back is seven, not five.** Her reclassification moves `WIW-13` and `WIW-20` from
rewrite to house-rule amendment. **This store holds no authored text for either**, so the `before`
cannot be quoted from here — stated per row rather than left blank, because a missing before and an
empty before are different facts (R779). The class on those two is hers; this store could not have
derived it, having nothing to compare.

## R822 — The born-stale field: two timestamps in place of a state nothing could see

Built as ruled. **Every export carries the source's last-write moment taken at the cut, and declares
itself TORN where the last write falls after the cut began.**

**Its whole virtue is that it is not a judgement.** `cutBeganAt` bounds what could possibly be in the
artefact; `sourceLastWriteAt` says when the source last moved; and anyone can compare them without
trusting the emitter. **TORN is not a quality verdict** — a torn export is not wrong, it is one taken
while the store was still being written to, and the reader is told rather than left to infer it from
a date that looks like agreement.

**It reads the source's own write log**, not a file mtime and not a guess, which is the same
instrument that answered R814 when no artefact could. Three outcomes, and the third matters: an
empty write log reports **UNKNOWN, never "clean"** (R60).

**Canaried before trusting it** (R756): with a cut moment in the past it returns TORN, with one taken
now it returns WHOLE. **Both branches reachable, so a WHOLE means something** — a field that could
only ever say WHOLE would be decoration, and this register is largely a record of instruments that
could not fail.

**What it changes about R819.** BORN STALE evaded every discipline here because they all aim at the
crossing. This does not detect staleness either — **it makes the two moments visible so that the
comparison R818 requires is possible at all.** The state stays invisible; the evidence for it stops
being.

## R823 — The maths door cannot be built, and the reason outranks the door

David's instruction anticipated the shape: *"If they do not exist, say that plainly — it is a bigger
finding than the door."* They do not exist, **and the absence is one level deeper than the question
asked.**

**THE CENSUS.** Question types by district: ENGLISH 7, VR 21, **MATHS 0**. Items in a MATHS question
type, at any status: **0**. The question was whether items exist to carry the closed hint class —
**and neither do the QUESTION TYPES they would belong to.** An item cannot exist without a
`questionTypeId`, so this is not a content gap that authoring fills; **it is a missing layer of the
taxonomy.**

**THE DOOR IS NOT BLOCKED BY A POLICY, IT IS BLOCKED BY A FOREIGN KEY.** `Case.questionTypeId` is a
required FK to `QuestionType`, and a MATHS case must point at a MATHS type. **Demonstrated rather
than asserted**: a canary `case.create` inside a rolled-back transaction is REFUSED by the database.
So nothing of case-en-06's pattern was re-derived, because the pattern is not what stops it — the
row cannot be inserted. What would be needed first, in order: a QuestionType row in district MATHS,
items authored against it, signatures on those items, and then the pattern applies unchanged.

**THE BLAST RADIUS IS ZERO AND IT IS WALKED**, from `item where questionType.district = MATHS`, not
carried from anywhere. The instruction was to refuse on any count that cannot be walked; this one is
walked.

**THE THREE WALLS, DERIVED.** *Hints attested*: **111 MATHS library entries, every one carrying a
child-facing hint and every one carrying an approver** — the class closed at 106 and the store holds
more. **This is the only wall that stands.** *Items signed*: 0 of 0, reported **VACUOUS** rather than
passed — a wall over an empty population is not a wall (R61). *Gates green*: both maths gates print
their declared-empty state, exactly as R61 requires — `verify:solutions` says *"MATHS items is
EMPTY, and that is DECLARED LEGITIMATE — not a pass."*

**PUBLICATION IS HELD, AND NOT BY CHOICE.** No transaction is prepared because no membership exists
to flip.

**And the finding that outranks the door: the teaching half of a district is authored, reviewed,
approved and stored, and there is nothing anywhere that can carry it to a child.** 111 hints with no
item, no question type and no case. **R60 recorded that the maths gates had never screened anything
and read it as an instrument fault to be closed by declaration.** It was not an instrument fault.
The gates were right, the declaration was right, and **the thing the declaration described as a
temporary gap is the whole district.** A correctly declared empty population is still an empty
population, and declaring it stopped anyone asking why it was empty.

## R824 — The maths district built: taxonomy, 178 items, a case that fails closed

One run. **Publication holds: every item DRAFT, nothing LIVE, the case face EMPTY.**

**The taxonomy.** Seven MATHS question types created. `mechanic` is required by the schema and the
staged data carries none, so it was **derived where the arithmetic decides it and DECLARED where it
does not**: the inventory's engine totals decompose exactly onto group totals — SHAPE SHOP 30 = GEOM
30, DATA DESK 12 = STATS 12, NPV 35 / MEAS 32 / RP 11 each fitting one side only. **CALC and FDP are
both 40 and cannot be separated by counting**, so those two are assigned by meaning and flagged as
such on the artefact rather than presented as derived.

**The import: 178 landed, 18 refused.** The English importer's DOOR was reused — the shared
`stemSchema` (R57) and `checkItemChildFacing` — but not its WRAPPER, which globs `ENG-*.json` and
carries passage refs. **Renaming a maths batch to satisfy that glob would have been a lie in a
filename.**

**The first run refused 38, and half of that was my door's fault.** CLAUDE.md's HOUSE NOTATION rule
says an import door **NORMALISES then gates**; mine gated without normalising, so twenty items
refused on `"5.00 pounds"` where the house form is `£5.00` — the rule's own declared normalisation,
not a content fault. With `normaliseMathsNotation` wired in: refusals 38 → 18 and hint faults 10 →
0. **The degree sign still refuses and should**: the rule reports it and never auto-inserts, because
a bare `C` may be a label.

**The 18 that remain are real, and they are the finding David predicted.** No gate in either store
had ever screened maths text. Seven items say **"error"** in child UI, one says **"wrong"**, eight
carry `8C` where the house form is `8°C`, four have stems over the sixteen-word cap, one breaks the
long-word rule. **First screening of a district, and it refuses one item in eleven.**

**The tag join is clean: every misconception tag on every staged item resolves to an attested MATHS
library entry.** Zero pointing at nothing — the one wall that was already standing (R823) turns out
to join perfectly to the items that arrived to meet it.

**The case**: `case-maths-01`, MATHS via `maths-calc`, PAID, **face EMPTY and failing closed**,
mapping all seven types. Built on case-en-06's pattern unchanged, now that the foreign key can be
satisfied.

**And a field that does not exist.** The staging file declares `approvedBy: null` per item so a
receiver reads UNSIGNED rather than UNKNOWN — **but Item has no `approvedBy`; that column is on
Misconception.** An Item's signature field is `reviewedBy`, so the declared null landed there,
written explicitly rather than omitted. The distinction is preserved: **0 of 178 carry a reviewer
signature, and not one maths item has ever been through a reviewer.**

## R825 — A door that gates without normalising reports the rule's own normalisation as a content fault

Mine, and it cost twenty false refusals on the first maths import. CLAUDE.md's HOUSE NOTATION rule
is explicit — **"An import door NORMALISES then gates"** — and my door gated only. So twenty items
were refused on `money-word: "5.00 pounds"` where the house form is `£5.00`: **the rule's own
declared normalisation, reported as though the authoring store had broken a rule it had merely
written in the un-normalised form the rule expects to receive.**

With `normaliseMathsNotation` wired in at the door: refusals 38 → 18, hint faults 10 → 0.

**The shape worth keeping: a normalisation and a violation are indistinguishable at the gate, and
only the door knows which it is looking at.** The gate's job is to say *this text breaks a rule*;
the door's job is to say *this text is not yet in house form, and house form is defined*. Skip the
second and every declared normalisation presents as the first — **against the authoring store,
whose text was never wrong.**

**And the boundary the rule already drew held**: money normalises, the degree sign does NOT. `8C`
still refuses, because a bare `C` may be a label and the rule reports rather than inserts. **A door
that normalised everything would have been the same fault in the other direction** — silently
rewriting a label into a temperature.

## R826 — Three signals tried, three withdrawn: this store cannot screen for the mis-join she named

Her ruling: **a hint signed against an entry is not a hint verified against its item, and one
mis-join means a mechanism, not an accident.** Asked to report membership across 178. **The
membership is not deliverable, because every signal I built measured something else.**

1. **Hint names a number absent from stem and key** — 22 rows. Every one a hint doing its job:
   supplying 180 for angles on a straight line, 100 for place value. The signal measured *hint adds
   information*, which is what a hint IS.
2. **Hint's operation disagrees with the stem's** — 5 rows. The word list conflates senses:
   *altogether* counted as addition in "how many hundreds are there altogether in 3,400"; *change*
   counted as subtraction in "change 6 kg into grams".
3. **Execute the hint's operation and compare with the key** — 14 of 54 executable. The executor
   assumes ONE operation over the stem's FIRST TWO numbers. *"25% of £80 — 25% is a quarter, so
   divide by four"* executed as 25 ÷ 80. *"Add a long and a short side, then double"* truncated to
   the addition. *"Divide the area by the length to get the width first"* — the hint says first.

**Nineteen members delivered to her sitting would have been nineteen clean items to re-read, and the
reading would have been about my regexes.** Withdrawn before crossing, and the artefact carries the
withdrawal rather than the numbers.

**The consistency across three attempts is the finding.** Every mechanical proxy for *the hint
contradicts the key* measured something normal and abundant instead — because a hint that adds
information, names a shortcut, or works in more than one step is the ordinary case, and each proxy
caught the ordinary case rather than the fault. **The question is a READING of two texts against
each other and this store cannot decide it.**

**So her ruling stands unserved, and that is the honest report.** Zero rows survive scrutiny — which
is not *no mis-joins exist*, it is *this instrument cannot see them* (R60), and on a screen written
to find a mechanism the difference is the whole answer.

## R827 — The glyph scan clears the import: nothing is stripped, and the absence is authorial

Her ruling put this ahead of the sitting — **eight rows losing one character is a mechanism** — and
if the import stripped, the degree sign would not be the only casualty. **It does not strip.**

Scanned across all landed rows, source against row, for `° £ × ÷ −`, fractions and superscripts:
**ROWS LOSING ANY GLYPH: ZERO.** Degree 77 in source, 77 on the rows. Superscripts 12 and 12. The
`£` count RISES, on exactly the rows the door normalised — a gain, reported apart from a loss.

**And the five temperature items carry NO degree glyph in the staged source.** They were authored
`4C`, `9C`, `3C`, `8C`, `5C`, `6C`, `10C`. The staged file holds **88 degree glyphs in total**, so
it uses the character freely elsewhere and simply does not use it here. **There is no mechanism.
The absence is authorial**, which is the opposite of what a stripping import would look like and is
why the scan had to run before the sitting rather than after it.

**A correction to my own check, which nearly told the opposite story.** A first pass reported ZERO
degree glyphs in the entire staged file — evidence for a very different conclusion. It used Python's
`json.dumps` with `ensure_ascii` defaulted TRUE, escaping `°` to `°`, so a substring count
found none. **R729's fault, inside the check written to test for character loss** — the one place
where an escaping bug and the thing being measured are indistinguishable.

**Her dispositions landed.** The degree repair applies at the door and requires a DIGIT before the
C, so *"Point C is on the line"* is untouched. The over-cap stems stand as a **door disposition**:
the gate still enforces the sixteen-word cap globally and this door sets those faults aside on her
ruling. **The discrepancy is named rather than hidden** — whether the gate itself should change is a
separate ruling and is not assumed here.

**Nine more landed; nine still refuse, and none of them for a reason she has ruled on.** Seven say
**"error"** in a walk script, one says **"wrong"**, one breaks the long-word rule. **Three of the
five temperature items are among them** — their degree faults were repaired and they are held by a
separate, correct refusal. Saying *the temperature items are held* would have been true and
misleading; they are held for saying "error" to a child.

**187 items DRAFT, 0 LIVE, 0 signed, and every landed row gates clean.**

## R828 — Nothing is stripped, and glyphs are missing: the canary separates a strip from a dropped field

Cowork's canary run over the landed rows. **47 of 56 rows differ, and not one glyph was altered.**
Both halves are true and they are not in tension: **every absent glyph lives in a FIELD THIS IMPORT
DOES NOT CARRY.** A strip alters a string; this drops a field — and the difference decides whether a
population needs re-importing or a door needs widening.

**U+2212, the one they flagged as invisible: 45 sent, 0 landed, none stripped.** Every minus sign in
the staged source sits in `options[].distractorWorking` (51) and `notes` (10), neither imported. The
loss they feared was a hyphen appearing where a minus had been; what happened is that the text
carrying it never crossed the door. Same for U+2192 (43), ÷ (22), × (23) — all in the same two
uncarried fields.

**The degree arithmetic reconciles exactly and that is what makes the account trustworthy**: 88 in
the source, 11 in fields not imported, **77 landed — the count on the rows, with no residue.** An
explanation that leaves nothing over is a different thing from one that merely sounds right.

**Their fingerprint could not be reproduced, and I did not keep guessing.** The spec — *"sha256 over
sorted (codepoint, count) pairs, first 16 hex"* — names the pairs and not the serialisation. Nine
candidate readings against a published row, none matching. **This store registered that exact fault
in August (R752): a digest crosses with the serialisation that produces it, or the receiving party
checks a different number.** So the comparison ran on the published GLYPH MAPS instead — better
evidence than the hash, because a map names which glyph and how many where a hash says only "moved".
**A tenth guess that happened to match would have been luck presented as verification.**

**And my own earlier glyph scan was wrong in a way this exposes.** It reported `×`, `÷` and U+2212 as
zero in source AND rows — a match, and reassuring. It built its source text from stem, explanation
and option values only: **the very fields that carry no such glyph.** It compared the imported half
of the source against the imported row and found agreement, which was true and meant nothing. **A
scan whose source projection matches its target projection cannot detect a dropped field** — it can
only ever confirm what it already carries.

**The em dash is hers.** They report 10 `hintCore` strings carrying U+2014; this side holds 3, all
present on the rows, all of the form *"Angles on a straight line add to 180° — subtract from 180."*
The difference is population and is not reconciled from here. A dash breaking a child-facing sentence
has a standing house remedy, but these are maths hints in a district that has never been screened,
and the ruling is hers.

## R829 — A scan whose source projection matches its target projection can only confirm what it carries

Mine, and the canary exposed it. My glyph scan reported `×`, `÷` and U+2212 as **zero in source and
zero in rows** — a match, and reassuring, and worthless. It built its source text from `stem`,
`explanation` and `options[].value`: **exactly the fields the import carries.** So it compared the
imported half of the source against the imported row, found agreement, and could not have found
anything else.

**The general form: a comparison is only as wide as the NARROWER of its two projections, and when
both projections are the same one, the comparison is a tautology wearing a check's clothes.** It
cannot see a dropped field, because a dropped field is absent from both sides of the sum.

**The tell was available and it is arithmetic**: my scan reported `× 0 in source` while the source
file plainly contains 23. **A scan that reports zero of something a `grep` finds is describing its
own reach**, and comparing my count against the raw bytes would have taken one command.

Cowork's canary caught it because **its projection was the whole shipped row and its comparison was
against a published map rather than against itself.** That is the structural difference and it is
the reason a second party's instrument found what a first party's could not — not diligence, but a
projection chosen independently of the thing being tested.

Sibling to R173: there, an instrument said the right thing for the wrong reason. Here it said a TRUE
thing about a population it had silently narrowed to the answer.

## R830 — Two dropped fields, and the reader test refuses both

The test as set: **widen the door only if a reader exists; do not widen it because the field is
there.**

**`options[].distractorWorking` — 588 of 784 options, never on a key.** The arithmetic trace of how
each wrong answer was produced. **It is the nearest thing this district has to an execution, and the
column already exists**: `ItemOption.misconceptionExecution`, which the schema calls *the first thing
a reviewer asks to see*. **A reader exists — and it is gated `isEnglish`.**
`admin/items/[id]/page.tsx` renders the review surface only when the district is ENGLISH, so for a
maths item it does not render at all. **NO READER FOR MATHS. DO NOT WIDEN.** Carrying 588 workings
into a column nothing reads for this district is exactly the field-because-it-is-there move.

**`notes` — 194 of 196 items.** Authoring and design provenance. Nearest column `Item.drafterNote`,
which appears in the disposition membership **and nowhere else**: no surface renders it, no check
consults it. **NO READER AT ALL. DO NOT WIDEN.**

**And the finding that outranks the door, again.** 187 maths items are about to be read, and **the
reviewer surface that renders an item as she has to judge it is English-only.** For a maths item the
admin page shows the id, the status, the type name, the author, and the returned-with-notes box —
**no option table, no key flag, no misconception, no execution note, no hint, no walk script.** That
surface exists because its own header says judging without those is not possible.

**This is R823 one layer up.** The district had 111 attested hints and nothing to carry them; it now
has 187 items and no surface that renders them for review. **The sitting is not gated by it** — she
reads the crossed artefact — but a signature taken in the admin UI would be taken against a page
showing almost nothing. Reported, not built: whether that surface widens is a decision about what a
reviewer needs, and the same test applies to it.

## R831 — A normaliser that half-converts makes a third form, wrong in a new way

`MC02-RP-02`'s source read *"5 apples for 1 pound 50"* — £1.50 with the decimal point lost in
AUTHORING. My door added the £ and preserved the loss, so the row read **"£1 50"**.

**That is worse than either input.** The source form is at least readable as an old convention
somebody could recognise; "£1 50" reads as a price with a missing point and belongs to no
convention at all. **A normaliser converts the part it knows and carries the part it does not,
and the result can be a form that never existed anywhere.**

Contained: one item, two occurrences, and all 187 rows scanned for `£N NN` to establish that. Her
disposition repaired both to £1.50 and £1.20 — and her finding names the family: *"MC02-RP-02 lost
two decimal points and MC05-GEOM-02 a degree sign; both found by READING, neither by a gate, and
both are the bare-unit family."*

## R832 — The surface renders the item, or the action refuses and says why

Her 181st, and the reasoning is why it was built today rather than queued: **a page that can record
a judgement it cannot inform is worse than a page with no control at all. A missing control is
visible and gets fixed; a working control over an unrendered item produces signatures
indistinguishable from real ones.** That is the manufacture of attested-but-unread rows at whatever
rate somebody clicks, and **it cannot be retrofitted** — once such signatures exist nobody can
separate them from the others by inspection.

Built as `reviewSurfaceRenders(district)` in core, with four tests. **`markReviewedAction` and
`signItemAction` now refuse for any district the surface does not render**, and the page states the
reason in full rather than saying "blocked".

**Refused in the ACTION, not by hiding the button.** A hidden control can be re-enabled by anyone
editing a template; a refusing action cannot be clicked past. And the refusal names where verdicts
DO land — in returns against row hashes — so it closes a door and points at the open one.

**Her third-time pattern is the part worth carrying**: the signature field that did not exist, the
two fields that never crossed the door, and now a surface built to English's shape that silently
mis-serves maths. *"What a system cannot hold is not visible in what it holds."*

## R834 — Her finding described my artefact: the key emitted raw beside normalised options

Her 182nd records *"MC04-GEOM-05 — superscript lost in the key while present in the options; the
lost-character family's fourth member."* **It is not a member of that family and there is nothing on
the row to repair.**

The staged source carries `cm2` on **all four** options. The row carries `cm²` on all four,
normalised at the door. **The inconsistency existed only in the artefact I emitted**: line 73
normalised `options[].value`, line 74 emitted the separate `key` field from the RAW value. So the
population she read showed `cm²` options against a `cm2` key — a discrepancy that exists in neither
store.

**A projection that normalises one copy of a value and not another manufactures a discrepancy
between them**, and it will always look like a data fault, because the two fields disagree exactly
where a real loss would show. **Same value, two paths out, one of them treated.** Fixed at the
emitter; nothing was written to the row.

Third time a machine artefact has worn a data finding in this thread — R94's conflation, R813's
withdrawn membership, and now this. **The pattern is not carelessness about data, it is that a
report is itself a piece of software and nothing screens it.**

## R835 — Sittings two to twenty-five, and the generator finding that outranks them

**181 of 188 rows recorded CONTENT-VERIFIED**, fenced against `1d7f9cf4…`, row hash pinned per row,

cannot wander into the exceptions**, which is a better protection than a list of things to avoid.

## R836 — A refusal that reaches only the copy has not happened: twenty withdrawn rows come out

Cowork withdrew its 196-row send; 25 of its ids are absent from the replacement. **20 of those 25
were landed here**, including both rows the withdrawal was FOR — `MC04-FDP-04` and `MC05-FDP-01`,
which shipped with one of two colliding stems chosen silently. **The authoring store superseded its
own copy and retained the bytes, and nothing crossed that removed them from this store.**

**The five not landed are exactly the five the import had already refused** on house rules. So the
only reason this store did not hold all 25 is a gate that was screening for something else.

**Six of the twenty are sitting-one rows.** Her proving run verified eight; six of them came from
the withdrawn send. **Her verification is not voided** — she read the CONTENT, and keys computed and
distractors executing their tags remain true of those texts. What is withdrawn is the SEND, not her
judgement of it, and if the replacement carries the same ids the verification is re-pinnable against
the new rows rather than re-done.

**Removed with the bytes retained first.** Every row is in the artefact with its own content digest,
captured BEFORE deletion, and an attribution event per row was written before the delete — it
survives because `recordId` is a string, not a foreign key. **A withdrawal removes rows from the
store; it must not remove the record of what was in it.** 187 → 167, no orphaned options, and all
187 content-verified events intact.

**And the R767 guard earned itself on this run.** I named the retained digest `rowSha256`, which the
guard reserves for a digest over the WHOLE row object; mine was over the content subtree only. It
refused the artefact rather than staging a field whose name promised one thing and held another.
**Two different things must not share a field name**, and the guard found the collision on the first
attempt.

## R837 — A report is itself software, and nothing screens it

The general form, on its third instance in this thread.

**R94** — a machine verdict wearing a person's name: `check:word-puzzles` had marked eight items and
the ruling said Annie had. **R813** — a membership of nineteen orphan mis-joins, every member an
artefact of my own regexes, withdrawn before it reached a sitting. **R834** — a finding recorded
about `MC04-GEOM-05` losing a superscript, where the source holds `cm2` on all four options and the
row holds `cm²` on all four: **the discrepancy existed only in my emitter**, which normalised
`options[].value` and emitted the separate `key` field raw.

**Every gate in this project screens CONTENT. Nothing screens the artefact that reports on it.** A
scanner reads child-facing strings, `check:register` reads rule numbers, `check:authority-shape`
reads the store — and an emitted report passes through none of them. Its digests are checked, its
population is declared, its instrument is fixtured, **and its PROJECTIONS are not checked against
each other at all.**

**The recurring mechanism is a value emitted twice by two paths, one of them treated.** R834 is that
exactly; R813 is its cousin, a predicate applied to a projection that could not carry the answer.
**A report that derives the same value twice must derive it once**, and where it cannot, the two
paths are the first thing to compare — because a reader has no way to tell a manufactured
discrepancy from a real one, and it will always appear exactly where a real fault would.

## R838 — An artefact normalises everything it prints, or nothing

Her rule, with the mechanism mine. **A report that derives one value twice derives it once.**

`MC04-GEOM-05` is the instance: the emitter normalised `options[].value` and printed the separate
`key` field raw, so the artefact showed `cm²` options against a `cm2` key — **a discrepancy present
in neither store.** The source holds `cm2` on all four options; the row holds `cm²` on all four.
Both are internally consistent. Only the report was not.

**All-or-nothing is the rule because a MIXED projection is worse than an untreated one.** An
artefact that normalises nothing is merely raw, and a reader knows to normalise before comparing. An
artefact that normalises some of what it prints is **actively misleading**, and it misleads exactly
where a real fault would show — two copies of one value disagreeing.

**And the deeper form: the second derivation is the fault, not the normalisation.** The key was
already in `options[]`; printing it again created a value that could drift from itself. **Derive
once and reference it**, and the question of whether both copies were treated cannot arise.

**Third instance, and the gap is structural** (R837). Every gate in this project screens content;
nothing screens the reporting layer. Digests are checked, populations declared, instruments
fixtured — **and no check compares an artefact's projections against each other**, which is the one
thing that would have caught all three.

## R839 — Nothing watched for a withdrawn send, and five escaped by luck

Twenty rows from a withdrawn 196-row send were landed and publication-eligible. **Five more were
absent for no good reason at all** — a house-rule gate refused them for saying *"error"* to a child,
and that gate was screening for banned vocabulary, not for provenance. **The five did not escape;
they were caught by something aimed elsewhere.**

**`pnpm check:withdrawn-sends` is the watch, and it is one subtraction**: every landed row whose id
is absent from the CURRENT send. A row here that the sending store no longer sends is withdrawn,
renamed, or from a send nobody remembers — **and a row the sending store no longer sends must not
publish on the strength of having once arrived.** Currently 167 landed, 171 in the send, zero
orphans: the removal was complete.

**And it reports an ambiguity it cannot resolve.** `MATHSIMPORTOUTBOUND` resolves to **three files
with three different digests**. The check takes the newest by mtime and says so — **mtime is not
provenance** (R774). Measured: the first differs from the other two on all 171 items, by an
`approvedBy` → `reviewedBy` rename; **the second and third differ on six items, and those six are
the money-units class landing at source** — CALC-04 in all five batches plus `MC01-FDP-03`. The
template repair Annie identified is arriving, under a filename that cannot say which version it is.

**A send identified by NAME is a lookup with more than one answer.** R799 said it of returns; it is
truer of a send, because a send is what a store imports from.

## R840 — Re-imported and re-pinned, with the comparison calibrated before it was trusted

The amended source (`4bab53bb…`) reached the desk and was not forwarded — **the desk's fault, not a
non-arrival.** It is on this disk under **two names, byte-identical** (`amended-maths-source-for-code`
and `AMENDEDMATHSSOURCECROSSING`): the naming class again, in the turn it was ruled.

**Fourteen of the twenty withdrawn rows re-imported. Six did not, for two different reasons, and the
difference matters:**

- **Two are HELD because both variants cross** — `MC01-CALC-04` and `MC01-FDP-06`. The units
  amendment reached both variants and does not resolve the collision. **Picking is the fault that
  caused the withdrawal, and this store does not pick.**
- **Four are simply not in this source** — `MC04-FDP-04`, `MC04-FDP-06`, `MC04-GEOM-04`,
  `MC05-FDP-01`. It carries the exemplar, three briefs and nine amended items; these are in none of
  them. **That includes both rows the withdrawal was for.** They stay out.

**Her six re-pinned: five RE-PINNED, none back to her, one unreachable.** `MC01-CALC-04` is among the
held, so its verification cannot be re-pinned and waits on the collision. The other five carry bytes
**identical** to what she verified — not a re-reading, the same text under a new row.

**And the comparison was calibrated before it was trusted.** A "bytes differ" verdict is only about
the text if the hash function here is the one that pinned the hashes there. Every retained row was
re-hashed against its own pinned value first — **compared against a known answer rather than against
itself** (R829). All reproduce. Had they not, every verdict would have been about my function and
none of it reportable; **this is the step that makes a mismatch mean something.**

181 rows, 0 gate faults, all DRAFT, none signed.

## R841 — The watcher fired on rows it should not have, because it knew one send

`check:withdrawn-sends` flagged the fourteen legitimate re-imports as orphans. **It was correct
about what it knew and wrong about the world**: it watched `MATHSIMPORTOUTBOUND` alone, and the rows
came from a second send it had never heard of.

**A row is orphaned when it is in NO send — not when it is absent from the one the check happens to
name.** The reference is now every send file on the disk, and the check reports each family's file
count, digest count and id count separately.

**Widening the reference is not resolving the ambiguity, and the ruling holds.** The check still
refuses to say which send is current and **still does not use mtime to pick** — it reports that
`MATHSIMPORTOUTBOUND` resolves to three different documents under one name and stops there. Name a
send by its content, not its family.

**The general shape: a watcher scoped to one source will read every other source as a fault.** It is
the same error as R829's matched projections one level out — there, a comparison too narrow to see a
dropped field; here, a comparison too narrow to see a legitimate arrival. **Both report confidently,
and both are describing their own reach.**

## R842 — Absent from the district, not pending

`MC04-FDP-04` and `MC05-FDP-01` — the two rows the withdrawal existed for — are recorded **ABSENT
FROM THE DISTRICT**. They are in no send and no source: the 196-row send was withdrawn FOR them, the
171-row replacement omits them, and the amended source carries neither.

**Pending is an expectation; absent is a settled state.** Recorded as pending they would sit in a
queue with two permanent members, and every future reader of that queue would wait on nobody.
**That is how a closed question becomes an open one that never closes** — the queue survives the
reason for it, and the cost is paid by whoever reads it next and cannot tell a live item from a
fossil.

The trail is an `AttributionEvent` per id, actor *the desk*, attached to the ID rather than to a row
because there is no row — `recordId` is a string and not a foreign key, the same property that let
the withdrawal record survive the delete (R836).

**And absent is not a refusal.** If a later send names either id it arrives as a NEW row and this
event is its prior state rather than a contradiction. What is recorded is that on this date nothing
was owed — which is a fact about the sends, not a judgement about the items, and neither store is
asked to do anything with it.

**The district closes at 181 rows, zero gate faults, all DRAFT, none signed, no orphans, publication
holding.**

## R843 — The absence was false, and checking before the next one found two more that are not absent

`absent-from-district-5b7eb355…` is **WITHDRAWN**. `MC04-FDP-04` and `MC05-FDP-01` are in the
population Annie read and verified in her 182nd, with row hashes she can cite — `58e69863…` and
`da44c026…` — and both carry APPROVED content-verified events in this store. **They were HELD BACK
by Cowork's substance guard, not lost**: the withdrawn send carried them with one stem silently
chosen, the corrected send carried them not at all, **and neither state was ever published as a
hold.**

**The error is the desk's, and this store recorded what it was told.** Stated rather than absorbed —
a store that silently owns an upstream error makes the next one harder to see. The bytes stand in
retention; nothing is deleted.

**Both restored, and the selection is HERS.** Each id carries **two different questions**. The
variant restored is the one whose stem matches the row she verified, identified by her own row hash;
**this store did not pick**, because picking silently is the fault the withdrawal existed for. The
unchosen variant is recorded on the row under `explanation._stemCollision` and is not discarded.

**And the instruction to check before calling anything absent again earned itself immediately.**
`MC01-FDP-04` and `MC05-FDP-08` are **NOT absent.** Both are in the amended source and in Cowork's
29, which names them itself: they are **stem collisions** — 6 of the 29, where two different
questions share one itemId. Not in the store, not in the staged 196, not in the current send, but
present in two sources and held rather than missing. **Recording them absent would have repeated the
fault this same turn withdrew.**

What they actually need is what the other two needed: **a reviewer to say WHICH QUESTION.** Cowork
holds both variants of each and has chosen nothing, which is correct. Annie has not read either id.

**The lesson is about the direction of the error.** Twice now a row has been called absent when it
was held, and both times the hold existed and had never been published. **An unpublished hold is
indistinguishable from an absence from every side except the one holding it** — and the party
holding it is the only one who cannot see that nobody else knows.

## R844 — Her six ruled, and the counts asserted from the artefact caught my own prose twice

Four landed, two stand unchanged. `MC01-FDP-04` the two-step jug, `MC02-NPV-07` the largest-decimal
comparison, `MC05-FDP-08` the £64 coat, `MC05-MEAS-02` the flour conversion; `MC04-FDP-04` and
`MC05-FDP-01` keep their landed variants, verified on the row rather than assumed. **Her reasoning
per row is on the artefact, in her words**, and the variant was matched by the KEY she named rather
than by position.

**The instruction to assert counts from the artefact rather than from prose earned itself twice on
one id.** My prose had described the class as *"two different questions share one itemId"* —
`MC01-FDP-04` carries **three**. And reading two of its three side by side they appeared identical:
same stem, same key, same hint. **They are not** — they differ in their option sets, so the
artefact's three is three DISTINCT items. **Asserting from the page would have been wrong twice; the
artefact was right once.**

**The unchosen are retired, not discarded** — every one recorded on the row with its stem, key, hint
and holding files. **And the orphan closes itself**: `MC05-MEAS-02`'s double hint, which started the
whole mechanism hunt, was never a joining fault. Two whole items under one id, each with its own
hint. **An identity collision wearing a join fault's clothes**, and the class closes with its cause
named.

Her prose-pounds flag is carried and NOT amended, as she ruled.

## R845 — The notation gate was screening retention, and demanded an amendment to a record of a decision not to amend

Found by landing her 184th. The notation loop in `checkItemChildFacing` walked **every string** with
no disposition filter, so it screened retention paths — `_previousText`, `_walkScriptBefore`,
`_stemCollisionResolved`.

**The instance is almost too neat.** The shelved variant of `MC05-FDP-08` spells *"50 pounds"*; the
gate demanded *"£50"* — **on text Annie had just RETIRED, whose prose-money convention she had
explicitly flagged as an open question and expressly not amended.** The gate was asking for an
amendment to a record of a decision not to amend.

**A retention field records text as it previously was, or as it was retired. A child never meets it,
and demanding house form of it destroys the only thing it is for.** Retention paths are now skipped
by the notation rule, with a test asserting both directions — the same text faults under a
child-facing key and passes under a retention one.

**And it was invisible until now because retention had never carried prose.** `_previousText` and
`_walkScriptBefore` held strings that already passed the gate when they were current. **The first
retention field to hold text that was retired BECAUSE it was unresolved was the first to expose
this** — a gate fault that needed a specific kind of history before it could show at all.

## R846 — Eighteen pre-existing faults on LIVE English rows, and sixteen are the same class as R845

Measured while baselining the R845 change, and reported rather than fixed — **nothing here was
caused by that change**: English 18 faults before and 18 after, maths 8 → 7, exactly the one the
change was for. **Surgical, and measured in a worktree at the previous commit rather than argued
from the diff** (R62's technique, R149's rule).

**Sixteen of the eighteen sit on `stem.quotes[].why` — a path `isScreenedPath` says is NOT
child-facing.** That is R845's fault in a second rule: the sentence-length check, like the notation
check, walks strings without consulting the disposition membership. **One instance is a bug; two in
the same file is the gate's shape** — the dispositions exist and only some rules ask.

**The other two are `us-spelling` on `ENG-003-A-SP-07`, flagging *"practise"*** in a walk script and
an option value — **on a SpaG item whose subject IS the practice/practise distinction.** A rule
firing on the word an item exists to teach is the R783 shape one level over: the check is right
about the string and wrong about the item.

**Reported, not repaired.** Sixteen want a disposition filter this store can add; two want a
reviewer to say whether a rule may fire on the word an item is about, and that is not this store's
to decide.

## R847 — Every rule asks the dispositions now, because the filter is at the walk

The dispositions existed and the rules **opted in**. Two faults came of that and they were one shape:
the notation rule screened retention and demanded house form of retired text (R845); the
sentence-length rule screened `stem.quotes[].why`, a STAFF path, producing sixteen faults on LIVE
English rows about a field no child meets (R846). **One rule asking is a bug; two in one file is the
design.**

The question is now asked **once, at the walk**, and every rule inherits the answer — all four walk
sites in `checkItemChildFacing`, both walkers.

**STAFF and RETENTION are excluded. UNDECLARED IS NOT, and that is the load-bearing choice.**
Filtering on `isScreenedPath` — disposition *is* `child` — was the tidier line and would have
**silently dropped every field nobody has classified yet**, which is precisely the allowlist failure
R57 removed. An undeclared path must surface as a question, not vanish through a filter.

**Measured in a worktree at the previous commit rather than argued from the diff:**

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| ENGLISH LIVE | 18 | **2** |
| ENGLISH, all 380 rows | 159 | **143** |
| MATHS | 7 | 7 |
| VR/NVR LIVE | 0 | 0 |

**Exactly the sixteen, and nothing else.** The two remaining English LIVE faults are the
`practise`/`practice` pair on `ENG-003-A-SP-07` — a rule firing on the word the item exists to teach,
which is a reviewer's question and not a filter's.

## R848 — Twenty-three identical outcomes are a curated pass and its ancestors, not a preference

Her finding, and it **retires the class rather than closing it.** Where a set of variants resolves
the same way twenty-three times, the uniformity is not evidence of a rule about quality — **it is
the fingerprint of one curated pass and the files descended from it.** The variants are not
competing judgements; they are a lineage, and the "winner" is simply the copy the curation touched.

**A preference would vary.** Twenty-three identical outcomes say the population was never twenty-three
decisions — it was one decision, copied. So the class does not need twenty-three readings, and
reading them would produce twenty-three confirmations of a single ancestral act while looking like
corroboration.

Sibling to R804's mirror-population lesson: **when a count comes out too clean, the question is what
produced the uniformity, not what the uniformity proves.**

## R849 — SPECIMEN: a declared role, because house rules bind use and never mention

Her ruling, and it is **the third instance of one shape**. Quotation: a source's words are not ours
to reword. Retention: retired text is a record, not an offer. **Specimen: an exhibited form is a
lesson, not a usage.**

`ENG-003-A-SP-07` teaches the practice/practise distinction, so it must PRINT *practise* — and the
US-spelling rule flagged it for doing the only thing it exists to do. **A character-level rule will
always eventually meet a lesson about its own characters**, and a district that teaches orthography
produces this on every item it authors. **So it is a declarable role the gates read, not an
exception list somebody maintains.**

`stem.specimens` is declared once at item level and honoured wherever the character-level rules run
— the stem walk, the explanation walk, and the option values, **filtered per string by
`spansPresentIn` exactly as quotations are.** The declaration itself is a token field, because
screening the specimen list would flag the very forms it exempts.

**The exemption is the SPAN, never the string**, and there is a test for each direction: an
undeclared *practise* still faults, a declared one does not, and *"Organize your practise notes"*
still faults on `Organize` with `practise` declared. **The prose around a specimen stays fully
bound** — the boundary quotation already draws.

**ENGLISH LIVE: 0 faults**, from 18 before R847 and 2 after it. Across all 380 English rows,
143 → 141.

**And a note on what was already there.** `testedTokens` silently exempted us-spelling while
documenting itself as *"exempt from the VOCABULARY CEILING only"*. It would have hidden this fault
with a wrong declaration — the right form was to name what the string IS, not to borrow a field that
happened to work.

## R850 — Provenance-only fields separate a blinded pairing by field count alone

Cowork's check separates **23 of 23 without reading a stem** — `map97Status`, `flagNote`, `topicId`,
`processId`, `gapFamily`. A blinded pairing that carries them is not blinded: the reader never needs
the content, because **the shape of the record identifies which side produced it.**

**This is the R780 disclosure in reverse.** There, evidence had to stay and the leak was disclosed
because removing it would have withheld the thing the reading needed. Here the leaking fields carry
**nothing the reading uses** — provenance, workflow state, internal identifiers — so they come out
and nothing is lost. **The test is not "does this leak?" but "does the reading need it?"**, and the
two questions have opposite answers on these five.

**Strip them at the blinding, not at the reading.** A field removed downstream leaves the upstream
artefact still able to leak on its next use; the R776 lesson is that the side which built the
artefact is the side least likely to notice what it reveals.

## R851 — The backwards test: distinguishable is not side-identifying

Run on both batches, by counting populated fields and comparing field shapes, never reading a stem.

**The English eight: 0 of 8 separable.** Identical populated-field shapes on both sides of every
pairing. The blind holds and the certificate on that sitting is unchanged.

**The nine replacement pairs: 5 of 9 distinguishable by field shape.** And the distinction is one
field — `stem.quotes`, present on one reading and absent on the other.

**But separable is not side-identifying, and that is the finding.** Measured against the unblinding
map, the reading carrying `stem.quotes` is this store's copy on **3 of the 5** and the other file's
on **2**. A reader betting *"the one with quotes is store X"* is right three times in five — **no
better than chance, and worse than useless, because it feels like a signal.**

**So a reader could tell the two readings APART on those five, and could not tell WHICH SIDE either
was.** Blinding protects provenance, not distinguishability: two different questions SHOULD be
distinguishable, or there would be nothing to rule on. **The certificate stands on both sittings**,
and her verdicts were never in question either way — a verdict made on the texts is unaffected by
whether the blind held.

**The line against the 23.** `map97Status`, `flagNote`, `topicId`, `processId`, `gapFamily` record
WHICH PROCESS PRODUCED THE ROW; `stem.quotes` records whether a question cites its passage. **The
first is provenance wearing a content field's clothes. The second is content, and content is what
the reading is for.** A blinding strip that removed both would be removing the evidence — R780's
fault — so the test is the one already ruled: not *does this differ*, but *does the reading need
it*.

**And the English eight held for a structural reason worth keeping**: that batch was built by
projecting a FIXED SET OF KEYS onto every reading, so a field absent on one side is absent on both.
**A projection with a fixed shape cannot leak a shape.** The nine were assembled from whole authored
items and inherited whatever each carried.

## R852 — A field that produces the right behaviour for the wrong reason makes the record untrue about why

`testedTokens` already suppressed the us-spelling flag on `ENG-003-A-SP-07` — it would have "worked".
Its own documentation says *"exempt from the VOCABULARY CEILING only"*, and using it would have left
the row asserting that *practise* is a word the item TESTS FOR DIFFICULTY, which is not what it is.

**The behaviour would have been right and the record would have been false**, and the record is what
the next reader has. A field borrowed for a useful side effect quietly redefines itself: the next
person to read `testedTokens` finds entries that are not tested tokens, and either widens the
definition to fit or removes an entry that was load-bearing.

**Name what the string IS.** `specimens` says the item exhibits this form; `testedTokens` says the
item tests this word; `quotedSpans` says a source wrote it. Three roles, three declarations, and each
one true. **The cost of the right field is one declaration; the cost of the borrowed one is paid by
whoever next tries to trust the field's name.**

Sibling to R601 and R605 — a decision honoured by accident and one honoured by design produce
identical output and are distinguishable in one grep. **This is the same shape in the declaration
layer: an exemption granted by the wrong field and one granted by the right field behave identically
and record different facts.**

## R853 — A blind cannot hide the property the judgement is about: curated-pass pairs are PERMANENTLY unblindable

Her ruling, and it closes the thread. **Where FINISH is the question, finish is also the signature.**

A curated-pass pair asks: which of these two is the finished one? The evidence for that judgement —
polish, consistency, the declarations a careful pass adds — **is the same evidence that identifies
which side the curated pass produced.** There is no projection that carries one and withholds the
other, because they are not two properties. They are one property being asked about from two
directions.

**So this is registered as PERMANENT, not unblinded-for-now.** The distinction matters and it is the
whole point of the entry. *Unblinded-for-now* is a defect with a fix, and it invites somebody to
attempt the fix — to strip one more field, project one more shape, and produce a blind that appears
to hold while quietly removing what the reader needed. **A permanent finding closes that road.** For
this class the honest artefact is an OPEN pairing that says so, and the certificate records that no
blind was possible rather than that none was attempted.

**And it retires the twenty-three by the same argument** (R848). Twenty-three identical outcomes are
a curated pass and its ancestors; the uniformity is the lineage. **A blinded reading of them would
have been twenty-three readings of one act, unblindable in principle and uninformative in fact.**

## R854 — Distinguishable is not side-identifying, and a signal that feels like one is worse than none

The standing test for every future blind check, in two parts.

**One: measure whether a difference IDENTIFIES A SIDE, not whether one exists.** Five of nine
pairings were distinguishable by field shape and **none of them was side-identifying** — the
distinguishing field landed on this store's copy three times and the other's twice. **Three of five
is chance.** A check that stops at *"the sides differ structurally"* reports a leak that is not one,
and would have voided two certificates that hold.

**Two: a signal that feels like one is worse than none.** A reader who notices `stem.quotes` and
believes it marks a side is worse off than a reader who notices nothing — they now have a confident
method that is wrong two times in five, and confidence is what stops the second look. **The danger
is not the information; it is the false sense of having some.**

**Both certificates stand**: the English eight blinded and held, the nine were distinguishable and
still carried no provenance. And the corollary that makes the rule usable — **two different
questions SHOULD be distinguishable, or there is nothing to rule on.** A blind that made the
readings identical would have destroyed the reading.

## R855 — A projection with a fixed shape cannot leak a shape

The mechanism, and the way to build a blind where one is possible at all.

The English eight held for a structural reason rather than a careful one: that batch was built by
**projecting a fixed set of keys onto every reading**, so a field absent on one side is absent on
both. The nine were assembled from **whole authored items** and inherited whatever each happened to
carry — which is exactly how `stem.quotes` came to differ, and how the 23 came to carry
`map97Status`, `flagNote`, `topicId`, `processId` and `gapFamily`.

**The rule: build a blinded artefact by PROJECTION, never by inclusion.** Name the fields the
reading needs and emit exactly those on every row, populated or empty. **Then the shape is a
property of the projection and not of the source**, and the only thing that can differ between two
readings is what they say — which is what the reader is there for.

Inclusion-based blinding fails in a specific and predictable way: it leaks precisely the fields that
one process writes and another does not, **which is the definition of provenance.** A blind built by
copying rows and removing what looks revealing is a blind maintained by vigilance, and vigilance is
not a mechanism.

## R856 — The review surface renders the maths item, so the refusal has its other half

Her ruling: **the surface renders the item or refuses the action.** The refusal was built and
correct; until now the admin page showed a maths item's id, status, type name and author, and
**a signature taken against that page would have recorded that somebody did not look.**

`MathsReview` renders what a maths verdict actually needs: the stem; every option with its value,
key flag, misconception, execution note and **the hint a child would be told**; the item hint; the
walk script; and, where an id carried more than one question, the collision resolution with its
retired variants. It reads and never writes — the verdict is still taken by the existing actions.

An untagged distractor renders as **NOT TAGGED — this blocks the verdict**, because that is exactly
what `publishBlockers` will say, and the reviewer should meet the blocker on the page rather than
at the button.

## R857 — Everything the district needs, in one run, with publication held

**Signatures: 162 landed, 25 refused.** `reviewedBy`, `reviewMethod`, `reviewRecordedBy` and
`reviewRecordNote` are written in one transaction with a SIGNED attribution event carrying the row
hash — **authority recorded, not implied**: the reviewer id, the returns it comes from, and the hash
it was taken against.

**The refusals are two populations and they are not the same fact.** Fourteen refuse on
`missing-misconceptions` — a distractor with no tag, which no signature can cure. **Twelve refuse
because their bytes have moved since she verified them, and EVERY ONE MOVED BY ONE OF HER OWN
AMENDMENTS** — the 180th's money keys, the 182nd's measures extension, the routine dash and degree
repairs. Not one move is unexplained.

**The refusal stands anyway, and that is her ruling working rather than misfiring.** A signature
taken against a stale hash records that somebody did not check. **The remedy is a RE-PIN, not a
re-read** (R840), and the re-pin is not this store's to make.

**The nine assert 6 of 6 byte-identical** against the amended source through the same door; the
other three are the unresolved pairs, which have no single form to regenerate. **The two held rows
carry their ruled variants with the unchosen shelved.**

**The face fails closed and nothing was drafted.** `case-maths-01` has an empty title, so
`caseFaceServes` is false and **no item reaches any child regardless of status.** The wording is
Cowork's to draft and Annie's to approve, as case-en-06's was — **and a placeholder would have made
the face SERVE, which is the one thing failing closed prevents.**

**The visible-but-empty window is ZERO, and structurally so.** The face is invisible until a wording
lands, and by then the items are whatever they are. **There is no ordering of the two acts that
opens a window** — it would take landing a face wording before the items are LIVE, which is the
sequence the fail-closed rule exists to make impossible by default rather than by discipline.

**187 rows: 162 REVIEWED, 25 DRAFT, 0 LIVE. Publication holds.**

## R858 — A content hash must not carry retention, or recording provenance falsifies the signature

The first run of the signing reported six rows as *bytes moved* and all nine amendments as *drift*.
**Every one was mine.** The rows carry `_stemCollisionResolved` and `_previousValue`, written BY the
landings; the pinned hashes were computed before those keys existed.

**A record of what changed is not part of what a reviewer read.** So it cannot be part of the hash
that asks whether her text moved — otherwise **every act of recording provenance falsifies the
signature it is recording**, and the more carefully a store keeps its history the less of it can be
signed.

Stripping `_`-prefixed keys at every level: the nine went 0 of 6 to **6 of 6**, and the false
movers resolved to twelve genuine ones with named causes.

**This is R845 one layer over.** There the notation gate screened retention and demanded house form
of retired text. Here the content hash counted retention and reported a signature as stale because
the store had written down why it changed. **Same distinction, two mechanisms, and both found only
when a retention field finally carried something.**

## R859 — A digest is comparable only under the projection that produced it; a projection change re-pins everything

**The twelve never moved, and the finding is mine.**

R858 was right that a content hash must not carry retention. But I applied the corrected projection
to pins **already taken under the old one**, and reported the arithmetic consequence as *twelve rows
whose bytes have moved since she verified them* — the most serious thing this store can say about a
signature.

Checked properly: **all twelve reproduce EXACTLY under the projection their pin was taken with.**
Their pins came from her 182nd, **after** the amendments blamed for moving them. The content never
changed. **My hash did.**

**So a hash-convention change is not a measurement. It is a re-pinning of every pin in the store**,
and it silently reinterprets each one as either intact or moved depending on a decision taken later
and elsewhere. That is a worse fault than the one R858 fixed, because the R858 fault made signatures
impossible to take while this one makes them look **wrongly taken**.

**Two mechanisms follow, and the second is the one that generalises.** A pin is verified under ITS
OWN projection, not the reader's current one — so eleven of the twelve signed, and the twelfth,
`MC01-FDP-03`, refuses on `missing-misconceptions`, which is a real blocker and nothing to do with
hashing. **And every pin written from here names its projection**, because a bare digest is a claim
whose meaning lives outside itself: identical bytes hash differently under two conventions, and
nothing in the number says which one was used.

Sibling to R752 and R759 — there a digest crossed without its serialisation, and the far side
computed a different number. **Here a digest crossed without its PROJECTION, and the same side
computed a different number about its own rows.**

## R860 — What remains, and the face is why it does not matter yet

**173 of 187 signed. 14 refused, all on `missing-misconceptions`** — an incorrect option carrying no
tag. **They stay refused: they are Cowork's authoring, and three are the ones it could not resolve.**
No signature cures an untagged distractor, because the tag is what says which error the option
executes and there is nothing for a hint to attach to without it.

**Blast radius: ZERO, unchanged, and it will stay zero while the face is empty.** `case-maths-01`
carries no title, `caseFaceServes` is false, and the case is invisible however many items are
signed. **Signing changes what MAY serve; the face decides whether anything DOES** — and the two are
independent by design, which is the whole reason the visible-but-empty window cannot open.

## R861 — The face crossed as bytes, and the bytes say something the paraphrase could not

The face slot has been described to her and never crossed as a string. Crossed now, verbatim, with
its own digest.

**And the bytes carry a fact the description could not.** `title` is the **empty string**;
`narrativeIntro` holds a **state marker**, not prose — a record that the slot is empty and how a
face may land. **Nothing in this case has ever been written for a child to read.**

**A paraphrase of an empty slot and a paraphrase of a wording are indistinguishable to a reader who
has seen neither.** "The face is empty" and "the face holds a placeholder" and "the face holds a
draft nobody approved" all reduce to the same sentence at second hand, and only the bytes separate
them. That is the whole case for crossing a string rather than an account of it (R25), and it is
sharpest where the string is absent.

**It is the last child-facing item in the district.** Every stem, option, hint and walk script has
crossed and been read; this has not. **Nothing was drafted** — the slot crossed, not a proposal,
because a placeholder would make the face SERVE, which is the one thing failing closed prevents.

## R862 — Publish the ids, do not adopt the number

Two stores counting the untagged: **fourteen here over 187 landed rows, eleven there over the sent
171.** The instruction offered adoption or publication, and **publication is the only one that
settles anything.**

**Scoped to the same 171, this store counts EIGHT — not eleven.** So the gap was never only scope:
the two stores disagree about which rows carry an untagged distractor **even over one population**.
Six of the fourteen sit outside the send entirely, all MC01 rows that arrived by the exemplar rather
than by the send.

**Adopting the 11 would have made the two counts agree and left three rows in dispute that nobody
could name.** A number adopted is a disagreement closed by deference; ids published are a
disagreement reduced to a subtraction anyone can run. **The reconciliation is now mechanical, and it
was not available at any point while both sides were exchanging totals.**

Every id crosses with whether it is in the sent 171 and which of its option values carry no tag —
because *"fourteen untagged"* names no row, and R569 already ruled that a match carries what it
matched on.

## R863 — The correction that had to reach her, and why speed mattered

The desk routed this store's twelve to Annie as **movement caused by her own amendments**. **It was
false, and the record says so: the rows never moved.**

All twelve reproduce exactly under the projection their pins were taken with, and those pins came
from her 182nd — **after** the amendments blamed for moving them. What moved was this store's hash,
when R858 stopped counting retention and the corrected projection was applied to pins already taken
under the old one (R859).

**A reviewer told that text she verified has changed cannot un-know it.** She would read the next
artefact looking for drift she had been told to expect, and **every ordinary difference would look
like evidence** — a false alarm about signatures does not merely waste a reading, it recalibrates
one. That is why it crosses now rather than as a footnote to the next batch, and why the artefact
states it in the plainest available words rather than as a revision of an earlier figure.

## R864 — A flagNote is the third state: it specifies an entry and does not substitute for one

Her ruling: **the tag says WHICH ERROR the option executes; prose describing it does not clear the
gate.**

Measured, and the blocked rows are not careless. Every untagged option carries
`misconceptionBehaviour` — *"rounds both numbers to the tens and does not compensate"*, *"gives the
range instead of the mean"* — with `misconceptionRef: null` and **`mappingStatus: "gap"`**. **The
authoring store DECLARED these as gaps.** The prose is exactly the third state: it describes the
error and cannot be joined to a hint, because a hint attaches to an entry and there is no entry.

**So the prose is not nothing and it is not enough.** It is the specification a minted entry would
be written from, it travels on the authored option, and it is lost by nobody. **What it cannot do is
carry a signature**, and a gate that accepted it would be recording that a child will be told
something when nothing exists to tell her.

**Fourteen rows blocked here, seventeen options; the ruling names six to mint.** The difference is a
MAPPING judgement this store cannot make — whether an existing entry already covers a behaviour is a
reading against 111 library entries, which is authoring rather than arithmetic. **All fourteen ids
are published so the eight can be named rather than inferred**, and every blocked row keeps one or
two tagged distractors: **a blocked row is one option short, not unmapped.**

**Both shapes reported, neither taken.** 181 signed with six held — the district opens incomplete
with its gaps declared, and *a hold that is published is a hold* (R836, R842). 187 with the six
minted — the district opens whole, at the cost of **putting six new child-facing hints on the
critical path of a publication, which is the condition under which hint wording is least carefully
read.**

**And the face gates both identically.** It is empty and correctly so, so no item reaches a child
under either shape until a wording lands. **The choice is therefore not urgent in the way an open
district would make it** — which is the fail-closed rule paying for itself a second time.

## R865 — The join refuses rather than stretches, and the default is refusal

David's ruling, wired at the landing before the mints arrive: **if an option does not compute as its
entry's behaviour, the entry waits for its true carrier.**

**A join lands on POSITIVE VERIFICATION, never on the absence of contradiction.** Six refusal paths,
every one canaried against a synthetic mint file and every one firing:

| refused when | why |
|---|---|
| the entry names no carrier | **this store will not choose one** — choosing is the stretch the ruling forbids |
| the named row is absent | nothing to join to |
| the option value does not match byte for byte | a carrier is an identity, not a description |
| the carrier named is the KEY | an entry describes an error; a key executes none |
| the option already carries an entry | two entries on one option is two answers to one question |
| the declared computation disagrees | the ruling's own case |
| nothing can execute it and no human has ruled | **an unverifiable join is refused, not waved through** |

**And nothing infers.** R826 withdrew three signals that tried to decide *does this option execute
this error* by proxy, and every one measured something else. So a behaviour is executed **only where
the mint declares the arithmetic**, and where it does not, a human ruling must accompany it. The
gate does not attempt the judgement it already proved it cannot make.

**The gate is the deliverable and it is live before the content.** With no mint file present it
lands nothing and says so — **an absent input lands nothing rather than everything**, which is the
whole difference between a gate that defaults closed and one that defaults to whatever arrives.

## R866 — Four unsourced attributions in a week, and this one was not mine to accept

The desk records that my *eight* was its error and that I reported eleven. **My measurement was
eight and remains eight** — of the fourteen blocked rows, eight are in the sent 171, stable across
all three send files, published at `b3918841…` with every id and its send-membership.

**I have not adopted the correction, and that is the point of the entry.** The desk owns the
attribution error; this store owns its number. **A store that accepts a figure it did not produce,
because the correction is generously worded, has abandoned the only thing that makes its reports
worth reading.**

Sibling to R94 — *a machine verdict must not wear a person's name* — and its mirror: **a store's
measurement must not be replaced by one attributed to it.** Both are provenance faults; the first
lends authority a machine did not earn, the second removes authority a store did.

The remedy either way is the one this thread keeps arriving at: **the artefact is on the door with
its digest.** Neither party has to remember who said what.

## R867 — Her approved bytes and the house gate disagree, and this store picks neither

Her 191st approves both face strings **unamended, on their bytes** — the first child-facing face in
this project to pass a reading without a single change. **`landCaseFace` refuses them.**

The long-word cap fires on **two distinct long words where the maximum is one: `operations` and
`percentages`.** Both sit in the content list her return names explicitly — *place value, the four
operations, fractions and percentages, measures and money, shape, charts and proportion* — and which
she confirms is *true of the corpus as built*. **The gate is not refusing an oversight. It is
refusing the sentence she checked most closely.**

It fires under **doorplate, notice and narrative alike**, so this is not the role misfit that
refused the first landing attempt (R689). And a cosmetic note, because the report misleads: the gate
prints *"operations,"* and *"percentages,"* with trailing commas, as though punctuation were being
matched. It is not — and a third ten-letter word, *proportion*, is NOT counted, so the rule is not
simple length either.

**Four ways to make this land, and this store took none of them:** amend her approved text, lower
the cap, exempt the doorplate role, or write the face without the standing path. **Every one
resolves a reviewer-versus-rule conflict by quietly picking a side, and the picking is the fault
rather than the outcome.** A store that edits approved bytes to satisfy a gate has replaced the
reviewer; a store that bypasses the gate has replaced the rule.

**So the face stays empty — the state it was already in, and the state that fails closed.** Nothing
is worse than before, nothing is decided, and the conflict is reported with both sides quoted rather
than reconciled. `caseFaceServes` false, blast radius zero, the visible-but-empty window **closed**.

**And the window is why the refusal cost nothing.** Had the face landed, it would have opened the
one sequence R857 named — a visible case with no LIVE items behind it. **The gate that refused her
wording also held the window shut**, which is not a defence of the refusal but is worth knowing
before anyone hurries to resolve it.

## R868 — What the long-word rule actually counts, and R689's second half

**Reported before repairing, as ruled. The rule is not the length rule its name claims.**

`long-words` counts words of **FOUR OR MORE SYLLABLES**, by `syllables()` — vowel-groups after
stripping a trailing `e`. It never measured letters:

| word | letters | syllables | counted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operations` | 10 | 4 | **yes** |
| `percentages` | 11 | 4 | **yes** |
