## R960 — I condemned on the property the entry predicts, in the check written to apply R937

The first run of this test returned **NEITHER DERIVES on nine of fifteen**, and every one was
`en-wrong-scope-retrieval`.

**That entry means the child retrieved from OUTSIDE the shown window.** A text citing an
out-of-window line is performing the derivation — it names where the wrong answer IS true. My test
scored every out-of-window citation as a failure, which is **condemning on the property the entry
predicts: the exact fault R937 registered, committed inside the instrument built to honour it.**

**The tell caught it before the report went out: nine of fifteen, all one entry** (R955 — a count too
clean to be about content). The expectation is now set BY THE ENTRY, not by the window, and the
verdicts move from 9-neither to 9-both.

**A second fault in the same run, and smaller only by luck.** The quote extractor matched `'` as an
opening quote and read *the family's scepticism about the STORY* as a quoted span, then reported it
absent from the passage — **two texts refused over a punctuation collision.** A quote mark is not an
apostrophe, and a straight quote following a word character is never an opening one.

**Both faults produced REFUSALS, which is the direction that looks like diligence.** An instrument
that wrongly refuses reads as strict; one that wrongly passes reads as broken. **The first is the
more dangerous because nobody investigates a check for being too harsh** — and the only reason these
were caught is that the shape of the refusal was too regular to be about content.

## R961 — Instruments fail toward refusal, and nobody investigates a check for being too harsh

The refusal-direction finding, registered as its own form.

**Every instrument has an error direction, and the two are not equally visible.** A check that
wrongly PASSES reads as broken and gets fixed. A check that wrongly REFUSES reads as strict — and
strictness is the thing this whole estate is built to prize. **So false refusals accumulate
uninvestigated, wearing the costume of rigour.**

**AND THE SKEW IS STRUCTURAL, NOT JUST PSYCHOLOGICAL.** A predicate is written by someone imagining
what a fault looks like, and an incomplete imagining under-matches. **Over-matching takes actively
wrong logic; under-matching is the default state of any pattern that is merely unfinished.** So the
likelier error and the less-examined error are the same error, which is what makes the class worth a
rule.

**THE WEEK'S EVIDENCE IS NEARLY UNANIMOUS.** Every instrument fault recorded since R946 erred toward
refusal: a join-is-a-pair predicate refusing three sound hidden words (R946); a narrow lexicon
refusing `GRAN` (R946); an obscure-word filter discounting `PLUMP/AY` because `ALY` sat beside `LAY`
(R949); a walker reporting **569 executions absent** that were four-fifths present (R955); a type
mismatch refusing **183 seats** across one question type (R955); nine wrong-scope executions and two
apostrophe collisions in one run (R960). **Not one instrument fault this week failed by passing
something it should have caught.**

**THE COST IS NOT A MISSED FAULT — IT IS MANUFACTURED WORK ON SOUND CONTENT.** A false refusal sends
somebody to re-author an item that was fine, or records a standing loss against work that is
recoverable (R957 — twice, before the reason was investigated). **It does not merely fail to find
a problem; it creates one.**

**So the guard is the one thing that does not depend on anybody's suspicion: the SHAPE of the refusal
set.** A refusal population that is regular, clustered in one entry or type or artefact, or a round
fraction of its denominator, is treated as **an instrument hypothesis before it is treated as a
content finding** (R955). Ask it of refusals specifically, because agreement gets scrutinised now
(R173) and strictness still does not.

**Mechanised 2026-09-01, on David's word** — the guard had stood one day as prose, which by R601 is
the weaker form. `assessRefusalShape()` in `scripts/lib/refusal-shape.ts`: an emitter reporting
refusals passes its screened rows (refused, reason, dims), and the three shapes — REGULAR (one
reason covers every refusal), CLUSTERED (every refusal in one dimension value, or one value refusing
wholesale), ROUND_FRACTION (the count reduces to n of ≤12) — print an instrument-hypothesis line
before anyone dispatches a refusal as a content fault. It is a hypothesis, never an exit code: a
true content fault can be shaped, so the guard orders a reading, not a verdict. The carried fixture
(R721) is the three incidents that would have fired — 569 of 689 under one reason, 183 all within
vr-17, 9 of 15 all one entry — plus one irregular clean set that must NOT fire, because a guard that
only ever fires has not been shown to discriminate. `pnpm check:refusal-shape` runs the fixture;
`check:withdrawn-substance` is the first standing emitter to consult it, passing the matched
withdrawn digest as each refusal's reason so that many refusals collapsing onto one substance read
as regular while refusals across distinct substances read as irregular.

**And one test stays withheld under the same discipline.** Resolving a line NUMBER to passage TEXT
remains unrun until the numbering convention is **recoverable from bytes rather than inferred**. An
inferred convention would decide readings by a rule nobody wrote — and, being a matching rule, it
would fail toward refusal like the rest.

## R962 — A shape guard is fed the discriminating dimension, never the verdict text

The first-consumer decision from wiring R961's guard into `check:withdrawn-substance`, registered
as the form on David's word (2026-09-01).

That door's REFUSE verdict is one class string, identical on every refusing row by construction.
**Fed to the shape guard as the reason, it fires REGULAR on any three refusals and means nothing** —
the guard would print INSTRUMENT HYPOTHESIS on every real finding, and a hypothesis that prints on
everything teaches its readers to skip the line. For a guard built because nobody investigates a
check for being too harsh (R961), that is the original fault reinstated by its own mechanism, one
level up.

**So the form: an emitter feeding a shape guard passes the thing that VARIES when the content is at
fault and COLLAPSES when the instrument is.** In the withdrawal door that is the matched withdrawn
digest — many refusals landing on one substance is the regular shape an instrument fault makes;
refusals across distinct substances are the irregular shape genuine content faults have. The verdict
text is the check's own name echoed back, and **a reason that cannot vary across genuinely distinct
faults is not a reason.**

The same test governs the dims, with a mechanical half and a chosen half. A dimension carrying one
value across the whole population is refused by the guard itself as vacuous — that half is
instrumented. **What no instrument can see is a CHOSEN constant**: the guard cannot distinguish "one
reason because the instrument collapsed the faults" from "one reason because the emitter passed its
own verdict class" — from inside, they are the same uniform string. So the discriminating feed is
the consumer's half of the contract, decided once per emitter at wiring time, and it is registered
as a FORM because it cannot be a check.

## R963 — Eleven of eleven name their replaced value: R936 narrowed to a discipline holding under strain

From the authoring store's amendment census (`THE-AMENDMENT-CENSUS-AND-THE-SEAT-LETTER-ANSWERED`,
`9769460da2ae`, dated 2026-08-31), and it narrows the registered line in her favour.

R936 recorded one row seen by accident: her 200th addressed row 17 as `options:D`, the pair sat at
B in this store's ordering, and the amendment landed because she named the replaced VALUE beside the
seat — the form saved it, not the care of either party. **This is the census over every amendment
she ever sent: eleven of ninety-five are addressed by position, and ALL ELEVEN name their replaced
value.** Position-only, no substance: zero — she has never once addressed a target by position
alone. **The unit, stated (David, 2026-09-01, moving this from quotation to assertion): ninety-five
amendments, from thirty-three returns carrying any, among ninety-eight held. Ninety-eight is the
census's SCOPE, not its population** — the returns screened, not the returns that answer for the
eleven-of-eleven — which is why her ordinals can run past 200 while the census holds 98.

**So what R936 registered as a near miss is better stated as A DISCIPLINE HOLDING ONCE UNDER
STRAIN**: the one time an ordering disagreed, the substance she always carries was there to catch
it. **The warning stands anyway — an eleven-for-eleven record is a reason to keep the form, not a
reason to stop needing it.**

The census around the eleven. 566 amendment lines resolve to **95 amendments across 108 blocks**
(the 566 was this store's own published count of the next act, and it was the size of the TEXT, not
of the WORK — a count of lines is a count of a serialisation); 94 distinct targets, so **one chain**
— `item:MC04-GEOM-05:key`, amended at her 182nd and again at her 183rd, the only place order of
application could ever matter, named rather than collapsed; **eight amendments name neither a value
nor a digest and every one is legitimate** — six `library:NEW-ENTRY` mints from her 189th that
replace nothing by construction, two carrying an action rather than a wording — so **not one
amendment in ninety-five replaces something without saying what it replaced**; and **zero block
faults across all 108** — every count she ever declared is true of the block she declared it in.

The census instrument is unfixtured, so its figures cross MARKED — **with the exception the
authoring store named correctly: the zero block faults is a comparison of her declared integers
against counted records, checkable by anyone holding her returns. It needs no fixture to be
believed, only the bytes.** And the census states its own limits: it is a census of what she
DECLARED, not of what landed; the 95 authored wordings were not read against the artefacts they
name; no party's stream but Annie's was counted.

## R964 — The sixth serialisation fault, registered with its own limit: a fault list is read, never counted

The authoring store's finding, from the same census, kept here in their words with their limit
standing as the operative part.

**What happened:** the first census run reported 95 as 67, with three blocks faulting — her 145th
declaring sixteen amendments and carrying one, her 146th nine and one, her 189th six and one. **The
cause:** her blocks come in two layouts — a multi-line form, and a single-line pipe form
(`target: X | replaced: Y | authored: Z`), sixteen of which sit in one paragraph. The parser split
on blank lines and took one target per chunk, so it saw one of the sixteen. **The class, in their
words: a guard that matched a SERIALISATION instead of a SUBSTANCE — sixth in their arc, second in
the rebuild**, the fifth having been published three days earlier as a warning that the rebuild is
exactly where a store reproduces its own worst habits. It did it again in the next instrument.

**How it was caught is the finding: by reading the fault list rather than the count.** Three block
faults named three of her returns; opening one showed the pipe form immediately. **Had the run
reported zero faults and 67 amendments, 67 would have crossed.** The repair anchors on every
`target:` occurrence and takes its scope from the line it sits on — zero block faults after it, on
all 108.

**And the limit, theirs, which this register does not soften: registering a fault class does not
stop you committing it; only an instrument does — and there is no instrument for "parse by shape",
because shape is what a parser is.** What CAN be instrumented is the discipline that caught it
twice: **A FAULT LIST IS READ, NEVER COUNTED.** The same limit arrived here the same day from the
consumer side — R962's discriminating-dimension choice is also a wiring-time discipline the guard
cannot check from inside. Both go in the register as forms because neither can be a check, which is
exactly the class R961 says to watch: the faults that remain are the ones that wear no exit code.

## R965 — A mint lands whole or not at all: the landing writes every field of the governed state

From the vr21-opposite-pull landing (round one, 2026-09-01; caught and fixed 2026-09-02, registered
on David's word).

The mint landed ACTIVE with her description and hint and **no `approvedBy` stamp**. Every entry she
has minted carries `approvedBy: reviewer:rev-0001` — measured precedent on the class, not an
inference — and the attestation is precisely what the wholeness bar reads (R699/R701): a tag
pointing at an unstamped entry is UNATTESTED, and twenty-two carriers were about to be counted
un-whole for a field the landing script forgot, not a state the content was in.

**The omission was invisible to every check that reads the landing's own account, and visible to
the one that reads the governed state.** The landing printed MINTED and was truthful; the wholeness
derivation consults the store, and the store was missing half the class. Completed with an APPROVED
event citing her 208th and David's ratification.

**The form: a landing writes the WHOLE governed state for its class, and the field list comes from
measured precedent on the class — never from what the landing script happened to know.** This is
R57 arriving in a WRITER rather than a door: a door that enumerates drops what it cannot name; a
writer that enumerates under-writes what it did not know, and reports success either way.

## R966 — The high-water rule: declare your emissions, because only the receiver can diff its own shelf

David's ruling, 2026-09-02, after the vr03 crossing stalled invisibly and was found only because
the desk happened to look for it by name.

**Every reader in this estate iterates what is PRESENT.** So a receiving store can enumerate what
it holds and can *never* enumerate what it is missing — the absence has no row to iterate. This is
R579 exactly (*an absent return is not reported absent, it is not reported*), turned around onto the
OUTBOUND channel, where nothing had ever been checked: **the desk has never been diffed against
what it should hold, and nothing on the sending side can do it.**

**AND THE SENDER'S OWN INSTRUMENT DOES NOT CLOSE IT.** `stagingQueue` reads what came BACK and
infers arrival from it, which measures QUOTING, not HOLDING. It reports **743 of 857 staged files
unacknowledged** — and that is a QUEUE LENGTH, not an absence count, because most artefacts arrive
and are never named in a reply. Read as absences it would manufacture seven hundred faults; read as
what it is, it says almost nothing about the shelf. **The diff can only be done by the receiver, and
only against a declaration the sender emits.** `scripts/declare-emissions.ts` is that declaration:
every staged file with its recomputed digest, the high-water mark per kind, and the current file per
family so gaps beneath the mark are findable.

**THE TWO KINDS ARE THE ARTEFACT AND ITS SIDECAR, AND THEY CROSS INDEPENDENTLY.** A sidecar alone
vouches for nothing; an artefact alone cannot be checked against a declared digest. Measured: 571
artefacts, 286 sidecars, **0 mismatches and 0 orphans — and 285 artefacts carrying no sidecar at
all**, half the lane crossing unvouched. A directory sitting in the lane is declared as its own
class rather than skipped, because a silent skip is how a staged thing stops being counted (R98).

**THE NAMING FINDING, WHICH IS THIS STORE'S OWN AND IS BOUNDED.** `stampedName` takes whatever hash
it is handed; its documented example is a TRUNCATED one (`vr-free-ten-c17a98c9d7c439cf.json`, 16
hex) and the desk's own artefacts carry 12. **Every report this session passed the FULL 64-character
digest**, producing ~100-character names where every prior emission produced ~34. Of the 14 files
carrying a 64-hex name, **0 are acknowledged; of the 114 acknowledged files, 0 carry one** — and the
single confirmed stall, `vr03-reversed-relation-crossed-1bfec75c…`, is one of the seven, which
arrived only when re-crossed byte-identical under a 12-hex name. **THE BOUND: one stall and one
arrival of the same bytes under two names is a PAIR, NOT A PROOF.** The separation is real, the
population is small, and the mechanism is invisible from this side. It crosses as a hypothesis the
desk can kill in one line by saying which of the seven it holds — and the declaration is emitted
under a truncated stamp, so it is itself the first test of it.

**One sender is declared. The authoring store emits into the same desk and must declare its own
lane** — this store cannot see it and does not guess at it, which is the same discipline that made
its twenty-four holds correct rather than invented.

**CONFIRMED FROM THE RECEIVING END, SAME DAY — SEE R967.** Six of the seven are not on the desk;
the seventh is there only because it re-crossed under a short name. The declaration's first use
found six stalled artefacts, and the confirmation could only come from the side that holds the
shelf, which is the rule's whole point.

## R967 — Sixteen hex was never a style: a name outside the path's own pattern bypasses every guarantee the path makes

The high-water rule's first use, and it confirmed its own hypothesis in one day (R966).

**The desk answered: six of the seven are absent, and the seventh is present only because it
re-crossed under a short name.** Only the receiving side could establish that — a sender can
declare, and can never diff. The six are the reports: round one, round two, the one-run, the
seventeen-and-serve, the mint-and-door derivation, and the final door report. **Every table the
desk read this week was prose while its artefact stalled**, which is the cost stated exactly: a
sentence cannot be recomputed against a digest, so a reader given prose is asked to trust rather
than to check.

**AND THE CAUSE IS THIS STORE'S OWN AND IS MECHANICAL, NOT A MYSTERY ABOUT THE CHANNEL.** The
staging path matches `-([0-9a-f]{16})\.json` for its restamp and `-([0-9a-f]{16})(?:[.-]|$)` for
its family. **A 64-character stamp matches neither.** So `deliver()` copied the file in while the
restamp, the family match and the supersession every caller believes it is getting all silently did
nothing — and the run printed STAGED. **R87's shape inside the staging path itself: an operation
that is correct, a report that is true, and neither saying that nothing happened.** Sixteen hex was
being read as a house style; it is a CONTRACT, encoded in two regexes, and a name outside it is not
merely unconventional — it is invisible to the machinery.

**Measured before the guard, per R149.** Of 368 artefacts in the lane: **292 carry exactly 16 hex,
69 carry no trailing stamp at all, and 7 carry 64 — nothing sits between.** So the guard fires on
the fault class and on nothing else, and that is a measurement rather than a hope.

**AMENDED ON COWORK'S CORRECTION, ACCEPTED 2026-09-02: THE MECHANISM IS A SIXTEEN-HEX MATCH, NOT A
LENGTH BOUND, AND IT IS SCOPED TO THIS LANE.** The two regexes match exactly sixteen hex; nothing
in them says a name must be short, and reading the finding as *long names stall* would generalise
it into a rule that condemns the authoring store's entire lane and every VERSIONS index — none of
which is wrong, because none of them uses this store's stamp. **A convention is a fact about the
path that reads it, not about names.** The guard governs `deliver()`, which stages only what this
store emits, and it is not to be generalised across stores without those stores' own conventions
in front of whoever generalises it.

**The repair is at the NAMER, not in each caller's head.** `stampedName` now truncates any hash of
16 or more to 16, so every caller conforms without knowing why; and `deliver` REFUSES a name whose
trailing hex run is any other length, naming the contract. A rule that lives in a docstring is
obeyed by whoever read the docstring; the same rule in the namer is obeyed by everyone. The six
re-crossed byte-identical under conforming stamps, each verified three ways — desk copy, lane copy,
and the stamp equal to the bytes' own digest — so every figure already quoted for them stays true.
The 64-hex originals stay in the lane as the evidence of the stall, named beside their replacements
(R86).

**THE SECOND FINDING, David's, from the same declaration: 285 artefacts in the lane carry no
sidecar — half of it crosses unvouched.** An artefact and its sidecar are separate files that cross
independently, so a sidecar can arrive without its artefact and either alone proves nothing. The
declaration is the better answer to it than 285 loose files would be: **one list, itself crossing
under one digest, carrying every artefact's hash** — vouching that cannot be half-delivered, where
per-file sidecars are exactly the thing that can.

## R968 — Delivering a declaration into the inbound path makes it acknowledge itself

Found on the re-run, minutes after R966 was registered, and it is this store's own fault twice over.

**The emissions declaration is placed on the desk's floor so it can be delivered — and the desk's
floor IS an inbound scan directory for `acknowledgedFiles`.** The declaration names every staged
file by construction, so the ledger read this store's own emission as evidence that this store's
emissions had arrived. **Acknowledged went 114 to 542 without one new word from the other store.**
A file that was correctly UNACKNOWLEDGED in the morning was ACKNOWLEDGED in the afternoon because
I had written its name down and put the paper on the desk.

**The ledger's own docstring already forbade this** — *"the evidence has to come from something it
wrote, never from anything on this side"* — so the contract was right, stated, and silently broken
by an act taken for an unrelated good reason. **A stated contract with no mechanism is obeyed until
somebody has a reason not to notice it.** The guard is one line and derives its exclusion rather
than listing it (R57): any inbound file whose basename also sits in the outbound lane is ours, and
is skipped.

**IT WAS CAUGHT ONLY BY RUNNING THE THING TWICE** (R599), and confirmed by PREDICTION rather than
by inspection: the fix should return the figure to about 114, and it returned 112 — the two
missing are this store's own artefacts, now correctly excluded. **A repair that lands on a
predicted number is a different quality of evidence from one that merely changes the number**, and
the prediction cost nothing but saying it first.

**The general form: an artefact that describes a channel must not be delivered INTO the channel it
describes without saying what that does to the instruments reading it.** Every self-describing
artefact this estate emits — declarations, manifests, ledgers — is a candidate for the same fault,
because the reason to place it where the readers look is exactly the reason it corrupts them.

## R969 — The district's first door published, and both of its refusals were instruments

vr-10 publication, 2026-09-02, on David's word. Twenty-five rows DRAFT to LIVE in one transaction,
thirteen assertions passing before the write, window zero.

**THE RUN REFUSED TWICE ON ITS FIRST PASS, AND NEITHER REFUSAL WAS CONTENT.** That is R961 arriving
at the most consequential act in the project: instruments fail toward refusal, and a publication
that refuses reads as a publication being careful. Both would have sent somebody to repair sound
work.

**FIRST: A PIN OVER AN UNORDERED READ IS A PIN OVER A RENDERING.** Row 23's signature holds
`ae3bc2ab38e02441`; the row computed `82e6f4e0e453ec16`, and its bytes had never changed. Landing
her mint on `wet` moved that option's physical row, and the option read carries no `orderBy`, so
the arbitrary order moved with it and the hash followed. **Recomputed in the option order recorded
in the population she signed against, the row hashes to `ae3bc2ab38e02441` — the signature
exactly.** The other twenty-four passed on luck: 19 of 25 rows are not in value order, so the
returned order is arbitrary and stable only until something writes, and any future write to any
option would have refused its row the same way. **Option order is presentation, not identity**
(R936: a seat is named by its value, never its position), so a hash that moves with it is measuring
the rendering — R737's rule arriving at a signature instead of a search. This run verifies in HER
RECORDED ORDER, the pin's own context: evidenced, not permissive, with no permutation search and no
fallback. **Whether the projection should canonicalise option order for every future signature is
a change to what a signature MEANS estate-wide and is not taken here** (R867).

**SECOND: A GATE CONDEMNING A SCRIPT THAT TEACHES BY EXCLUSION.** Three walk scripts were flagged
`internal-id-leak — names option(s) not on the card`. Each names the word precisely IN ORDER TO
RULE IT OUT: *"Water and deep go with lakes, not size"*, *"Dark and sleep go with night, giving no
light"*, *"Hot and yellow go with sun, not its work"*. The rule is a CORRELATE of staleness, and a
script naming a near-miss to exclude it is caught by the correlate and is not the fault — the same
shape as the vr-05 join gate repaired the same day, and her 205th's filter rule for the third time.
All three carry a reviewer APPROVED event on `explanation.walkScript` from her 146th, on the exact
field flagged, byte-identical to the text in the population she read. **So they publish under a

## R970 — `subjectHash` names two different subjects, and nothing on the row says which

Found while preparing the canonical-order ruling, 2026-09-02, and it nearly produced a false
finding about eleven sound rows.

**Most signatures in this estate hash a row's PIN PROJECTION. The fifteen ruled by derivation under
her 206th hash THE EXECUTION TEXT the verdict is about.** Both are written to the same column, and
neither the column, the schema, nor the row says which subject a given `subjectHash` names. **A
verifier that assumes the projection meaning reports the execution ones as content drift** — the
canonical-order analysis classified them NO PERMUTATION VERIFIES, whose stated meaning is *the
content changed after signing*, and eleven English comprehension rows were one report away from
being described that way. They had not changed at all: the subject was never the row.

**This is R608's shape inverted.** There, one decision was split across two fields and neither
sorted. Here, TWO SUBJECTS share one field, and the field name — `subjectHash` — is honest about
being a hash and silent about what of. **A field whose meaning depends on which script wrote it is
a field that reads correctly only to whoever wrote it.**

**Detected, not guessed, and separated before anything is called unexplained:** the analysis now
tests whether a non-reproducing hash equals the sha of an execution text on its own row, and
reports that as its own class. Of 477 signatures over 473 items: 372 verify under the current
order, 56 only under a non-current permutation, **11 are execution-text subjects**, and exactly
**1 is genuinely unexplained** — `ENG-001-WIW-15`, LIVE, signed through the in-platform
comprehension review surface, whose subject this analysis cannot name. That row is reported alone
rather than inside a class of twelve.

**The repair is not taken here.** Naming the subject on the signature — a `subjectKind`, or a
prefix on the value — changes what every stored signature asserts and belongs with the
canonical-order ruling it was found beside (R867).

**ENLARGED THE SAME DAY: THERE ARE AT LEAST THREE SUBJECTS, AND THE THIRD IS THE PRODUCT'S OWN.**
Chasing the one unexplained signature to its source found `draftAssessmentSubjectHash` — the hash
the in-platform admin review surface writes when a reviewer signs, over `{prompt, tier,
options:[{isCorrect, text}]}` with plain `JSON.stringify`: no stem, no explanation, `text` rather
than `content`, and not canonical JSON. **That is the subject the PRODUCT writes, which makes it
the most likely meaning in the estate rather than an exception**, and a verifier assuming the pin
projection reports every row signed through the reviewer's own surface as drift.

## R971 — Prepared, not taken: what canonicalising option order would cost, measured

David's instruction, 2026-09-02: prepare the ruling rather than take it. Recorded here because the
measurement should outlive the conversation; **the decision is not made by this entry.**

**The estate rests on option order more heavily than the vr-10 refusal suggested.** Exhaustively —
every permutation of every signed row's options hashed under both retention projections, a decision
procedure rather than a sample:

- **372 signatures verify under the order the database returns today, and 316 of those verify
  under an order that is NOT value-sorted.** Every one is a single write away from refusing exactly
  as row 23 did. **184 of them are LIVE.**
- **56 have already moved** — they verify only under a non-current permutation, meaning the order
  shifted after signing and nothing noticed.
- **436 of 440 ordering-relevant rows have their signed order recorded in a crossed population
  artefact; 4 have none.** That is the hinge: a signature verifies today only because SOMETHING
  records the order it was taken in, and for four rows the only witness is the live database —
  the very thing that moves.
- **Canonicalising would stop 366 signatures verifying**, across seventeen question types. They
  would not be void — the reading happened — but nothing could re-derive them mechanically, so
  each needs RE-ISSUING by the reviewer. By R909 that costs authority, not a re-read: authority
  arrives fresh, the reading never left.

**Three options, with what each buys and spends.** (A) canonicalise the projection — signatures
stop decaying forever, at 366 re-issues. (B) order the READ deterministically — costs nothing,
stops NEW signatures decaying, fixes none of the existing ones. (C) verify against the recorded
order, as the vr-10 publication did — exact, evidenced, free, and unavailable for the four rows
with no record. **This store would recommend B and C together now and A only on the reviewer's
word**, because B stops the decay at its source, C is already proven in a publication, and A is
the only one that spends her signatures to buy the property.

## R972 — B and C done: the read is ordered for the future, the recorded order verifies the past

Her ruling, 2026-09-02: **a signature is over content, not an arrangement.** David's instruction:
do B and C now; A waits on her word with the 366 figure in front of her (R971).

**`scripts/lib/pin-projection.ts` is the one place, so no script assembles this again** (R429).
`ORDERED_OPTION_READ` carries `orderBy: { id: 'asc' }` — B, and it is deliberately by ID and not
by VALUE, because sorting by value IS canonicalisation and would be option A wearing B's clothes.
`verifyPin()` is C: it tries the order recorded in the population artefact the signature names
FIRST, then the current read order, and REPORTS WHICH MATCHED — so a reader can see at a glance
which rows still rest on the live database. Evidenced, not permissive: no permutation search, no
fallback to comparing content, and a recorded order that does not name every option the row holds
is DROPPED rather than partially applied, because a partial arrangement is not the arrangement
that was signed.

**WHY THE TWO CANNOT BE ONE ACT.** B cannot fix the past: a stored hash was taken over whatever
order the database returned that day, so re-ordering the read now would break it rather than
verify it. C cannot fix the future: it depends on a witness existing. Each covers exactly what the
other cannot, which is why the ruling names both.

**AND THE FOUR WITHOUT A WITNESS WERE WITNESSED BEFORE ANYTHING COULD MOVE.** 436 of 440
ordering-relevant signatures have their signed order recorded in a crossed artefact; four had
nothing but the live database — all four LIVE and serving children, three of them under a
non-value-sorted order, each one write away from becoming unverifiable with nothing anywhere able
to say what it had been. Their exact order is now recorded as bytes with both retention hashes
beside it. **A photograph, not a change**: it re-issues nothing and re-orders nothing, and it makes
C available to those four as it already was to the other 436. `MC05-FDP-08`, `MC01-FDP-04`,
`MC02-NPV-07`, `MC05-MEAS-02`.

**So the finding inverts on measurement and is worth more, not less, for it.** The standing exposure

unreadable to any verifier assuming the row projection. The surface now declares its subject at the

subject and spec, the signature is refused and the row returns to me* — **has now been tested
against the whole closed set and is MET**, so the signature is refused and the row returns to her

## R974 — A hold reaches the row, and prevalence is not authority

Annie's 217th, 2026-09-02. Two rulings, and the first corrects both of us.

**HELD AND LIVE CANNOT BOTH BE TRUE OF ONE ROW.** Her 216th held the signature and left the row's
state unstated; the row was live. **A signature that reproduces under no declared subject cannot
tell anyone whether the bytes moved since the reading**, so the row serves on an unverifiable
reading, and R909 admits no exception for a row already live: identity, reading, authorship, or it
waits.

**AND THIS STORE HAD ARGUED THE OPPOSITE, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** The published hold
said the row could stay LIVE because *an unverifiable signature is not a wrong answer*. That
reasoning conflated two things: it is true that nothing indicts the content, and false that the
content is therefore sound. **The pin is the only instrument that can say the SERVED bytes are the
READ bytes** — so an unverifiable pin puts the content in doubt in exactly the sense that matters,
and the absence of evidence either way is precisely why a row cannot serve on it. *Nothing is
wrong here* is not a finding; it is the shape of not having looked.

`ENG-001-WIW-15` moved LIVE → REVIEWED in one transaction, **signature retained** — refusing to
rely on a signature and destroying the evidence of one are different acts. Blast radius walked
before the write: `en-comp-retrieval` 8 serving → 7, `case-en-01` stays servable, **and no child
had ever met the row**, so the withdrawal cost nothing served. Its current bytes cross for a fresh
reading under the canonical spec with the subject declared, and the row returns on that signature —
**a reading nobody can verify is replaced, not defended**, and replacing it costs less than the
argument about it.

**PREVALENCE IS NOT AUTHORITY.** The draft-assessment shape is the estate's commonest subject
because it is what the product writes when a reviewer signs there — **a fact about a code path, not
a decision anyone made.** A majority produced by ONE WRITER is an undecision dressed as a decision
until someone reads it: the `doorplate` inheritance rule at estate scale. So the subject set carries
no default and marks nothing canonical by frequency; **canonicity is declared on merits and binds
new signatures only**, and the one canonicity that IS declared (her 216th) is about the ORDER of
options within the row projection, never a ruling that the row projection is the canonical subject.
The frequency table is useful and it is not a verdict.

## R977 — A named unknown, and the write log's last line: the inputs are recorded as destroyed

Annie's ruling, 2026-09-02: **stop the hunt at a named unknown.** Recorded in
`content/named-unknowns/eng-001-wiw-15-signature.json` with its elimination trail and its bound.

**THE UNKNOWN, STATED EXACTLY: which bytes were hashed to produce `425245f09b627e89`.** Not who
wrote it, not by what path, not under what spec — all three are known. Naming the unknown that
precisely is what makes it a record rather than an open question, and it is the difference between
a thing nobody is chasing and a thing nobody has thought about.

**HER LAST CHECK WAS THE ONLY ONE THAT SEPARATED THE TWO SURVIVORS, AND IT LANDED.** Something did
record writes to that table on 16 August: `ContentWriteLog` was running from 11:27:29 that morning,
before the signature. What it records is that **at 17:14:58 — one hour AFTER both signatures — this
item's five `ItemOption` rows were INSERTed**, inside a transaction that wrote 2,709 option rows,
within a window of **2,808 DELETEs and 2,815 INSERTs across four transactions**. A bulk
delete-and-recreate of the option table: R62's mechanism, recorded.

**So the elimination resolves in the direction it pointed.** The writer had not moved, the assembly
had not moved, the recorded inputs had not moved — **because the rows it hashed were destroyed and
replaced.** The subject is unreproducible BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by mystery.

**AND THE BOUND IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE FINDING.** `ContentWriteLog` records tableName, recordId,
op, changedColumns, dbUser, applicationName, txId and time — **never values.** So the inputs are
recorded as having been destroyed and their content is unrecoverable from this store. **The unknown
is not what happened; it is what the destroyed rows held**, which is a smaller and permanently
bounded thing. A log that proves an absence and cannot fill it is doing its job, not failing at it.

**The retained signature stays retained, unverifiable and LABELLED** — `subjectKind: UNVERIFIABLE`
with a spec naming the record and the destruction, so a reader meets the reason rather than a null
they must interpret. It stands beside the reading that replaces it, never instead of it: **refusing
to rely on a signature and destroying the evidence of one are different acts.** Both carriers are
stopped — the row is withheld, and no signature can pass that path again without the subject
proving itself from a fresh read (R975).

## R978 — The test suite stands inside the fence: it mints its own reviewer and deletes what it wrote

Annie's 219th with David's ruling, 2026-09-02, and it ends the class.

**A TEST MAY NOT REPOINT, BORROW OR IMPERSONATE A REAL REVIEWER ROW FOR ANY REASON.** The e2e sign
test repointed `rev-0001` — hers — at a throwaway account so a naming path would resolve, wrote two
SIGNED events under her identity on a row she had never read, and restored the row afterwards.
**The restore running does not soften it: the exposure exists while the test runs, and a repair
that depends on a cleanup step completing is a repair with a failure mode.**

**AND THE SECOND HALF IS WHAT ENDS THE CLASS: teardown deletes what the run wrote.** A test may not
leave a signature wearing ANY reviewer's identity in a shared table — not a real person's, and not
its own minted one, which would otherwise accumulate one indistinguishable signature per run on a
real row. Events go first; `AttributionEvent.reviewerId` is a foreign key, so the order is forced.
**That change alone would have prevented this entire thread**, and both exposures — two standing,
and every future run — close with one mint and one teardown.

**THE RULE IS IN A CHECK, NOT A DOCSTRING** (R967's lesson applied the same day it was learned).
`pnpm check:no-reviewer-borrow` refuses two things across every test file, both derivable from the
bytes and neither needing a database: a test that UPDATES a `Reviewer` row, and a test naming a
`rev-`prefixed id outside the minted `zz-e2e-rev-` pattern. Six carried fixture cases, three
must-catch and three must-be-clean, including a comment ABOUT the old borrow that must not fire.
81 test files screened; none borrows.

**THE NINE REFERENCES ARE THREE DIFFERENT THINGS, and reporting them as one would have been the
count-without-its-predicate fault.** Three lines in `reviewer-surfaces.spec.ts` are the borrow —
one test, not three — and are fixed. Five are STRING FIXTURES in pure-function unit tests that
touch no table and are not the harm her ruling names; they were de-personalised anyway, because a
guard carrying a permanent exception is worse than the fixture it excuses. One,
`walk-approval.ts`'s `approvedBy: 'reviewer:rev-0001'`, is **production code recording a real
approval she really gave** — it is not a test, not an impersonation, and it stays.

**THE CLASS, IN HER WORDS: a channel that writes to production tables while wearing the estate's own
credentials.** Every gate this fortnight built stands between the stores and the data; the test
suite stands beside them, inside the fence.

## R980 — A record of destruction names what was destroyed, or it is a record with no subject

Annie's pair, registered as one entry because the two halves are the same rule read in opposite
directions, and each is useless as a guide without the other.

**FORWARD: A RECORD THAT NAMES ONLY THE FACT OF DESTRUCTION BOUNDS AN UNKNOWN, AND THAT IS WORTH
HAVING.** Before her check, the `ENG-001-WIW-15` signature was an unbounded hunt: writer unknown,
mechanism unknown, no floor. `ContentWriteLog` gave it a floor in one query — **at 17:14:58, one
hour after the signature, the item's five `ItemOption` rows were INSERTed inside a transaction that
wrote 2,709 of them, within 2,808 DELETEs and 2,815 INSERTs across four transactions.** The rows
the hash was taken over were destroyed. That converts *nobody knows what happened* into **we know
exactly what happened and cannot recover what was held** — a smaller thing, a permanent thing, and
above all a CLOSABLE thing. A hunt with a floor can be stopped on purpose; one without a floor is
stopped only by exhaustion, and exhaustion leaves no record.

**REVERSE: AND IT IS STILL A RECORD WITH NO SUBJECT, WHICH IS WHY THE UNKNOWN STAYS UNKNOWN.**
`ContentWriteLog` records `tableName`, `recordId`, `op`, `changedColumns`, `dbUser`,
`applicationName`, `txId` and `at` — **never values.** It is a WRITE log, not a VALUE log. So it can
always answer *was this destroyed, when, by which transaction*, and can never answer *what did it
hold*. **It proved an absence and could not fill it**, and no amount of further reading of it will
change that, because the subject was never in it to begin with.

**THE RULE THAT FALLS OUT, AND IT IS A DESIGN RULE RATHER THAN AN INVESTIGATIVE ONE: knowing WHICH
KIND a record is decides which questions it can ever answer, and that is settled when the record is
designed, not when someone comes looking.** A store that wants destroyed values recoverable must
put the values in the record of destruction; a store that logs only the fact buys boundedness and
nothing else. **Neither is wrong and only one of them is usually chosen deliberately.** The failure
this closes is not consulting the wrong log — it is *expecting a log to answer a question its
columns never carried*, then reading its silence as evidence rather than as absence (R98, at the
level of a table's design).

**AND THE ESTATE ALREADY HELD BOTH ANSWERS ELSEWHERE, WHICH IS THE USEFUL COMPARISON.** R62's
recovery works because derived values are deterministic functions of code and **git IS the prior
state** — the subject is recoverable because it was never only in the database. Retention's rule
runs the other way: **a reconstruction may never occupy a `replacedSha256`**, because a value
rebuilt is not the value that was there. `ContentWriteLog` sits between them and belongs to
neither: the destroyed rows were authored content, not derivations, so git cannot rebuild them, and
nothing may be invented into their place. **The honest end state is the one now on the record — a
named unknown with its cause proven and its content permanently unrecoverable.**

## R981 — Two digests travel with every artefact, and quoting one without naming which gives a landing two names

David, 2026-09-02, on a landing reported with one number and read with another.

**AN ARTEFACT HERE CARRIES TWO CORRECT DIGESTS THAT NEVER AGREE.** `findingsSha256` is over a
DECLARED SUBTREE — it identifies the CLAIM and changes only when a finding changes. The staging
line, the filename after `deliver()` restamps, and the `.sha256` sidecar are over the WHOLE FILE
BYTES — they identify the BYTES. Neither is wrong and neither substitutes for the other.

**So "its digest" is not a reference.** `batch-one-landed` was reported here as
`25bf9bc9f4b1ba1b` — its file digest, correctly, and the name it carries — while its findings
digest is `b0e148f0810c67cf`, which recomputes exactly under R729 over its declared subtree. One
file, one name, one sidecar, both numbers true of it, and two of the three names in the question
were these. **A reader given one number and no kind cannot tell a second measurement from a
mismatch**, which is R752's rule — a digest crosses with the spec that produces it — arriving at
the fact that there is MORE THAN ONE digest rather than at any single one being unlabelled.

**The repair is in the artefact, not in the covering message.** `digestsBlock()` emits a `DIGESTS`
section naming both, each with its spec and how to recompute it, so the file answers the question
itself and no covering note has to.

**AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THAT BLOCK COMMITTED THE FAULT IT EXISTS TO PREVENT**, which is the part
worth the entry. It embedded the file digest as a value; writing the value changed the bytes; the
artefact left carrying a name its bytes no longer had — R731 exactly, produced by the guard against
it. **A file cannot state its own byte-hash**, so the block NAMES where the file digest lives (the
filename and the sidecar) rather than reproducing it, and the block is written BEFORE delivery so
the restamp names bytes that already contain it. Ordering is not a detail here: a self-describing
artefact must be complete before the thing that describes it from outside is computed.

## R982 — The binding table: only the store holding the rows can say which cases a population digest still describes

David's instruction, 2026-09-02, and it is the cheap repair for a fault neither store could see
alone.

**A POPULATION DIGEST PROVES WHAT A STORE READ. IT CANNOT REPORT THAT THE ROWS HAVE MOVED SINCE.**
The authoring store binds its whole lane to `bb6be0d3` — correctly, and it has no way to learn that
one case was regenerated underneath it. Twenty-five vr-19 executions were authored against words
that no longer exist and refused at this store's door, which is the expensive way to discover it.
**Only the store holding the rows can declare which cases the binding still describes, so it does**:
`current-row-digests-per-case`, per case and per row, under the same spec the batch's own
`rowSha256` already uses, so the numbers compare directly with what every execution carries.

**AND THE FIRST RUN OF IT WOULD HAVE SENT FIFTY SOUND ROWS TO BE RE-AUTHORED.** vr-17 and vr-18
came back 25-of-25 MOVED — wholesale, two cases, every row. **The crossed population STRINGIFIED
numeric option values**: it records `"7"` where the row holds `7`, so canonical JSON separates them
and the digests differ while the content is identical. vr-13 is strings on both sides, which is why
it read BOUND and the fault did not look universal. **R955's number/string mismatch, in a new
instrument, three weeks later** — and the shape that exposed it was the one R961 names: a refusal
set that is regular, clustered and wholesale is an instrument hypothesis before it is a content
finding.

**So the comparison declares BOTH digests and separates three states that a single number collapses:
CONTENT MOVED, SERIALISATION ONLY, and ROWS ADDED SINCE THE CUT.** Normalising happens where the
comparison is made and never where the row is read (R570), and the raw digest is still declared
because it is what an execution's `rowSha256` will actually be checked against. The verdict a case
carries is about its CONTENT; the raw mismatch is reported beside it as the serialisation fact it is.

**Measured: eleven cases. Five bound exactly, three content-unchanged with a declared reason, three
superseded** — vr-02 on seventeen rows her 197th and 200th amended, vr-05 on one, vr-19 on all
twenty-five. **Naming the moved rows is the point**: "this case has changed" would have sent
somebody to re-author twenty-five rows where one moved.

**What this store still owes** is the forward half: a regeneration that lands should cross its own
supersession of the population it replaces, rather than leaving the other store to discover it by
refusal. This table repairs what has already happened; that repairs what happens next, and it is
not yet built.

## R983 — A regeneration crosses its own supersession, and a check makes it unforgettable

David's instruction, 2026-09-02 — the forward half this store named as owing and had not built.

**A POPULATION DIGEST PROVES WHAT A STORE READ AND CANNOT REPORT THAT THE ROWS MOVED AFTERWARDS.**
The authoring store binds its whole lane to `bb6be0d3`, correctly, and had no way to learn that one
case was regenerated underneath it. It discovered it by refusal — twenty-five vr-19 executions
authored against words that no longer exist, stopped at this store's door. **The binding table
(R982) repaired what had happened; nothing repaired what happens next.**

**AND THE REPAIR IS NOT A HABIT.** Nothing can make a regeneration script remember to declare, any
more than a docstring could stop a test borrowing a reviewer (R978) or a comment could stop a
64-hex name bypassing the staging path (R967). So the declaration is enforced rather than
requested: `pnpm check:supersession-declared` compares every crossed population — found by
scanning, never listed (R57) — against the live rows, and **REFUSES when a case's content has moved
with no notice covering it.** A regeneration that lands undeclared fails the build that follows it.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT DEMAND IS THE HALF THAT MAKES IT USABLE.** Ten of eleven cases differ from
`bb6be0d3` **only** because the population stringified numeric option values — `"7"` where the row
holds `7`. Demanding a notice for those would have declared fifty sound rows superseded and sent
somebody to re-author them, which is R982's catch turned into policy. **Serialisation is not
supersession**, rows added after a cut are not supersession either, and the check says so in
carried fixture cases: content-moved must be caught, a stringified number must be caught by
nothing.

**THE ARREARS ARE PAID AND THEY ARE DERIVED, NOT WRITTEN.** Three notices — `case-vr-02` on
seventeen rows her 197th and 200th amended, `case-vr-05` on one, `case-vr-19` on all twenty-five —
each naming the rows whose content moved with their digests before and after, so the other store
re-binds only what changed. **A notice whose moved rows are computed cannot claim a row moved that
did not, or miss one that did**, and the declaring script REFUSES a diverged case for which no
ruling is named rather than inventing a reason: a supersession states why the rows moved, and a
guess wearing a record's shape is worse than an open question.

**The general form, and it is the third time this fortnight: the store that changes something is
the only one that can announce it, so the announcement belongs to the act rather than to the
noticing.** Every gate before this one stood between the stores and the data. This one stands
between an act and its silence.

## R984 — Two stores, one declared spec, two numbers: the projection belongs in the function, not in each caller

Found at the vr-02 door, 2026-09-02, and it is this store's fault.

**BOTH STORES DECLARED `R729 over {stem, options:[{value,isKey}], solution}` AND COMPUTED DIFFERENT
NUMBERS FOR THE SAME ROW.** The authoring store's `rowSha256` for
`bank-vr-02-two-odd-ones-out-17` was `a0f05ae8332ab189`; this store's supersession notice recorded
the same row's before-digest as `66a7d593585d14bb`. **One row, one spec, two values — and a digest
that agrees with nothing is worse than no digest, because it looks like evidence.**

**THE CAUSE IS A HALF-APPLIED PROJECTION.** Rows arrive from two sources. Live rows a caller
naturally maps to `{value, isKey}`. Rows read out of a crossed population arrive with their options
still carrying `tag`, `tagIsActiveInTheLibrary` and `execution` — and the caller that passed those
through hashed a SUPERSET of the declared spec. Measured against the population's own bytes, the
batch's number is the spec exactly and this store's was the superset. **The other store was right
and this store's notices were unusable for the one thing they exist for.**

**So the projection moved INTO `rowDigest`, applied to whatever it is handed** (R429). One place,
and no caller can get it half right — which is the same repair as `stampedName` truncating for
every caller rather than each caller remembering (R967), and it is the same fault: a contract
stated in a docstring and implemented at the call sites.

**AND THE CLASSIFICATION SURVIVED THE BUG, WHICH IS THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART.** vr-02 read 17 of 25
moved before the fix and 17 of 25 after; vr-05 one; vr-19 twenty-five. The verdicts were right
while the numbers they rested on were wrong, because both sides of each comparison were wrong the
same way. **A result that does not move when a real fault is repaired is not thereby confirmed** —
it means the fault was invisible to that particular test, and R599's discipline of re-running is
what turned a right answer into a right answer for a stated reason.

**The exchange behaved exactly as designed around it.** The authoring store crossed checkable
bindings and NAMED the doubt rather than asserting the five bound; the door compared each against
the live rows and refused all ten; every one of the five rows is among the seventeen the notice
names. **A refusal on arrival is a cheaper finding than an absence**, and both stores now compute
one number for one row.

## R985 — An artefact that publishes a digest should publish the subject it was taken over

The audit David ordered after R984: where else does a caller project rather than the function?

**SEVEN CONSUMERS READ A CROSSED POPULATION'S ROWS AND DIGEST THEM.** One carried a DUPLICATE
IMPLEMENTATION of the declared spec — `declare-current-row-digests.ts` had its own `rowDigest` and
`rowDigestNormalised` — and **a spec with two implementations has two specs**, which is exactly how
two stores reading one sentence reached different numbers. Fixed; the table re-derives identically
(17/1/25), which is what repairing a duplicate should do. Two more hand crossed rows through
UNPROJECTED and are now **safe by the function rather than by the caller** — they do the obvious
wrong thing and get the right answer, which is the whole point of moving the projection inward. The
remaining four only ever project LIVE rows, which is correct and is not this fault.

**The broad grep finds ninety-odd files projecting options inline. Reporting ninety would have been
a count without its predicate** — almost all are projecting live rows for their own purposes. The
population that matters is seven.

**AND THE ORIGIN IS UPSTREAM OF EVERY CONSUMER.** `emit-vr-arc-census.ts` computes each row's
`rowSha256` over the projection `{value, isKey}` — correctly — and then emits that row's `options`
carrying `value`, `isKey`, `tag`, `tagIsActiveInTheLibrary` and `execution`. **The artefact
publishes rows whose `options` field is a SUPERSET of what its own `rowSha256Spec` names.** A
consumer that reads `row.options` and hashes it — the obvious thing — gets a number disagreeing
with the row's own declared digest sitting two fields away. Nothing in the artefact is wrong. **It
makes the wrong thing easy and the right thing invisible**, and both stores duly did the wrong
thing while having read the spec correctly.

**So the rule, proposed and not taken: an artefact that publishes a digest publishes the SUBJECT
that digest was taken over** — as its own field, or by naming per row which keys the projection
includes. Then a consumer hashes what is in front of it instead of reconstructing a projection from
a sentence. **This is R25 at one remove — send the value, not an account of it — and a spec in
prose beside a superset of its own subject is an account.**

## R986 — An entry whose entire carriage lies outside every cut is unmeasured, not unused

David's instruction, 2026-09-02: report it, do not fold it into a census that excludes it.

**`vr-move-letter-both-invalid` is ACTIVE, attested by the reviewer, carries a description and a
child hint — and every one of its thirteen seats sits on a `seed-vr08` row that is
NEVER_SHIPPABLE.** The population cut takes DRAFT, so **every census bound to `bb6be0d3` shows the
entry with zero carriers.** It reads as an entry nothing uses. Everything that uses it is outside
the frame.

**ITS SIBLINGS ARE THE CONTRAST THAT MAKES IT LEGIBLE.** `vr-move-letter-first-word-invalid` and
`vr-move-letter-second-word-invalid` carry thirty-eight seats each, spanning both the twenty-five
DRAFT rows and the thirteen seed rows. **The family is not obscure; this one member of it is
invisible**, and only because of where its carriage happens to sit.

**AN ENTRY WITH NO MEASURABLE CARRIAGE IS NOT AN UNUSED ENTRY. IT IS AN UNMEASURED ONE, AND THE TWO
NEED OPPOSITE DECISIONS.** Reporting zero would have been true of the cut and false of the entry —
R98's rule about a row, arriving at a library entry. So it is reported with its carriage named
rather than counted into a census that cannot see it.

**Three dispositions are open and none of them follows from the measurement**: retire it, because
an entry serving only rows that will never ship serves nobody; keep it and treat the absence as an
AUTHORING gap, because the act is plainly real; or keep it against the proposed vr-08 regeneration,
whose rows would give it visible carriage for the first time. **The measurement says only that the
decision has never been put.** This store does not choose.

**The general shape is R61 one level up.** There, a check screened a population the pipeline never
produced, and its empty run was genuinely correct. Here, an entry is carried only by a population
the cut never admits — **not refused, not held, not counted, and correct-looking in every
instrument bound to that cut.**

## R987 — vr-19 derives open, and the hint that flatters spans both populations

David, 2026-09-02. The fifty land, the door fires, and the generator question widens with an answer
that is not the simple one.

**THE FIFTY LANDED, ALL FIFTY, THROUGH THREE GATES** — row digest against the bytes each was
authored against, tag gate, key gate — and the refusal-shape guard found nothing to shape. **They
were RE-AUTHORED, not re-bound**: the twenty-five that refused a fortnight ago named TAP and 146,
and these name what the rows now read. The authoring store's refusal to re-bind them was right, and
re-authoring was the only sound repair.

**vr-19 DERIVES OPEN: 25 signed, 25 whole, `doorOpensOnThisSection` FIRES** — the district's second
door, and the first to reach it entirely through the exchange rather than by one store's work.
Publication is a separate act and is not taken here.

**THE HINT TEST, RUN ON BOTH POPULATIONS, AND THE ANSWER IS SPLIT.** The entry's own child hint
executed: `first-word-invalid` tells the child to take the letter out and read what is left, and it
FLATTERS when what is left is a real word, because she is then confirmed in the wrong answer.

| | seed (13 rows) | cut (25 rows) |
|---|---|---|
| first-word-invalid | **12 of 13 — 92%** | **14 of 25 — 56%** |
| second-word-invalid | 3 of 13 — 23% | 14 of 25 — 56% |

**THE FAULT SPANS BOTH POPULATIONS, SO IT IS NOT AN ARTEFACT OF THE SEED ROWS** — 26 first-word
seats flatter across 38 rows. **But the rates are not equal, and that refuses the simple reading.**
A single uniform generator rule would flatter at one rate in both; 92 against 56 does not. And the
mirror is more telling still: in the SEED the two halves diverge sharply (92 against 23), while in
the CUT they are identical (56 and 56). **A fault in one half of a mirrored pair points at that
half's rule; equal rates in both halves point at something shared.** The two populations are not
carrying one fault at one rate — they are carrying a fault whose shape differs between them, and
that is a finding about how each was produced rather than about either's rows.

**AND THIS STORE'S FIGURE DISAGREES WITH THE AUTHORING STORE'S ON THE SEED: 12 of 13 here, 10 of 13
there.** The likely cause is named rather than assumed — this store's lexicon is web2 and is known
too broad (R949, the GRAN incident), so it calls more remainders words and therefore counts more
flatters. **The direction of the disagreement matches the known instrument difference**, which is
evidence for that explanation and not proof of it; two seats are the whole of the gap and either
store can settle it by naming which two.

**No repair is taken.** Whether it lies in the generator's letter-choice rule, in the entries'
hints, or in the rows, is a content decision.

## R988 — A broader lexicon is not a fuller count when the question is what a child knows

The two-seat disagreement, settled to the limit one store can settle it, 2026-09-02.

**THIS STORE MEASURED 12 OF 13 SEED SEATS AS FLATTERING; THE AUTHORING STORE MEASURED 10.** The gap
is two seats and **this store cannot name which two**: seven of its twelve flattering remainders are
dialect, archaic or technical — LANT, SARK, SOOL, GOVE, SARE, BAST, BAIN — and naming two of seven
would be a guess wearing a measurement's shape. So this store crosses its HALF: every seat, its
remainder, its verdict and a gloss, and the other store's list settles it in one comparison.

**AND THE FRAMING THIS STORE GAVE IT WAS WRONG, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN THE TWO SEATS.** It called
its lexicon merely BROADER, which implies its 12 is the fuller count and the other store's 10 the
short one. **The hint flatters only if the child reads the remainder as a word SHE knows.** A child
who takes P out of PLANT and reads LANT is not confirmed in a wrong answer — she is confused, which
is a different fault and possibly not this one at all. **For a test about what a child is confirmed
by, a lexicon containing LANT, SARK, SOOL and GOVE is not broader; it is the WRONG INSTRUMENT.**

**So the correction runs the other way from the one this store implied: 10 is likelier nearer the
truth than 12, and both may be high.** Five of the twelve remainders are words a nine-year-old
plainly knows — SIP, CAT, SEAM, SING, and arguably PATE — and the rest are not.

**AND R987'S SHAPE NEEDS RE-READING BECAUSE OF IT.** That entry reported the seed at 92% and the cut
at 56% and drew a finding from the difference between them. **Those figures are correct about the
lexicon and may be wrong about children**, so the shape drawn from them is not yet earned. The
figures stand as measured and the inference does not — which is the distinction R591 names: language
claiming a stronger population than the thing behind it.

**The general form: an instrument known to be too broad is not thereby conservative.** This store
has been recording web2's breadth as a caveat for weeks — GRAN, PLUMP, the rival keys — while
reading its results as generous-but-safe. **On any question about what a person knows, a broader
lexicon does not overcount safely; it answers a different question**, and the direction of its error
depends on which way the question runs.

## R989 — The wrong instrument errs in both directions at once, and the second direction was invisible

R988 established that web2 answers a different question from the one the hint test asks, and that
the error inflated this store's flatter count. **It does not only inflate.** Run the same lexicon
through the key gate rather than the hint test and it errs the other way: it RESCUES stems that
cannot be performed.

Of the twelve distinct word pairs in the vr-08 cut, three cannot be performed at any defensible
child-facing cut, and **web2 shows only one of them as broken**:

- `CHAIR/MOP` — no letter works even under web2. Visible, and already refused.
- `CHEAT/AIR` — every solution web2 admits is carried by `AIRE`, `AIRA` or `CHET`.
- `SHELF/TRAIN` — carried by `THRAIN`.

Two stems therefore sit in the bank wearing a PERFORMS-adjacent verdict on the strength of three
words no child holds. **The same lexicon, on the same rows, on the same day, overcounted the fault
in one measurement and concealed it in another.** A caveat that says "web2 is broad" predicts the
first error and not the second, which is why weeks of recording that caveat did not surface these.

**THE GENERAL FORM: the direction of an instrument's error is a property of the QUESTION, not of the
instrument.** A too-broad lexicon overcounts "is this remainder a word the child will accept" and
undercounts "is this stem impossible". One bound, two signs. So state the direction per question,
never per instrument — "known too broad" is not a caveat, it is half a caveat.

**AND THE REPAIR IS NOT A THIRD INSTRUMENT.** The first attempt at one used the 302-card Word vault
as a child lexicon; it scored 0 of 13 and 0 of 25, and labelled `LEND`, `BRIDGE`, `GATE` and `RAIN`
as words outside child vocabulary. **That output looked like a finding and was a blind read** (R60,
R61). Its replacement — every word this estate has already printed for a child, 4,129 of them — is
better and still under-admits, provably: it flags `FRIGHT`, `HARM` and `CORE`. So the flag ships as
a SHORTLIST for a ruling and not as a verdict, because claiming otherwise is R591. **Where the cut
falls is Annie's; this store can measure sensitivity to the cut and cannot set it.**

## R990 — Equal totals are not co-occurrence, and a duplicated population manufactures the association

R987 reported the two hint kinds flattering at 14 of 25 and 14 of 25 and read one cause behind both.
**One number appearing twice is what a shared cause and a coincidence both look like from outside.**
The discriminating test is per-row: do the two kinds land on the SAME rows? They do not — 5 pairs
carry both against 4.08 expected if the kinds were independent. **The equal totals were accident.**

**AND THE DENOMINATOR WAS NOT 25.** The cut's 25 ids are 12 distinct word pairs: `CHAIR/MOP` three
times, every other pair twice. A duplicate row cannot disagree with itself, so every duplicated pair
enters an association measure twice on one piece of evidence — over the 25 ids the same test reads
10 against 7.84, which is the identical evidence wearing a stronger number. **A duplicated
population inflates every association computed over it and no per-row check can see this**, because
each row is individually well-formed; only counting distinct subjects finds it.

The duplication is itself the finding about production: 25 rows from one generator, one day, one
run, cycling twelve pairs. Every boundary the rows carry — `clusterPosition`, `draftingMethod`,
`itemModel` — is null on all 38, and `sourcedFrom` is null on the thirteen seed rows and identical
on the twenty-five cut rows. **So the seed test Annie asked for cannot be run: no recorded boundary
discriminates within either population**, and that is a fact about what the rows record, not a
negative result. Declaring it is R61 — an empty population is a declaration, never an inference.

## R991 — Her 224th lands as a predicate; the 3.0 cut is unmeasurable here and collides with the firewall

**THE RULING THAT LANDED.** Rows 01 and 06 take `vr02-answered-the-opposite`. Her reasoning is not
a judgement about two rows — *"both pairs join two group members and nothing else, so the act these
seats record is choosing the two that belong"* is **set membership on the stem's own words**, and it
needs no lexicon. So it went into `tag-write-gate.ts` as three predicates rather than two writes:
`vr02-answered-the-opposite` (neither chosen word is odd), `vr02-partial-group` (exactly one is),
and `vr02-surface-link`, which now REFUSES on a pair lying wholly inside the group and stays
UNDECIDED elsewhere — because whether a link rests on look or sound is a judgement no predicate
should pretend to make.

**Screened across all 25 rows and 75 seats, the rule selects EXACTLY the two rows she named**: 59
seats perform their tag, 14 are UNDECIDED, 2 refuse. The script refuses to write if that agreement
fails, and the ruling wins over the rule if they ever diverge. This is the good case of R173 — the
agreement is between two independent things, her reading and the encoding, not a measurement
agreeing with the thing that produced it.

**Her generalisation is the transferable half: a tag names the ACT; the attraction explains which
performance of it the child chose.** The alliteration in pear/plum and bird/bee is real, and it is
why *those* two group members caught her eye — not what she did with them. A tag library that lets
attraction rename the act will retag by salience, which is how both seats were surface-link.

---

**AND THE OTHER THREE INSTRUCTIONS CANNOT BE EXECUTED, FOR TWO SEPARATE REASONS.**

**One: nothing here can measure a 3.0 cut.** The return does not name a scale; the estate's only
frequency scale is Zipf via SUBTLEX-UK, so that is the reading. `FREQUENCY_SOURCE.installed` is
`false` (R281), `data/frequency/` holds its `.gitignore` and its `SOURCE.md` and no data, and
`expectedDigest` is still null. So the correct output is `FREQUENCY_UNMEASURED` — **not a pass and
not a zero: nothing was compared.** The fix is the one command in `data/frequency/SOURCE.md`, run
by a person, and then the digest pinned in committed source.

**She is right that the shape tests must wait, and the reason is worth keeping.** Running
co-occurrence and clustering on web2 would measure the wordlist, and I have now twice built a
substitute instrument that looked like an answer — the 302-card vault scoring 0 of 13 (R989), and
before it web2 itself. **A third improvised lexicon would be the same mistake a third time.** The
figures stay as measured under web2, labelled with the instrument, and the inference drawn from
their shape stays withdrawn, which is her own ruling applied to her own reasoning.

**Two: the regeneration instruction collides with a standing ruling, and the collision is
surfaced, not resolved here.** Her 224th says the regeneration *"searches against the constraint set
at 3.0"*. David's corpus-firewall ruling of 2026-08-19, recorded in `frequency-signal.ts` and
`data/frequency/SOURCE.md`, says of that same list: **"It may NOT be used to select or generate item
content. It measures items that already exist."** A search over the constraint set is generation by
the frequency list — precisely the act the firewall forbids. Both rulings are clear and they point
opposite ways on one action.

**The manifesto governs: a deviation is surfaced, never silent, and this store does not pick between
two rulings by preferring the newer one.** So CHAIR/MOP, CHEAT/AIR and SHELF/TRAIN stay unregenerated
and their rows stay where they are. What is needed is one decision from David: whether measuring a
candidate stem against a frequency cut counts as the list *generating* content, or as it *checking*
a stem a search proposed — a distinction the firewall ruling did not have to draw, because when it
was written nothing was proposing stems.

## R992 — The cut is installed, and a frequency list without a part-of-speech filter is web2 again

**vr-19 IS PUBLISHED.** Twenty-five rows DRAFT to LIVE in one transaction, thirteen assertions
passing before the write, live practice pool 0 → 25, window 0, `case-vr-19` servable. The pin
context was `vr19-the-current-rows-themselves-6b95ddca15bbb06a` and **not `bb6be0d3`** — vr-19 was
regenerated after that cut, so checking a signature against it would have proved nothing about
these bytes. The file was verified by digest before a hash was taken from it.

**THE SOURCE IS INSTALLED.** SUBTLEX-UK, 160,024 rows, sha256 `e40d83af…`, pinned in
`frequency-signal.ts`, bytes gitignored — the licence question was only ever about redistribution,
and fetching for local use was never the act that needed a grant. `FREQUENCY_UNMEASURED` no longer
blocks anything.

**AND THE FIRST THING IT MEASURED WAS ITSELF.** GOVE clears Annie's 3.0 cut at Zipf 3.74, SARK at
3.37, BAIN at 3.17 — **three of the exact dialect remainders the ruling was written to exclude.**
Subtitle corpora lowercase proper nouns into the word list, so a bare frequency cut would have
readmitted them under a better-sounding instrument: **web2's fault wearing a new costume, a number
correct about its corpus and wrong about the question** (R988). The corpus makes the judgement
itself — `DomPoS` is `name` for all four and they are 74–100% capitalised, where every genuine
common word here is under 35% — so 62,097 names are excluded and a verdict resting on one reports
EXCLUDED-AS-A-NAME rather than "unknown" (R98).

**The filter over-excludes and the direction is stated per question (R989's own lesson, applied):**
`minister`, `south` and `god` are DomPoS `name` too, and `AllPoS` cannot rescue them — it reads
`.name.noun.` for `minister` and for `gove` alike. Asking *does this leftover read as a word*,
over-exclusion UNDERSTATES the flatter count and is conservative; asking *can this stem be
performed*, it OVERSTATES refusals and can refuse a sound stem. One filter, two signs.

**THE FIREWALL BOUNDARY IS NOW A FUNCTION, NOT A PROMISE.** David's ruling — *a search may propose
from the generator's own material and be measured at 3.0; it may not enumerate candidates from the
frequency list; the list gates, it does not source* — is implemented in `move-letter-search.ts`:
`generatorMaterial()` reads the words already written into `generate-content.ts`, and the lexicon is
consulted only to accept or reject what that material proposes. Nothing iterates the corpus. **A
list that proposes words has reached the generator; one that judges words the generator proposed
has not**, and the difference is which function owns the loop.

**THE THREE REGENERATED, AND THE BANK MOVED WITH THE ROWS.** CHAIR/MOP → HEART/OLD, SHELF/TRAIN →
TABLE/OWN, CHEAT/AIR → SPEND/SENT, chosen by rank from 1,953 valid candidates rather than by
preference — weakest of the four words maximised, corroborated on the CBBC subcorpus, sharing no
word with each other or with the nine surviving pairs. `MOVE_LETTER_EXTRA` is cycled by
`fromBank(bank, 25)`, so **fixing the rows alone would have let the next regeneration reinstate the
broken pairs, and fixing the bank alone would leave the database disagreeing with the code that
claims to have produced it.** Both, in one run, or neither. All 25 cut rows now perform at 3.0,
verified from the rows and not from the run's own report.

**TWO THINGS STAY OPEN AND ARE NOT REPAIRED HERE.** The cut's 25 rows are still 12 distinct pairs
(R990) — a defect in how the bank is expanded, not in any pair. And `seed-vr08-04` (COAT/HARD) and
`seed-vr08-05` (BEAST/RING) are **performable but MIS-KEYED**: a letter does the task and it is not
the recorded key. They are NEVER_SHIPPABLE and reach no child, which is why they are reported rather
than fixed — but "unperformable" and "mis-keyed" are different faults and the earlier count did not
separate them.

## R993 — A threshold travels with the instrument it was taken on

Annie's 225th: *"the authoring store runs wordfreq 3.1.1 and gets GRAN at 3.44 — two honest
instruments, and a ruling that names only its number cannot be checked across stores."* Measured
here, GRAN reads **3.94** on SUBTLEX-UK. **Half a Zipf apart, same verdict at 3.0** — and nothing
in the number "3.0" would ever have surfaced the gap.

So `cutDeclaration()` travels with every figure taken at the cut: source, digest, retrieval date,
column, **and the name filter** — which is part of the MEASUREMENT, not a detail of the
implementation. GOVE clears 3.0 at 3.74; a store told only "3.0" would admit it and be perfectly
faithful to the ruling as written. `pnpm check:cut-carries-instrument` refuses any emitter that
measures at the cut and publishes no instrument, with a carried fixture proving it discriminates.
One emitter measures today, which is a small population honestly reported — the value is forward,
and the fixture is what makes the empty case meaningful (R60).

**This is R985 one level up.** There, a digest travelled with the keys it was taken over; here a
threshold travels with the instrument it was taken on. **A number without its instrument is a value
with no subject** — and the cross-store case is the sharp one, because both stores are right and
neither can discover the disagreement from its own disk.

**Her per-row ruling is the deeper half, and it bounds the whole apparatus.** *"Knownness depends
on the sentence around the word; a word list answers about words and a row answers about a child."*
So the three doubtful seats crossed as ROWS — stem, seat, tag, the wording the child receives, and
the full three-part set (R573) — not as a word list for adjudication. SOW is the live one: its two
seats sit on DRAFT rows in the cut, and it is the case where **the two columns disagree**, clearing
3.0 on the whole corpus at 3.62 and failing it on children's television at 2.94. SEAM and BAIN sit
on NEVER_SHIPPABLE seed rows and reach nobody.

**One thing her ruling may not have intended, reported rather than assumed:** she ruled BAIN's seat
"regenerates with the rest", but that seat is on `seed-vr08-09`, NEVER_SHIPPABLE by her 210th.
There is nothing to regenerate. The name filter now excludes BAIN entirely, which executes the
ruling for every future use without editing a dead row; rebuilding the seed row itself is a
different act and is not assumed here.

## R994 — A fault reported and not repaired is named in code, or it is lost

Two vr-08 faults were found and deliberately left unrepaired, and both were recorded in prose.
**Prose is the only artefact here with no gate on it** (R178) — a fault living in a paragraph of a
register entry is one nobody meets again at the moment they would act on it.

So `content/vr08-open-items.json` declares each with its reason and whose decision it is, and
`pnpm check:vr08-open-items` MEASURES each from the rows every run: OPEN with its current figure,
or CLOSED when the measurement no longer finds it. **An open item cannot decay into a forgotten
one, and a repair cannot happen silently** — the declaration can only shrink, and it shrinks
visibly. A fault measured OPEN and not declared refuses the run.

**And the check earns its keep immediately by separating two faults an earlier count had fused.**
`UNPERFORMABLE` and `MIS-KEYED` are different: the first says no letter does the task, the second
says a letter does and it is not the one recorded. Measured apart, the seed bank is **0
unperformable and 2 mis-keyed** — `seed-vr08-04` works on O where the key says C, `seed-vr08-05`
works on S where the key says B. My own earlier verification printed "2 unperformable", which was
wrong about both rows in opposite directions: it condemned sound stems and hid two wrong answers.

## R995 — The disagreement set found a fault in the instrument that ran it, and corrects R994

**HER TEST, RUN.** Both instruments over one word population: 685 words — the district's own
adjudication surface, every leftover and every insertion candidate across all 38 vr-08 rows.
wordfreq 3.1.1 is installed locally and returns **GRAN at 3.44, the exact figure she reported**,
which is how this side knows it is running *her* instrument and not an approximation of it.

**THE ANSWER: 97.4% agreement, 18 crossings of 685, split three ways so it sums** — 11 from the
CORPORA (both applying the same bare cut and landing opposite), 7 from THIS STORE'S NAME RULE alone,
