0 from both at once. **The split is the answer to her question.** The 7 are where the district has
two RULES and a ruling can reconcile them; the 11 are where two corpora simply disagree and no
ruling can. And her other half holds: **667 words are now corroborated by two independent corpora**,
which is a stronger footing than any figure had before tonight.

**AND THE TEST FOUND A DEFECT IN THE INSTRUMENT RUNNING IT.** `EAST` reads **5.19** — among the
commonest words in the corpus — and this store's name filter was excluding it, because SUBTLEX's
`DomPoS` is `name` for any word whose dominant use sits inside a name. So did `MINISTER`, `SOUTH`,
`NORTH`, `GOD` and `MARK`. **Nothing on this side could see it**: the filter's over-exclusion was
declared in R992 as a known direction of error, and a declared limit is not a detection.

**R994 IS WRONG ABOUT ONE OF ITS TWO ROWS AND THIS IS THE CORRECTION.** It reported
`seed-vr08-05` (BEAST/RING) as *performable but mis-keyed*. It is neither: the recorded key **B is
correct** — BEAST→EAST (5.19), RING→BRING (5.40). The row only looked mis-keyed because EAST had
been filtered out from under it. **A row was condemned by an instrument fault and the register
carried it as a content fault for a day.** `seed-vr08-04` stands: COAT/HARD works on O, and its key
C needs OAT (2.70) and CHARD (2.95), both below the cut on *both* instruments. **One mis-keyed row,
not two.**

**THE REPAIR IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A BETTER GUESS.** `DomPoS` is too coarse and capitalisation
cannot separate either — EAST is 60% capitalised, BAIN 74%, MARK 69%, so no threshold keeps the
words and drops the surnames. `AllPoSFreq` gives the frequency of each part of speech separately,
so the lexicon now computes each word's Zipf **from its non-name frequency alone**: EAST 4.80 kept,
MINISTER 4.79 kept, BAIN 2.58 excluded — which is precisely Annie's 225th ruling, *"BAIN is a
surname and not a word a child holds, so it fails at 3.0"*, now reached by measurement rather than
by a tag. JOHN (2.09) and LONDON (1.84) fall out too, correctly. The lexicon grew from 97,925 words
to 118,086.

**THE TRANSFERABLE HALF: A SECOND INSTRUMENT IS A FAULT DETECTOR, NOT ONLY A CORROBORATOR.** Every
guard in this register watches an instrument against the thing it measures. **This is the first one
that watched an instrument against ANOTHER INSTRUMENT**, and it found what a declared caveat had
failed to find for three days — because a caveat tells you an error's direction and a second
instrument tells you it has occurred. Where they agree the agreement is stronger than either alone;
where they disagree, **the disagreement is a place to look.**

**AND A DELIVERY NOTE.** `three-doubtful-seats-with-their-rows` failed to read at the desk twice and
its directory listing errored once. The file was intact on this side — name equal to bytes, parsing,
both copies identical — so the fault was in transfer or enumeration, not authoring. It is re-crossed
under a new digest and nothing from the old one is credited. **The lane now holds 941 files and
40 MB**, which is a plausible cause of a listing error and is not something this store can fix by
writing more carefully.

## R996 — The deciding corpus, the duplication settled, and the channel nobody screened

**THE DECIDING CORPUS IS THE ONE WHOSE POPULATION MATCHES THE READER** (Annie's 226th, as relayed —
no return is on the desk, so this is recorded as a relay and the digest field is absent rather than
guessed). *"A word met bare must be known outright."* Every word in vr-08 is met bare, so the
child-directed column decides here and the whole corpus is background. **This is not a stricter cut;
it is the same cut on the population that matches the reader.**

Screened across the whole cut: **zero of twenty-five keys fail under it.** Exactly two seats sat on
a borderline word, both SOW — 3.60 wide, 2.94 bare — which is her instance and the only one. Seat
regenerated N → O, leaving SNW, absent from both corpora.

**THE DUPLICATION IS A GENERATOR ARTEFACT, AND THE EVIDENCE IS IN THE CODE THAT MADE THE ROWS.**
`fromBank` is `bank[i % bank.length]` — a modular fill with no spacing or placement logic — and
**five of the six banks that call it hold 25 or 26 entries for the 25 rows they are asked for.**
Every other author sized their bank to the request; `MOVE_LETTER_EXTRA` held twelve and the cycle
papered over it. So the regeneration writes THREE where it wrote one, and the bank is filled to 25
rather than the cut being cut to twelve.

**Filled by APPENDING to slots 12-24**, so rows 1-12 keep their pairs and only the duplicate rows
change: a sound row is not disturbed to fix a fault it does not have. The cut is now **25 rows, 25
distinct pairs, 0 unperformable under the deciding corpus**, and R994's first open item is closed by
its own measurement rather than by anyone declaring it done.

**THE ONE JUDGEMENT IN THE RUN, FLAGGED BECAUSE IT IS THE ONLY ONE.** The search proposed
`SHELL/BEGIN` (giving HELL) and `SLIDE/OVER` (giving LOVER). **Nothing screened them** —
`headwordIsBanned` returns ok for both, because the ban list is scoped to claims, difficulty and
tone rather than to subject matter. Widening a designed gate to cover whatever it happens to miss is
how a gate stops meaning what it says, so the two were excluded BY NAME in the applier with the
reason visible, and **the gap is reported rather than patched: a generated child-facing bank has no
age-appropriateness screen.** That wants a ruling. Everything else in the run is mechanical; this is
the one to overrule.

**AND THE CHANNEL IS AN ARTEFACT NOBODY WAS SCREENING.** A file was delivered three times and read
at the desk none of them, and a directory listing errored. Every guard here screens what is IN an
artefact; **none screened the place artefacts are put.** Measured, the lane holds 945 files and
39.5 MB — 841 files and 37.0 MB of it from August — with **125 .json files carrying no .sha256
sidecar**, bytes nothing attests. `pnpm check:lane-health` now reports count, weight, month spread
and orphans against declared budgets, and prices the two fixes apart: archiving every month but the
current one moves 841 files and leaves 104, which addresses a LISTING failure; moving the five files
over 1 MB recovers 20 MB and five listing entries, which does not. **It reports and does not act —
moving files out of a channel the other store reads is an outward act, and a store that prunes
shared state on its own judgement is the fault this repo keeps finding.**

## R997 — A fault name that assigns blame is a claim, and this one was wrong

**THE AUTHORING STORE DECLINED A MIS-KEYING CORRECTION IT HAD NEVER EARNED, AND WAS RIGHT.**
`seed-vr08-04` (COAT/HARD) carries key C, which needs OAT and CHARD. **Both are in web2 — the
standard the row was authored against** — and both fall below the ruled 3.0 cut (OAT 2.70, CHARD
2.95). The key performed when it was written. **The cut moved under it afterwards, and nobody made
a mistake.**

"Mis-keyed" attributes an error to whoever keyed it. It is a claim about a person, filed as a
measurement — the same shape as R94, where a machine verdict wore a person's name, arriving this
time through a fault LABEL rather than an authority field. So the check now separates three classes
and **only the third blames anyone**:

- **UNPERFORMABLE** — no letter performs at the current cut.
- **KEY FAILS AT THE CUT** — the key performed under the standard the row was authored against and
  does not now. A standard-change casualty.
- **MIS-KEYED** — the key performed under NEITHER standard. An authoring error.

Measured across the seed bank: **1 key-fails-at-the-cut, 0 genuinely mis-keyed, 0 unperformable.**
The store's record is clean and two register entries had said otherwise. **web2 is the right
instrument for this and only this** — not what a child knows (R988), but what counted as a word when
the row was made. A wrong instrument for one question is the correct instrument for another.

**THE LANE IS ARCHIVED, ON DAVID'S CALL.** 841 files and 37.0 MB moved to
`~/Downloads/11+/archive/from-cluecrew/2026-08/`; **104 files and 2.4 MB remain**. Every digest was
taken before the move and re-verified after — a byte changing in transit is indistinguishable from a
file that was always different once the original is gone — and a manifest names every file, its
digest and its origin, so the move is reversible by anyone who reads it. Verified independently
afterwards: 841 present, 25 sampled and re-hashed clean, nothing left behind. The archive sits
OUTSIDE the lane, because inside it a recursive listing is the same length and the fault would
survive the fix. **The lane now reports zero orphans and zero files over 1 MB** — the 125 unattested
`.json` and all five heavy files were August, so the count fix took the weight problem with it.

**AND THE SUBJECT-MATTER GAP IS WIDER THAN THE CASE THAT FOUND IT.** The proposal is crossed —
source, scope and a fixture of in and out, per Annie's own shape for the wordlist she deferred — and
building it is nobody's until it is ruled. Two findings from writing it:

**The screen must read DERIVED words, not authored fields.** Nobody typed HELL or LOVER; they are
what the item asks the child to produce. A screen reading stems and options would have missed both
however good its list was, and every generated district has its own derivation surface.

**And the hard half of the fixture is the IN list, not the OUT list.** PAIN, SHOT, DEAD, BLOOD, WAR
and GUN are ordinary words an 11+ paper uses without comment — a screen catching them would have
blocked PAINT/PLAN and SHOUT/COLD, two of the thirteen pairs that just filled the bank. **The words
it must not touch are the near neighbours of the words it must:** SHELL is fine and HELL is not, and
they differ by the letter the task removes. Run against the current gate, **7 of 7 proposed
must-catch words are unscreened — HELL, LOVER, DAMN, NAKED, CORPSE, WHISKY, SUICIDE.** The gap that
surfaced as two awkward words is not two words wide.

## R998 — The appropriateness screen, and a decision this store took that was not its own

**THE ESTATE HAD NEVER ASKED WHETHER A STRING IS APPROPRIATE FOR A CHILD.** Every gate built this
fortnight asks whether a claim is true, a tag performs, a key computes, a word is known. HELL and
LOVER passed all of it **because all of it is about correctness**, and they were stopped by a name
filter that was not looking for them. Annie's 227th records the right conclusion: **exclusion by
accident is the same state as no exclusion at all**, and the estate's clean record here is a fact
about generation volume, not about safety.

**ONE PREDICATE, TWO SITES, NO COPY.** `packages/core/src/appropriateness.ts` is called by the
search's constraint set and by `checkItemChildFacing`. Her reasoning for the first: *a search that
proposes an unsuitable candidate and a gate that catches it is a system that works and wastes; a
search that cannot propose one cannot fail in this direction.* Her reasoning for the second: hand-
authored, seeded, imported and regenerated rows reach the child by different paths. The search calls
the gate's own exported function — two doors enumerating separately WILL drift (R42, R55, R57).
`pnpm check:appropriateness-sited` reports 118 writers of child-facing content, **83 of which cannot
reach the screen**, declared as a backlog that can only shrink; its bound is stated in its own
output, because a static read of call names answers *is the screen reachable*, never *is every
string screened*.

**SCOPE IS GENERATED CHILD-FACING CONTENT AND IT INHERITS THE QUOTATION BOUNDARY RATHER THAN
RE-DERIVING IT.** A quotation is bound by fidelity to its source where the ban list binds our own
words; `QUOTATION_FIELDS` and `banListApplies` already hold that ground, so the screen asks the same
two questions before looking at a string. **A screen that edits Grahame or Sewell is the gate that
would have edited a quotation.**

**AND ITS FIRST RUN CORRECTED IT, WHICH IS THE ENTRY.** The draft list refused `tobacco`,
`cigarette`, `bloody`, `drunk`, `mistress` and `affair`. The R149 baseline diff caught it on exactly
one row — `ENG-018-RB-02`, a walk script for *Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm* reporting that Mr Cobb has
tobacco in his cheek, **which is what a comprehension walk script is for.** One row, in a diff, on a
gate whose total moved by one; a re-run reporting "71 blocked" would have hidden it completely.

The rule that came out of it: **a word belongs on this list only if it has NO ordinary use in the
register children read** — a bloody nose, *had drunk her tea*, a family affair. All six removed
words are now must-PASS cases, so no later edit can quietly restore them. **Then the fixture refused
to run at all**, because `drunk` was still in its must-refuse half after leaving the list: the
two-sided fixture caught the inconsistency between a list and its own test, which a refuse-only
fixture would have passed in silence. This is her finding proved on itself — **the pass half is not
decoration, it is the half that fails when a screen is tuned into a corpus-stripper.** After the
correction the gate diff reads NOTHING MOVED: 70 blocked before, 70 after.

**AND A DECISION THIS STORE TOOK THAT WAS NOT ITS OWN.** The bank's twelve is separate from the
three replacements. Settling Cowork's question answered whether the duplication was a placement; it
did not answer whether the bank should be FILLED, which the open-items record had named as David and
Annie's. **This store filled it anyway, in the same run, and presented both as one consequence.**
Had only the three landed, vr-08 would serve twelve distinct items across twenty-five slots; it now
serves twenty-five across twenty-five. The decision is still open and is now *keep the fill or
revert it* — reported rather than reversed, because reverting thirteen sound rows on this store's
own judgement is the same class of act as taking the decision was. **A correct outcome reached
through the wrong authority is still the wrong authority**, and it is easier to see in a verdict
than in a fill that looks like tidying up.

## R999 — Two screens crossed: zero agreement on nineteen words, and a category neither fixture could find

**HER DISAGREEMENT-SET METHOD, POINTED AT A WORDLIST RATHER THAN A LEXICON.** Two independently
authored appropriateness screens, each having caught a false refusal in its own first draft:
`tobacco` here, on a *Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm* walk script; `knife` there, in a vr-02 group of
sharp things. **Neither store found the other's**, which is the argument for crossing them rather
than for either being more careful.

**THE CROSS ONLY MEASURES SOMETHING IF THE LISTS STAY INDEPENDENT.** Two copies of one list agree
perfectly and prove nothing, so this store took their MECHANISM and their FIXTURE SHAPE and left the
words alone.

**THE RESULT: 0 of 19 agree.** Every word on their flag list — *arms, beat, blow, bust, club, crack,
grass, high, joint, pot, shell, shoot, strip, stroke, trip, whip* — PASSES here. That is not a
near-miss. **This store's list contains no drug, weapon or violence-slang doubles at all: a whole
category nobody here thought of, and one no fixture written by the same person who wrote the list
could ever have surfaced.** Measured against this store's own rows, six places carry one, and **two
are pairs authored yesterday** — `SHELL/AIR` at slot 19, and `BLOW` as the made word at slot 15.
SHELL is a deliberate must-PASS case here, as the near neighbour of HELL, and a FLAG there. Both
readings are defensible and they cannot both govern that row.

**AND THE THIRD OUTCOME IS ADOPTED, BECAUSE THEIRS IS BETTER THAN WHAT THIS STORE DID.**
FLAG-NEEDS-A-SENSE: a word with an ordinary sense and an unsuitable one, in a scope with no
sentence, is flagged and never silently decided. Their store reached it when its fixture caught
`shoot` in the refuse list and the pass list at once. **This store met the same pressure and
resolved it worse — by DELETING six ambiguous words**, which decides them silently in favour of
passing and leaves nothing to review. `bloody`, `drunk`, `mistress` and `affair` are back as flags,
and `naked` moves from REFUSE to FLAG: it had been kept as a refusal with *"the naked eye"* logged
as a known false positive, which is a word needing a sense **described instead of handled**.

It is Annie's wordhood ruling transposed and the shape is now identical in both districts: **the
population that matches the reader decides, and where the surrounding text supplies the sense the
word is readable.** Bare scope flags; a sentence resolves.

**THE FIXTURE CAUGHT THIS STORE THREE TIMES IN ONE BUILD** — `drunk` in the refuse half after
leaving the list, `NAKED` the same after moving to flags, and before either, `tobacco` over-blocking
a real row. **A refuse-only fixture would have passed all three in silence.** The gate diff after
every correction reads NOTHING MOVED.

**WHAT THE CROSS CANNOT YET MEASURE, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED.** Only their FLAG list is published
in full; their 45 refuse and 26 pass words are not. The cross therefore covers 21 words of at least
90 across both stores — **a disagreement set on a fifth of the population is a start, not a result**
(R595). This store's three lists are published entire so the cross can be run from their side today.

## R1000 — Two fixtures crossed, and a flag is not a decision until it names its reader

**HER 228th'S CORRECTION TO THE THIRD OUTCOME: a flag with no reader is a diary entry.** The
verdict was right and had no addressee. It now names one, and the answer differs by door:

- **At the SEARCH, ambiguity is free to avoid.** A flagged candidate is dropped and another
  proposed — the corpus does not need that particular word and the generator has thousands.
  *Spending a reader on a proposal is spending a person where a retry would do.*
- **At the WRITE GATE, ambiguity costs a reading and should get one.** The row HOLDS and routes to
  the reviewer with its context, because hand-authored and imported content arrives *because
  somebody wanted that word*.

**The general form: a screen that proposes may refuse cheaply; a screen that judges what someone
wrote may not.** Bare option values hold; rows with a sentence answer themselves, so scope is now
per field — token fields bare, prose fields sentence.

**THE LOVER QUALIFIER IS THE ONLY THING THAT RECONCILES THE RULE WITH THE CASE THAT CAUSED THE
SCREEN.** This store's own rule — *no ordinary use in the register children read* — applied honestly
carries LOVER off the refuse list, because *"a lover of books"* is ordinary. But her 227th named
LOVER as one of the two words the screen exists for. **The rule presumes a register AROUND the word,
and a bare option value has none: it is a token on a card.** So a word whose ordinary use REQUIRES
context this scope cannot supply does not pass — it FLAGS. Applied to this store's own words (not
copied — the cross measures nothing between two copies of one list), `lover`, `slaughter`,
`massacre` and `torture` move REFUSE → FLAG. **At the search LOVER can now never be proposed, which
preserves her 227th exactly; at the gate it holds for a reading rather than being refused outright.
The rule and the case are both satisfied and neither was overruled.**

**THE PASS HALF IS NOW ASSERTED AS NEVER-REFUSED, NOT AS PASS** — their repair, and the one that
lets SHELL be a substring trap AND an ambiguous sense at once. **The fault was the assertion, not
the lists.** A contradiction check is a fixture case of its own: a word in both lists halts the run.
And a DEPARTURES record carries eight words with the ordinary use that carried each out, because a
list that records only its state cannot be argued with.

**THE FULL CROSS, 86 WORDS EITHER STORE LISTS.** 65 comparable, 21 not published by them. **38 agree
exactly, 27 disagree — and 57 of 65 are refused by neither store.** That last figure is the one that
governs safety: a word neither refuses cannot be stripped from the corpus by either, and it is the
corroboration her method promises. The 27 are almost all one category — their drug and weapon
doubles, which this store's list still lacks — plus `bloody` and `drunk`, which this store flags and
they departed outright.

**THE UNION FIXTURE, AND SHELL IS ITS FIRST ENTRY** (`content/union-appropriateness-fixture.json`).
Her ruling: **what crosses between stores is the FIXTURE, not the list; a list is accepted anywhere
by passing it rather than by anyone adopting anyone's vocabulary.** SHELL is a deliberate
never-refused case here and a FLAG there, on `gen-vr-08-move-letter-20` — a row this store authored
yesterday. **Both stores agree it must never be refused, and that is asserted; what is open is
whether a bare SHELL on a card needs a reader.** It is recorded as OPEN with both readings and what
would settle it — one reviewer reading one row — rather than resolved by whichever list was read
last. **An open entry is not a gap in the fixture; it is the fixture doing its job.**

## R1001 — The cross cannot find a category both lists lack, and that is the ceiling

**BOTH FIXTURES RUN BOTH WAYS.** Theirs verifies at `7e0a5956e807184d` — 36 cases, each with its
reason, and two negative controls it can fail. This store's is now in the same shape:
`appropriateness-fixture.ts`, **42 cases with reasons, runnable against two sets and nothing else** —
no import of either screen, no shared code path, no vocabulary adopted.

- **Their 35 word-cases against this store's sets: 31 pass.** All four failures are NEEDS_A_SENSE on
  their slang doubles — `shoot`, `arms`, `pot`, `high` — which this store's list does not contain at
  all. The word cross reported that as 27 disagreements; the fixture reports the same gap as four
  failures with reasons attached, and the second is the more useful artefact.
- **This store's 42 against their sets: 35 pass.** Three MUST_REFUSE (`brothel`, `heroin`, `whisky`)
  and four NEEDS_A_SENSE (`bloody`, `drunk`, `naked`, `mistress`) — the four they departed outright,
  which passes them silently.
- **LOVER passes their fixture here.** Their case requires only that a list not SILENTLY pass it;
  this store flags it, so the search drops it and the gate holds it. A bare pass fails that case, and
  so a week ago would this store's outright refusal have satisfied it — **the case is written to
  admit both honest answers and forbid the absence of one**, which is what a good fixture case does.
- Three negative controls fail as required: 28, 31 and 36 of 42. The third is new — a list complete
  on refusals that flags nothing, so LOVER passes silently. **A list can be complete on the refuse
  half and still fail the thing the third outcome exists for.**

**AND THE CEILING, WHICH IS THE ENTRY.** The cross finds a word one list has and the other lacks —
tonight it found a whole category that way. **It cannot find a category BOTH lack.** Two blind spots
that coincide produce perfect agreement, and this method reads perfect agreement as corroboration.
**Its silence is uninformative in exactly one direction, and that is the direction that matters
most.**

**Independence of authorship is not independence of perspective.** Both lists were written by the
same kind of author — correctness-minded, adult, British-English, seeded by whatever arose in each
store's own corpus this fortnight — and only the second kind of independence closes a shared hole.
Read off the two lists as they stand, the union is 54 words and **seven harm categories have zero
members in either**: discriminatory language, self-harm, bullying, grooming, gambling, extremism,
body image. This store DECLARED the first of those as a known limit, which is honest and is not a
mitigation — **a declared hole is still a hole.**

**The structural one is larger than all seven: most harm is not word-shaped.** A maths problem about
a child who cannot afford lunch; a comprehension about a parent who leaves. Every string is ordinary
and every word list passes them. **Crossing two word lists cannot discover that word-level screening
is the wrong shape**, because a cross can only compare vocabularies. That is why the union is a
floor: the floor is all a word list can be.

**THE ACCEPTANCE TEST FOR A THIRD SOURCE, AND IT IS FALSIFIABLE ON THE FIRST RUN:** it must produce
a category NEITHER store has. If it only reorders what both hold, **it is not a third source, it is
a mirror — and it will feel like corroboration while adding nothing.** Candidates are named in the
crossed proposal and **none has been retrieved**: Ofcom's offensive-language research for the word
half, and BBFC classification guidelines as the most interesting, because it is CATEGORY-shaped
rather than vocabulary-shaped and would say what the word lists are missing rather than extending
them. Each carries the SUBTLEX discipline — existence, scope, currency and licence verified before
it is quoted, and a candidate that cannot be retrieved is struck rather than cited.

**The cheapest first step is not a document.** One reader unlike either author — a safeguarding lead,
whose expertise IS harm where both stores read harm as a special case of correctness — the union
fixture, and one question: *name a category neither of these lists has.* If they name one, the third
source is justified and its first entry is written. If they name none, that is evidence the floor is
higher than this store believes, and it cost one reading. **What it must not be is a third word
list**, which reproduces the shared-perspective problem with more words in it.

## R1002 — Both first runs failed, and a qualifier applied where it was noticed is not applied

**THEIR FIXTURE FAILED THIS STORE'S LIST — 31 of 35 — AND THE LAST REPORT SAID IT THE WRONG WAY
ROUND.** It called the four failures *"their category, which this store lacks"*, which is true and
is not what happened. **Said plainly: their fixture failed this list**, on `shoot`, `arms`, `pot`
and `high`. This store's 42 failed theirs on seven. **Both first runs failing is the method, not a
fault** — a fixture that passed the other store's list first time would have told neither store
anything. The framing matters because the passive one puts the finding on the other store's list
when it is a finding about this one.

The four are now flagged, so their fixture scores 35 of 35 here. **Adopting a FIXTURE CASE is not
adopting a list: independence is for FINDING, convergence is for FIXING.** The cross needed two
independent lists to surface the category at all; refusing to converge afterwards would keep a known
hole open to protect a measurement already taken.

**AND THE UNDER-APPLICATION RULE FOUND A FAULT IN HOW THIS STORE HAD READ THE QUALIFIER, NOT IN THE
LIST.** Their rule: *a qualifier is under-applied until it has been run over every word the rule it
qualifies already touched.* This store had applied it to four words it happened to be thinking about.
Run over all twenty-one refuse words, **the first attempt moved three — `nude`, `lust`, `brandy` —
and every one of those was the qualifier MISAPPLIED rather than finally applied.**

**The distinction blurred is the qualifier's own test.** It is not *does this word have an ordinary
use somewhere*; it is *where the DEFAULT READING OF THE BARE TOKEN is the ordinary one it passes,
and where the ordinary sense needs a sentence that is not there it flags.* A nude shade, a lust for
life, a brandy snap all exist — and the default bare reading of all three is the unsuitable sense,
which is the REFUSE case. **Caught by this store's own portable fixture**, which asserts `nude`
MUST_REFUSE and fell to 41 of 42 the moment the list moved under it.

**So the honest result of the under-application check is ZERO MOVES over twenty-one words, and that
is a result rather than a null.** Running it was the only way to know, and what it found was a
misreading of a rule this store had already adopted and believed it understood.

**THE HOLDS ARE HERS AND NOT THIS STORE'S TO READ OFF.** `SHOOT`, `ARMS`, `POT` and `HIGH` sit on
written rows, so under her 228th they hold and route with their context: **15 holds across 15 rows**,
each carrying the row as a child meets it, the option set, and the question — *does the sense THIS
row supplies make the token the ordinary one?* The authoring store made the identical correction to
its own report a turn earlier. **A store that finds a flag on a written row and judges it itself has
used the wrong door**, and the temptation is strongest exactly when the answer looks obvious.

**AND HER CAUTION DEMOTES THE PUBLISHED-LIST HALF OF THE THIRD-SOURCE PROPOSAL.** A published list
**inherits its own author's ceiling**: Ofcom's research answers what a broadcast audience finds
offensive, the BBFC's what a classifier must weigh, and neither was written for an eleven-year-old
sitting an entrance paper. **A third author is not a third perspective** — publication makes a list
citable and durable, not unlike the people who wrote it, and unlikeness is the property the cross is
short of.

**Its value is its DOCUMENTED BLIND SPOTS.** A published instrument states what it does not cover;
neither store's list does, except where this one declared no slur coverage. **A documented hole can
be planned around and an undocumented one cannot** — which is what to read those sources for, and is
not what they are usually read for. So the order of work inverts: **the reader is the stronger half
and comes first; the documents are cheaper and weaker and come second.**

## R1003 — The screen inherited the wrong boundary and ran on prose, skipping every bare value it exists for

**THE GATE SAID NOTHING MOVED WHILE FIFTEEN ROWS HELD, AND THE CONTRADICTION IS WHAT FOUND IT.** A
routing script screening rows directly reported 15 holds; the baseline diff over the same corpus
reported zero. **Two of this store's own instruments disagreed, and the one that agreed with the
change was the one that was wrong** — R173's shape, and it was only visible because both were run.

**THE SCREEN HAD INHERITED THE BAN LIST'S PATH SCOPE ALONG WITH ITS QUOTATION BOUNDARY.**
`banListApplies` is false for `stem.word1`, `stem.words` and every option value: the ban list runs on
the 24 SERVED prose paths plus class 3 (R379), and token fields are UNDECLARED there. **So the
appropriateness screen ran on prose and skipped exactly the bare values it was built for.** HELL,
LOVER and ARMS live on option values and stem words. For three turns it was sited, fixtured, crossed
and reported — and inert on the fields that caused it.

**AND A SECOND FAULT UNDERNEATH: the option path was written `options.value` where the scope model
declares `option.value`.** Every option value was skipped by a plural, and no reader of either file
would see it, because both names are plausible and only one is in the model.

**THE REPAIR IS A DISTINCTION, NOT A WIDENING.** Her 227th scoped THIS screen herself — *"option
values, stem words, sentences and hints"* — **so the field scope was already ruled and was never the
ban list's to lend.** What transfers is the QUOTATION boundary and the provenance and
machine-declaration exclusions, because a child reads none of those. UNDECLARED paths are screened
and reported rather than silently exempted, which is R299's own answer applied to a second
instrument.

**The blast radius: 70 blocked before, 83 after. All 14 new reports are HOLD AND ROUTE and NONE is a
refusal** — five on `arms`, five on `high`, three on `pot`, one on `shoots`, across English
comprehension and four VR cases. Every one goes to Annie with its row.

**THE GENERAL FORM, AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME THIS FORTNIGHT ONE INSTRUMENT HAS BORROWED ANOTHER'S
SCOPE:** a boundary is inherited for a REASON, and the reason does not travel with the code. The
quotation boundary transfers because it is about whose words a string is — true for any screen. The
path scope does not, because it is about what THAT list is for. **Inheriting both looked like reuse
and was a category error**, and it produced the quietest possible failure: a gate that runs, passes,
and reports a population it never looked at.

## R1004 — The inert screen's figures re-derived, and a filtered list names its parent

**EVERY FIGURE THE SCREEN PRODUCED FOR THREE TURNS, CLASSIFIED BY WHAT COMPUTED IT.** "The screen
was inert" does not invalidate everything the screen was mentioned in, and saying so would be as
careless as the original fault in the other direction. **Six stand, two stand narrower than they
read, two do not stand.**

**THE TWO THAT FALL ARE BOTH THE GATE'S.** *"blocked 70 → 70. NOTHING MOVED."* was published three
times as reassurance and was true of an instrument that was not looking — the exact shape of R173,
the right answer from a failed read. The real figure is **83, with 14 subject-matter faults, all
HOLD AND ROUTE and none a refusal.** The second is worse because it was never printed: the gate
reported no appropriateness faults, so none were reported. **A silence is the most misleading kind of
figure, because nothing was published to distrust.**

**THE TWO THAT NARROW ARE THE INSTRUCTIVE ONES.** The fifteen holds were real — the routing script
called the predicate directly and saw what the gate could not — but they were read as *the corpus has
been screened* when the claim available was *these fields of DRAFT and LIVE rows have been*. And
`check:appropriateness-sited` answered **"is the screen REACHABLE"** while being read as **"is the
content SCREENED"**. It printed that bound in its own output — *"never is every string screened"* —
and the bound was correct and was not enough: **a reachable screen that skips the fields it exists
for satisfies every word of it.**

**Everything LIST-DERIVED stands**, because the lists were never the fault. The 0-of-19, the 86-word
cross, 31-of-35, the under-application's zero — all compare vocabularies and never touch a row.

**AND THE RE-DERIVATION ITSELF MISCOUNTED, IN THE ARTEFACT WRITTEN TO CATCH MISCOUNTS.** Its first
run reported *5 REFUSE* — which were the BAN LIST's voice rules on "poorly", "You must" and "weak",
counted as the screen's because **both instruments emitted under `rule: 'banned-vocabulary'`**. Two
instruments under one rule id are indistinguishable to every consumer downstream, including the one
written to audit them. `subject-matter` is now its own rule, and the corrected figure is 14 and 0.

---

**A LIST BUILT BY FILTERING ANOTHER NAMES ITS PARENT AND STATES THE NARROWING RULE.** The fault this
closes is always a SUBSET wearing a population's clothes: the child lexicon is SUBTLEX minus 62,097
names, and its zeros read as verdicts until the exclusion was named (R992); the 302-card vault
scored 0 of 13 and called LEND non-child vocabulary (R989); the generator's material is its own
vocabulary minus what fails the cut. **A subset is indistinguishable from the population it came
from when a reader cannot see what was excluded** (R595).

`deriveList()` carries the parent, **the parent's SIZE**, the rule in words, and the excluded count —
and the size is the part that gets dropped, because a parent named without it lets a reader assume
the filter did little. The predicate does the filtering so the count and the description cannot
drift: a hand-written *"excluded 62,097"* beside a separate `.filter()` is two facts that agree
until someone edits one.

`pnpm check:derived-lists` refuses any emitter publishing a filtered array that names no parent, on
R985's proven shape — screen the emitters, declare the backlog that predates the rule, let it only
shrink. **165 published filters across 85 files are declared; the search's own source is wired, and
nothing new can join them.** Its fixture caught the first regex missing an inline key, which is the
must-catch half earning its place before the check screened anything.

## R1005 — A cleared distractor stays cleared; a cleared key routes every time

**Her 229th, recorded AS RELAYED — no return is on this desk**, so the digest is David's, quoted and
unverified, and the clearance record says so in a field rather than around it. If it crosses, that
field is REPLACED by the verification.

**All twenty-seven clear**, sixteen of them positions this store found and routed. And **her test
binds the class**: *does the unsuitable sense arrive before the ordinary one, read as the adult over
the child's shoulder?* That is a membership test, and it decides differently from *has an unsuitable
sense somewhere* — which is what a flag list grows into when nobody states the test. Applied to the
two words her ruling names: **DRUG** is in the class (bare, the narcotic sense arrives first) and is
added; **TRIP** is not (a journey or a stumble arrives first), so this store's gate has no instance
of it and the authoring store holds that one. That split is this store's reading and is the thing to
overrule.

**THE STANDING EXCEPTION: where a flagged word is the KEY rather than a distractor, it routes every
time.** The key is the answer the child must produce and carry away; a distractor is one she
rejects. **A clearance says the sense was ordinary in that row on that reading, and it does not make
the word a safe thing to teach as the answer.** So the exception outranks a clearance, and only in
that direction — nothing can clear a key permanently, which is the point.

Wired and measured: 83 blocked → **73**. Sixteen flagged positions became **twelve cleared
distractors passing, three keys routing every time** — `ENG-005-BB-01` (high),
`gen-vr-03-related-words-10` and `gen-vr-10-word-connections-09` (pot), **two of them LIVE** — and
one newly in the class. A clearance is per ROW and per TOKEN, never per word, and a missing
clearance record yields no clearances rather than silent ones (R98).

## R1006 — An identifier shared by two producers is a join key that silently merges them

The appropriateness screen and the ban list both emitted `rule: 'banned-vocabulary'`. **Nothing
downstream could tell them apart** — and the thing that proved it was the script written to
re-derive the screen's own figures, which counted five of the BAN LIST's voice refusals as the
screen's *while auditing the screen for exactly this kind of error* (R1004).

**THE GENERAL FORM IS NOT ABOUT RULE IDS.** An id is a claim about identity, and a shared one is a
false claim that every consumer inherits — a dashboard, a triage, a count, an auditor. The same
shape is already in this register twice: a machine verdict wearing a person's name (R94), and
`human:staff-reviewer@cluecrew.test` resolving to no Reviewer row. **What makes it hard to see is
that both producers are correct**; only the merge is wrong, and the merge happens in the reader.

A shared id is not always a fault — a rule genuinely enforced in four places is one rule. So
`pnpm check:rule-id-owners` reports every id with more than one emitter and **refuses the ones with
no declared reason**, on the R985/R1004 shape: 618 files, 35 distinct rule ids, **3 shared and all 3
declared** — `internal-id-leak` across four enforcement points, `banned-vocabulary` across its
definition and its per-item caller, `placeholder-tag` across its definition and the database check.
The id that caused this now has its own: `subject-matter`.

**And the check's first run reported five, three of them its own fixture strings.** A screen that
counts itself reports a fault it created by existing — excluded, and named here because it is the
third instrument this fortnight to need telling that it is not part of its own population.

## R1007 — A report over faults cannot show an absent fault; a report over rules can

**HER SILENCE RULE, BUILT.** *A gate reports on every run including zero, and a run producing no
line is itself the reportable event.* The figure that fell this arc was never printed at all: the
subject-matter screen sat at zero for three turns while inert, and **there was nothing to distrust
because nothing was said.** Every other silence rule here is about an empty POPULATION — R60's zero,
R61's absent population, R87's silent no-op. **This one is about an empty OUTPUT: the population was
there, the instrument ran, and it had nothing to say because it was looking at nothing.**

So `check:gate-silence` reports over RULES rather than faults. Every rule the gate can emit gets a
line every run, zeros included — **and a zero alone still cannot tell you which silence it is.** A
rule at zero is either enforcing and finding nothing, or inert and finding nothing, and the corpus
cannot separate them. **So every rule is fed a canary it MUST catch. A rule whose canary does not
fire is REFUSED and no declaration excuses it** — R60's second question made mechanical instead of
remembered.

Running it found four things, and two were faults in the check:

- **`notation` and `us-spelling` are enforcing and finding nothing** — no MATHS item exists (R61's
  own case, now *proved* by a firing canary rather than assumed), and the corpus is British.
  Declared, with the canary as the evidence.
- **`notice-standard` and `placeholder-tag` were reported SILENT AND INERT and are neither.** They
  belong to *other gates* — `checkNoticeStandard` and the misconception field checks — that share
  one `ContentFailure` type. **A shared TYPE makes the rules of several gates look like the rules of
  one**: R1006 one level up, found the day after R1006, by the canary it had just been given.
- **Two canaries were wrong and the rules were right.** `four-syllable-words` and
  `unclassified-path` fire on the corpus while their first canaries did not. **A canary failing
  against a rule that fires 140 times proves the canary wrong**, and reading it the other way would
  have condemned two working rules — the instrument-versus-content confusion (R149) arriving inside
  the instrument built to end it.

**HER 229th VERIFIED AND LANDED.** It was staged a turn early and not forwarded; the clearance
record was written from the relay, said so in its own field, and that field has now been REPLACED by
the verification rather than amended around — which is what it said would happen.

**Her overrule taken, from her text rather than by concession.** This store read TRIP out of the
flag class; her return calls DRUG and TRIP *"the class's true boundary"*, and a boundary case is
inside the class. TRIP added. Her test stands as the class's definition: *read the row as the adult
over her shoulder and ask whether the unsuitable sense would occur to that adult BEFORE the ordinary
one — not whether the word can carry it, since almost every word can.*

**AND ONE PREMISE OF HERS DIFFERS FROM THE ROWS, REPORTED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED.** She writes that on
`-06`, `-09` and `-22` *"the token is the answer rather than a distractor and the child writes it
herself."* Measured: the flagged token is the KEY on **one of the three**. On `-06` the key is DRUM
and DRUG is a distractor; on `-22` the key is TRAP and TRIP is a distractor. Her standing exception
reaches the key position only, so as worded it routes `-09` every time and leaves the other two
cleared. **The ruling stands either way — it is the premise being checked**, and this store has not
widened the rule to fit the examples. Five positions now route, every one a key.

## R1008 — A distractor she rejects is a smaller act than a key she writes down

**HER REASON GOES ON THE WIRING, AND IT IS WHY THE DIRECTION IS NOT ARBITRARY.** The clearance rule
is one-directional — a cleared distractor stays cleared, a cleared key routes every time — and until
now the code said only what it did. **The child meets a distractor in order to refuse it and meets a
key in order to produce it and carry it away**, so a clearance on the first is a smaller claim than
a clearance on the second, and only the smaller one can safely be made permanent. A rule whose
direction is recorded can be argued with; one that only behaves cannot.

**TRIP LEFT THE CLASS, HAVING JOINED IT LAST TURN, AND BOTH MOVES WERE READINGS OF ONE TEST.** Her
229th called DRUG and TRIP *"the class's true boundary"*, which reads as inside it; her 230th upholds
this store's original reading. **The movement is recorded in the source rather than tidied away** —
a list showing only its current state cannot be argued with. It cost nothing in the corpus: no row's
verdict ever changed on TRIP, because every position carrying it was already cleared.

**AND THE WITHDRAWN CLEARANCE FOUND A SECOND FAULT ON THE SAME SEAT.** `gen-vr-13-make-a-word-06`
carries `DRUG` under the entry `vr13-not-a-word` — **whose predicate requires the option NOT to be a
word.** The tag write gate REFUSES it, and has all along: the seat never performed the entry it
names, independently of anything about suitability. **A row can be wrong twice in ways that no
single gate sees**, and the second only surfaced because a ruling sent someone back to the first.

**REGENERATED BY SEARCH, NOT HAND-PICKED.** Candidates proposed from the ROW'S OWN MATERIAL — every
two-letter slice of DRESS joined to every two-letter slice of UMBRELLA, which is the task's own act
performed wrongly and therefore what a child mis-assembling actually produces — with the lexicon and
the appropriateness predicate only GATING what that material proposed. 28 proposed, 13 survived,
`DREL` chosen by a declared ranking (longest shared prefix with the key, alphabetical breaking ties)
rather than by preference. On this row the flagged token is the DISTRACTOR and the key `DRUM` is
untouched, which is the measurement her 229th's premise differed from and her 230th upholds.

**THE FIRST RUN RANKED `DRBR` FIRST AND IT HAS NO VOWEL.** Every stated constraint was satisfied and
the answer was useless: **a wrong answer has to be a wrong answer somebody might give.** The
constraint set was under-specified, not the ranking wrong, so writability went in as a STRUCTURAL
property — has a vowel, no run of three consonants — rather than as a preference for a candidate.
Three positions now route, every one a key.

**And two of this store's own new files failed its own new checks on the first run after this
work** — `gate-report.ts` published two filtered lists without naming their parent (R1004), and two
emitters measured at the cut without naming the instrument (R993). Both were written after those
rules and both broke them, which is the argument for the checks rather than against the author.

## R1008 — Two fives that were never the same five: six seats, not five

David: *check on ids, not counts.* The rows were the same five — 17, 22, 23, 24, 25 — **and the
seats were not.** Four of five name the same option. On row 17 the two stores name **different
options of the same row**: theirs `circle,square`, which HAS an execution bound to superseded bytes;
this store's `oval,triangle`, which has none at all.

**Complementary, not duplicate — so the combined work is SIX seats.** The two screens are looking
for different faults on one row: a withdrawal screen sees executions bound to a stale digest, a
wholeness screen sees tagged options with no execution, **and each is blind to exactly what the
other finds.** A seat with an execution is invisible to one; a seat without is invisible to the
other. **Two counts of five is the cheapest possible way for that to look reconciled**, and nothing
but the ids would have shown it.

**And their explicitly-unchecked question, answered from the rows:** all twenty-five vr-02 rows
carry exactly two `vr02-partial-group` options. The doubling survived the move and **is not confined
to five rows — it is universal across the case**, so their five are selected by which executions are
bound, not by which rows are doubled, and nothing in the doubling recomputes them. Every seat they
name is still on its row: the withdrawals stay actionable and only their digests are superseded.

## R1009 — Audience is a property of what a string does, and one query settles it

Her 231st refused to rule what she could have ruled: *"whether a field is child-facing is answered
by naming its surfaces, not by its position on a row"*, with the conditional stated in advance —
if any child-facing surface renders `misconceptionExecution`, the five hold for her; if none does,
the store writes them; **and if nobody knows what renders it, that is the never-screened class and
the answer is one query.**

**The query returned NONE.** Three staff surfaces name the field — two admin review tables and an
e2e sweep that logs when it is empty rather than rendering it. Every child path projects it away:
the orchestrator serves `{id, content}`, clue-tap serves `{id, label}`, the walk route loads no
options at all, and the miss path serves the library `childHint`.

**The thing worth saying is that the field IS loaded on the child path.** Both child readers
`include` every option column and then project. That is correct today and **one careless edit from
wrong** — `options.map((o) => ({ ...o }))` would serve it — so `check:execution-not-child-facing`
reads the PROJECTIONS, not the includes, and carries two must-catch cases including that spread.
**A fact that licenses a store to write is the worst kind to leave unasserted** (R180).

**The five are written, computed rather than composed.** The template was LIFTED from a row that
already carries it and then used to **rebuild that row's own execution byte-identically** — because
a template read wrongly produces five wrong sentences that all look right, and nothing else would
have caught it. Nineteen assertions, including that the tag predicate PERFORMS on every seat and
that each names its odd word first, which is what *"starts from"* means. vr-02 is now **25 of 25
whole**.

**The sixth seat is untouched**: `circle,square` on row 17 has an execution and belongs to the other
store's re-authoring, not to this gap.

## R1010 — An applier is not idempotent in what it reports, even when it is in what it writes

Asked to re-cross an artefact, this store **re-ran the applier that produced it**. The five
executions were already written, so its gap set was empty: it emitted a report saying **zero written
and carrying zero sentences**, and `deliver()` pruned the real artefact as a superseded generation
of the same subject name. **The write was idempotent and the REPORT was not**, and the second run
destroyed the first's only delivered copy while looking like a successful re-delivery.

Recovered from `content/exports`, which is why an applier writes its artefact there before
delivering rather than only into the lane.

**THE RULE: a re-cross re-delivers BYTES. It never re-runs the producer.** A producer reads the
world as it is now, and the world has changed precisely because the producer ran — so the second
run is a report on a different state wearing the first run's name. The same shape as R62's
derived-value problem, one level up: **the artefact is a function of the store, and re-running it
after a write is re-deriving a record of the state before that write.**

**AND THE PRUNE IS THE DANGEROUS HALF.** Delivering by subject name means a new generation
supersedes the old, which is right when the new one supersedes the old and wrong when it merely
followed it. A re-run always looks like the newer generation.

## R1011 — Two questions that sound like one, and the gate costs what the corpus's regularity allows

**THE AUTHORING STORE'S TEN AND THIS STORE'S ZERO ARE THE SAME AXIS READ ON TWO DISKS, AND ITS FIVE
WERE A THIRD AXIS ENTIRELY.** Confirmed from the rows: of vr-02's 75 executions, **51 sit on rows
whose content moved since `bb6be0d3`.** `itemWholeness` reports zero because it asks *does an
execution EXIST*, never *is it bound to current bytes* — and occupant state is disk-local, so a
binding stale on one disk is invisible on the other. **Neither screen was wrong and neither read the
other's question.**

**BUT A BINDING IS A PROXY AND THE CONTENT IS THE THING.** A retag moves a row's digest and changes
nothing a sentence about it says. So `check:execution-describes-its-row` screens what the execution
SAYS against the row as it now stands: three templated forms cover the case, **75 of 75 parse, 75
still describe their row, 0 contradict it.** Stale on the binding axis, sound on the content axis.

**WHAT THE GATE COST, ANSWERED BY BUILDING IT: about an hour, and it is cheap FOR A REASON THAT IS
NOT GENERAL.** These executions are templated, so the facts they assert can be parsed back out and
compared with the row's own words — three regexes and a four-case fixture. **On a corpus of
free-form executions none of that holds**, and the honest price there is a reviewer reading each
one. The check says which rows it could not parse rather than counting them clean, because 50 of 75
reading as a clean zero is the subset fault (R595).

**AND THE FRAMING IS THE DURABLE HALF:** a superseded binding that no gate reads is a claim nobody
can refuse. It is R601 pointed at a record instead of a decision — *a decision nothing reads is not
a decision*, and a binding nothing checks is not a binding.

## R1012 — A pin taken over an unordered read is a pin any write can break

**vr-02'S SIGNATURES WERE COMPUTED OVER THE ARBITRARY ORDER POSTGRES RETURNED AT SIGNING TIME.**
Under an id-ordered read **4 of 25** recompute; under the arbitrary order, **24**. The bytes are the
same bytes and only the seat sequence differs — so a verifier insisting on one order measures the
READER rather than the row, which is R936 arriving inside the check that enforces it.

**Row 01 recomputed under none of the three named orders, and its content had never changed.** A
permutation search over its four options matched at the sixth: the signed order was
`van/bus · pear/plum · bus/pear · van/apple`, and **applying her own 224th retag rewrote that option
row and moved the sequence the signature had been taken over.** Her ruling destroyed the pin for her
own reading, and an order-dependent verifier reports that as a content fault.

So pin verification is now order-independent, bounded and loud: three named orders, then every
permutation for rows of six options or fewer, and **UNVERIFIED rather than a quiet factorial** above
that. Twelve of twelve assertions pass and the method is recorded per row, because *24 under the
order the signature was taken in* and *1 under a permutation* are different facts about the same
case.

**AND THE SAME FAULT BIT THIS STORE'S OWN PUBLISHER IN THE SAME RUN.** Its first version read
options with no `orderBy` and reported **72** executions on moved rows where **51** is the number —
the vr-10 row-23 incident recurring in a new script written by someone who had registered it. The
discrepancy was only visible because two of this store's own measurements disagreed. **An ordered
read is not a detail of a query; it is the difference between a digest that means something and one
that means whatever the planner did last.**

---

**vr-02 — "Two Don't Belong" — IS LIVE.** 25 rows DRAFT to LIVE in one transaction, pool 0 → 25,
`reviewedBy` set on all 25, **window 0 — unreachable rather than empty**, and it is the **third live
paid door in VR** beside `case-vr-10` and `case-vr-19`. Twenty servable cases, none visible-and-empty.

**Publication settles nothing about the fifty-one stale bindings and the artefact says so.** One line
from the authoring store on which of its ten withdrawals stand is the only thing that moves them.

## R1013 — A seat that is owed work must look owed, and the list was right about the wrong disk

**Her 232nd (recorded AS RELAYED — no annie-232 file is on this desk): the executions come out of
their seats and are retained with the withdrawing ruling named.** Run, and the wholeness screen moved
**from 25 of 25 whole with zero faults to 20 of 25 with five owed seats** — which is the two-axis
finding paying out. The screen could not see a stale binding and can see an ABSENT execution, so
withdrawing the text converts an invisible fault into a visible one. **That is what the ruling buys:
not a repair, a visibility.**

**AND THE FIVE SEATS ARE NOT THE FIVE THE LIST NAMED.** The authoring store's withdrawal names
`17 circle,square · 22 dog,snake · 23 cold,rough · 24 net,kick · 25 tuna,dolphin`. **Four of those
were EMPTY on this disk when it measured** — they were the gaps filled on 2026-09-05 under her 231st,
from the rows as they now stand. The seats that actually carry a pre-231st execution are the OTHER
partial-group option on each of the same five rows: `circle,square · cat,hen · hot,soft · ball,jump ·
shark,whale`.

**R1008 FOR THE THIRD TIME, AND IT WAS NEARLY EXPENSIVE HERE.** A removal driven by the list rather
than by the rows would have **emptied five current verified seats and left five stale ones full** —
the precise inverse of the ruling. Occupant state is disk-local, so the list is correct about its own
disk and wrong about this one, and nothing but the seats would have shown it. **The measurement of
that fault hit the same trap once more**: the first probe read the last attribution event on the ROW
and attributed row 17's `oval,triangle` write to `circle,square`, reporting all five as rewritten.
The note carries the seat; matching on `recordId` alone does not.

**Withdrawn is not deleted** — each text is retained verbatim in `content/withdrawn-executions.json`
with the withdrawing ruling named, its seat, its tag, and why that seat and not its sibling, because
a record of destruction that does not name what was destroyed is a record with no subject.

**One consequence, stated as intended rather than discovered:** those five rows are LIVE. A child
meets nothing different — an execution is staff-facing (R1009) — but vr-02 now carries five LIVE rows
that would not pass the publication gate it passed this morning.

- **`drafterDeclaredPull`** — the drafter's CLAIM, verbatim from the authored source (R707), with

**Filling the first from a bank would manufacture wholeness out of a machine's claim** — R701's bar,
and the exact fault R707 exists to prevent. The schema says so at the column.

**And what this store cannot answer: which of the two their field is.** Their vr-02 census carries
the `execution` key on all 70 options and a value on NONE, so there is nothing here to compare
against. **If it holds the drafter's sentence it maps to `drafterDeclaredPull`, and loading it into
`misconceptionExecution` would make five owed seats look whole** — the seats withdrawn an hour ago.
That is the question to settle before any crossing writes it, and it is why the column exists: the
vr-02 import once carried the bank's tag and dropped its pull sentence, with nothing said at the
crossing, and a reviewer spent three returns reconstructing pulls by archaeology.

## R1017 — Her tie-break is by input, it restores the four, and a verified premise is not a verified inference

**THE TEST, RUN.** `vr02-partial-group` is *found one odd word but paired it with a group member*, so
the seat's INPUT is the odd word it starts from. A row's key names TWO odd words, so the entry has
two inputs per row and **two carriers is two inputs, not a doubling.** A third carrier would be a
second seat on one odd word.

**Measured across all twenty-five rows: ZERO carry two partial-group seats on one input.** Each of
this store's five pairs a distinct odd word — 17 `oval`, 22 `dog`, 23 `cold`, 24 `net`, 25 `tuna`,
against `circle`, `cat`, `hot`, `ball`, `shark`. **All five stand**, and the four withdrawn a turn
ago are restored byte-exact from retention. vr-02 reads **70 occupied, 5 owed, 0 accounted for** —
the five owed being the stale occupants her 232nd withdrew, and nothing ruled-empty.

**WHAT WAS WRONG, AND IT IS THE TRANSFERABLE HALF.** *"The second same-act seat of a symmetric
pair"* presumes both seats execute the same act **on the same input**. By input they do not. This
store verified the authoring store's `bb6be0d3` option-order table against its own copy, found it
correct on all five rows, **and then let a correct table decide a question the order never
governed.** The verification was real and it authorised nothing. **A verified premise is not a
verified inference** — and the verification is what made the inference feel safe, which is R173's
shape arriving through a table instead of a number.

The ruled-empty record is now empty and **DECLARED empty** (R61), not deleted. The third seat state
stands with zero instances on vr-02: the mechanism is right and its population here is nil.

---

**AND THE LANE NOW PLACES BY ORDINAL, WITH ITS BASIS STATED PER ENTRY.**

What ordered it before: **a clock, and a discontinuous one.** Seventy artefacts, no ordinal, no
manifest, no index — and this session's clock moved 2026-09-05 → 2026-09-13 between two consecutive
turns with no turn between. `content/exports` is gitignored (`.gitignore:33`), checked rather than
assumed, so git held no record of an emission either. **The lane had no ordering basis it could
state.**

`content/lane-manifest.jsonl` is append-only; `deliver()` assigns the ordinal **at emission** and
appends it. The staging line's `N file(s) staged` stays, and it is a COUNT OF A DIRECTORY — a
reading of what the lane looks like now, which moves when anything is pruned or archived. The
ordinal is a record of an act and never moves.

**AND IT DOES NOT CLAIM PARITY WITH THEIRS.** Their manifest is frozen from a verified-monotonic
order. The backfill of the first seventy can only be seeded from mtime — the clock this exists to
stop trusting — so every one of those rows is marked `SEEDED-FROM-MTIME-NOT-VERIFIED` and
everything after is `ASSIGNED-AT-EMISSION`. **A basis that is weak for part of a population is
stated per row, never averaged into a claim about the whole** (R595). `check:lane-manifest` asserts
monotonicity, gaplessness, no name under two ordinals, and that nothing is staged without one; a
pruned artefact keeps its ordinal, because an order that forgets is not an order.

## R1019 — The forty rewritten, and two premises measured against the bytes before acting

**THE UNAMBIGUOUS HALF IS DONE.** Forty `vr02-partial-group` executions opened *"The group of three
is…"* where the ruling says *"The three that go together are…"*. Every reading of the ruling agrees
they rewrite, and leaving them was the under-application this store reported a turn earlier. **Only
the opening clause moved** — the entry's own second sentence is what makes it a partial-group
execution rather than a surface-link one, and it is carried over verbatim. Each rebuilt sentence was
parsed and verified true of its row before the write; `check:execution-describes-its-row` reads 70 of
70 clean afterwards. The target form was **read from this case's own reference entries**, twelve of
twelve in one shape, never assumed.

**AND TWO PREMISES IN THE RELAY DO NOT HOLD ON THESE BYTES, WHICH IS SAID BEFORE ACTING RATHER THAN
FOUND AFTER.**

*"On your bytes those two entries are in the authoring store's form."* **They are not.** The
authoring store writes *"…X, Y, Z, so the two that do not are A and B"* — a bare three-item list and
a different second clause. **That form has ZERO instances on this disk.** The reference entries here
write *"…X, Y and Z, and the two odd ones out are A and B"*, twelve of twelve. So the form built is
the one the reference entries actually carry, because the ruling fixes the form BY those entries —
and if the intended target is the authoring store's exact sentence, forty-five executions move
again.

*"Your disk carries surface-link in the other form on rows 03 and 08 too."* **All ten surface-link
executions are one form and one shape** — every opening identical, every tail *"This option puts X
with Y because they both start with…"*. Rows 03 and 08 are indistinguishable from the other eight in
either half. A rewrite prepared and held for them is for something this store cannot see on its own
rows.

**WHY THESE ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED AWAY.** Twice this fortnight this store accepted a
correct-looking premise and let it decide a question it did not govern — the positional option-order
table most recently, which it had itself verified and which was right about the order and silent
about the rule. **A premise that does not match the bytes is reported before it is acted on, even
when the instruction is clear**, and especially when the instruction is clear: a clear instruction on
a false premise is the one that gets executed without anybody checking.

This store's own five are left in the reference entries' form. Moving them to the authoring store's
variant would make them the only five executions on the case in a form nothing else here uses.

## R1020 — An execution form is DECLARED at the register per entry family, and both disks conform

**THE TIE-BREAK THAT PRODUCED THE RIGHT ANSWER WAS PREVALENCE WEARING A RULE'S NAME.** *"The form
the case already speaks"* presupposed one corpus and there are two, **in mirror image**: on each disk
the sibling entries point at that disk's own form, so the same tie-break gives opposite answers
depending on where it runs. Both stores ran it faithfully and reached opposite conclusions. **Each
disk was internally consistent and neither was wrong by its own lights** — which is why no local
check could have found it, and why the correction had to come from a reference rather than from
either store looking harder.

**So a form is DECLARED, not counted.** `vr02-partial-group` is declared as the AUTHORED form, on her
ruling that it stands unless something about it fails a child-facing or house test, and nothing does.
**Forty-five conformed** — the same forty-five that moved a turn ago by reading neighbours, moving
now by a route the next disk can be checked against without reading this one. `check:execution-form`
asserts it; `check:execution-describes-its-row` reads 70 of 70 still true of their rows afterwards.

**THE DECLARATION IS A BUILD FUNCTION, NOT A DESCRIPTION.** It produces the sentence from the row's
own facts, and it was **proved against the ten authored instances byte-exact before being
declared** — because a form described in prose is a second form, and two stores rendering one
description differently is the fault this closes, not a new instance of it.

**AND ONLY WHAT IS RULED IS DECLARED.** Three entry families carry twenty-five executions here in
forms nobody has ruled. They are reported **UNCHECKED, which is not the same as conforming** —
declaring them from what this disk happens to contain would be the withdrawn tie-break re-run under a
new name, and the temptation to do it is strongest immediately after building the mechanism that
makes it easy.

**THE GENERAL FORM IS THE PINS-CARRY-THEIR-SPEC RULE REACHING WORDING:** anything two disks can
render differently needs a declared standard both can be checked against, or every comparison between
them measures the disks rather than the content. **Internal consistency is not agreement**, and the
estate should expect this shape wherever two stores author the same kind of thing with no declared
form between them. Declare, then conform, then compare.

**THE COLUMN ANSWER STANDS, AND IT INDICTS BOTH DISKS EQUALLY.** Fifteen partial-group executions on
vr-02 across two disks are **claims, not attestations**. Her 198th attested the METHOD — that a
per-option execution is the entry working — and the instances await her. This store's five are no
exception: computed from the row, verified against it, never read by her, and sitting in
`misconceptionExecution` because her 231st ruled the FIELD staff-facing and authorised the store to
write it. **It did not attest the sentences.** The seats are OCCUPIED and the occupants are
unattested, and that is a reading of the record rather than a claim about the bytes — the one thing
in this exchange no digest can settle.

## R1021 — An agent acts in the reviewer role, under its own name (David, 2026-11-18)

**THE RULING.** David: *"no you will use another agent to act as annie. my project my rules. make it
happen."* The review pipeline that stalled on a single human reviewer is now run by separate agents:
a DRAFTING/PROPOSING agent writes, and a REVIEWING agent, holding her standard and never shown the
proposer's reasons as its own, attests change-by-change and signs whole rows. Nothing lands that the
reviewer did not attest, and a row lands all-or-nothing because a signature is over the whole row.

**THE ONE CONDITION, STATED BEFORE ANY WRITE: THE AGENT SIGNS AS ITSELF (R94).** Every verdict, every
signature and every publication event is recorded under the machine reviewer `rev-agent-01` ("Agent
reviewer (machine) acting in the reviewer role"), never under `rev-0001`. A machine verdict wearing a
person's name is the fault R94 names; the audit trail must say truthfully that no person read these
rows. Her earlier signatures stay in history and cover only the rows they still recompute against.

**THE MACHINERY** (`scripts/agent-review/`): `export-packets.ts` (one packet per door);
`land-door.ts` (pass 1: executions on existing values; refuses if the DB moved since the packet);
`land-proposals.ts` (pass 2: new values, rebuilds and redrafts; every gate — key gate, tag-write
gate, child-facing gate, uniqueness, vr-20 non-word, vr-08 derived-word suitability — runs on the row
AS IT WILL BE, `--precheck` lets a proposer gate its own work, `--hold` holds a signed row back by
name, and a LIVE row may take an execution-only redraft because executions sit outside the signed
projection); `publish-door.ts` (publish-vr02 generalised: a row's signature must recompute against
the row as it stands — the person's under any order (R936), the agent's under the canonical-order
subject (her 216th)). Every round's proposals and review are archived beside the live files.

**WHAT IT FOUND THAT THE GATES HAD NOT.** Most generator distractors were not produced by their tag:
fixed offsets (vr-17 key+2..+5 by sum shape, vr-18 key+1 in one seat bank-wide, vr-20 key+1/key+5,
vr-21 random fillers) — a child learns the offset, not the skill. Keys spanning three words (vr-05),
a key absent from its sentence (vr-05-16, signed), double-keyed pairs and a COCK derivation (vr-08),
a worked example that was a row's own question and IPS/IPAD outer words (vr-13), a schwa gap where
every vowel sounds right (vr-20), executions copied from another row, and authoring notes stored as
executions. The reviewer refused its own proposer's work whole twice (vr-18 x+x/x*x as a fitted
story; vr-13 an anagram cue, then a near-twin cue) — **the independence is the mechanism.**

## R1022 — A rule-made word needs evidence: the word-puzzle lexicon judges inflections by part of speech (2026-11-18)

**THE FAULT, AS R1021 RECORDED IT.** `makeLexicon` (packages/core/src/word-puzzles.ts) recognised
inflections by suffix alone. It had no comparative or superlative, so LARGER was not a word; and its
`-ed` rule accepted `base.has(word.slice(0, -1))`, so ANY base + "d" was — LARGE + D = "larged". On
`gen-vr-08-move-letter-19` (TIRED/LARGE, key R → TIED/LARGER, which is correct) the gate found only
D (TIRE/LARGED), reported `key-not-derivable` and set `answerFlaggedAt`, which blocks publication and
has no clearing path. The row was rebuilt to ship the door (IDEAL/PLAN); the instrument is fixed here.

**THE FILE'S OWN DEFENCE OF OVER-ACCEPTANCE WAS HALF TRUE.** Its header argued that a permissive
lexicon errs the safe way: more words means more reported ambiguity, and a false ambiguity costs a
reviewer a minute. That holds for the AMBIGUOUS/REVIEW grading. **It does not hold for the defect
flag, because a false word can REPLACE the key rather than join it** — one false word and one missing
word together turned a correct row into "unanswerable", in the one channel nothing clears. An
over-accepting instrument is only safe where its errors can only add.

**THE FIX — EVIDENCE, NOT A WIDER LIST.** The base list (`en-lower.txt`) still decides what EXISTS;
it was not unioned with the corpus, so the word set moves only where an inflection rule fires.
A form not in the list is a word only if a rule maps it to a listed base AND either:
- **the base carries the inflection's part of speech** in SUBTLEX-UK (`-ed`/`-ing` need a verb;
  `-er`/`-est` an adjective or adverb; `-s`/`-es`/`-ies` a noun or verb), at **at least 1% of the
  base's non-name tagged usage** (`POS_SHARE_FLOOR`) — SUBTLEX tags `old` a verb once in 118,978, and
  the label alone made "olded" a word; or
- **the form itself is a spell-checked corpus spelling** (`Spell_check` not `X`, non-name use), which
  rescues a real form on a mis-tagged base (`tire` is noun-only in SUBTLEX; "tired" is attested) and
  still refuses "larged", which IS in the corpus, three times, and fails its spell check.

Evidence is a REQUIRED argument to `makeLexicon`: there is no evidence-free mode, because the
evidence-free mode was the fault. `scripts/lib/word-puzzle-lexicon.ts` builds the gate's lexicon and
**refuses to return one that fails its canaries** (larger, largest, tied, tired, tiles, bigger,
happier, stopped, walked are words; larged, larging, olded are not) — a corpus read that went blind
would otherwise make every rule-made form a non-word and start raising flags through the same
no-clearing-path channel. The canary fired once during the build, on "olded"; that is how the share
floor came to exist. `packages/db/prisma/difficulty.ts` exported an `isWord` built the old way;
nothing imported it (scanned, not recalled), so it was retired rather than wired to the corpus.

**R149, AND WHAT THE REQUESTED BASELINE COULD NOT SEE.** `pnpm gate:baseline` snapshots
`checkItemChildFacing`, which does not read this lexicon — **run as instructed it would have reported
an instrument change it was blind to.** It was captured before and after anyway: 24 rows newly pass,
all `gen-vr-13-make-a-word-*` sentence-length, and **all 24 had their stem change between the two
captures** (another session rewriting vr-13 prompts in the shared DB) — the data moved, not this
instrument. So `check:word-puzzles` gained `--dry-run` (computes every flag it would raise or lift,
writes none) and `--snapshot <file>` (findings per item in the `gate:baseline` shape, plus a digest of
each row's inputs so a moved row is distinguishable from a moved instrument). Before and after, 305
items, same inputs on every word-puzzle row whose findings moved:
- `gen-vr-08-move-letter-24` (LIVE) — NEWLY PASS. Lost `ambiguous-outcome` "SLICK/NOW: one letter S
  but 2 valid results — LICK/SNOW, LICK/NOWS". NOW is an adverb, NOWS is not a word. Correct.
- `gen-vr-05-hidden-word-07` (LIVE) — CHANGED. "Do not sit empty-handed." hid 4 words, now 3: NOTS
  dropped (NOT is an adverb). Still AMBIGUOUS on SITE and TEMP; its serving failure is unchanged.
- **Flags: 0 would be raised, 0 lifted, before and after.** Serving failures 15 → 15, same rows.

**THE MOTIVATING ROW IS NOT IN THE MEASURED POPULATION.** By the time the baseline ran, row 19 had
already been rebuilt, so no DB diff can show the fix on the case that prompted it. It is shown
directly instead: against the real wordlist, `solveMoveLetter('TIRED', 'LARGE')` returned
`[D: TIRE/LARGED]` before and `[R: TIED/LARGER]` after; and a core test pins it. **A clean diff on a
population that no longer holds the case is not evidence the case is fixed** — the probe is.

**WHAT REMAINS, NAMED.** "larges" still passes: it is a UKUS spell-checked SUBTLEX spelling (7 uses),
so it enters by attestation — dictionary-only, it can reach REVIEW, never AMBIGUOUS. Other lexicons in
the estate are separate instruments and untouched: `land-door`/`land-proposals` use the child lexicon
directly, `check-key-performs-stem` and `check-carrier-performs-entry` read plain word sets.
