## R1023 — Agents may rewrite held English item text; the return leg carries every change to Cowork (David, 2026-11-20)

**THE RULING.** David, asked whether agents may now rewrite the 183 English drafts R1022 held for the
authoring store: *"Yes, agents rewrite."* This extends R1021 from REVIEWING to AUTHORING, for those rows
only. "Cowork authors, the DB holds" stood because two stores editing one item drifted invisibly; it is
not repealed. It is overridden for the held rows, by David, because the store it routes them to has
delivered no English since the end of August and the rows would otherwise never move.

**THE CONDITIONS, STATED BEFORE ANY WRITE.**
1. **Machine authorship is recorded as machine authorship.** Every rewritten row carries an AMENDED
   event naming the drafting agent as author and `rev-agent-01` as reviewer, with the exact fields it
   changed. No row is attributed to Cowork, to Annie or to any person for text an agent wrote (R94, R98).
2. **The hold is cleared only by the review that placed it re-reading its field** (R1022). The
   reviewer reads each rewritten row against its passage and against the ORIGINAL hold reason, and
   says whether that fault is fixed; a row leaves the hold file only on SIGN with the fault fixed.
3. **Independence.** One agent drafts, a separate agent reviews and never adopts the drafter's
   reasons as its own. Every change is attested, every touched row signed whole, all-or-nothing.
4. **Fix the fault named, nothing else** — no restyling of fields the hold did not name, so the
   changeset Cowork must absorb is as small as the faults.
5. **The return leg carries every change** (R88, "export a MERGE, never a wholesale replace"): the
   landing writes a field-level changeset — item, field, value before, value after, the hold it
   answers — as its final step, delivered for Cowork to merge.

**A PRECONDITION THAT COULD NOT BE MET HERE, NAMED.** The plan was to diff Cowork's copy against the
database before writing, in case Cowork had moved since August. Cowork's store (`~/Downloads/11+`)
is not on this machine, so that diff was NOT run. The changeset is therefore built to be safe against
a moved copy: it carries the BEFORE value of every field it changes, so Cowork can tell at merge time
whether its own copy still holds what this side replaced, and must not apply a change whose before
value it does not hold.

**OUTCOME (2026-11-20).** Of the 183 held rows, **180 are rewritten, signed by `rev-agent-01` with the
original hold re-read and fixed, and LIVE**: English went from 197 to 377 LIVE. Three rounds: 146 of
183 landed in round 1, 32 of 36 in round 2 (each row repaired from the reviewer's named faults, with
the previous proposal in its packet), and 2 of 4 in round 3. 514 field changes over 180 rows:
executions 152, option values 93, hints 77, walk scripts 72, tags 49, stem text 22, `lineRefs` 13,
`passageRef` 10. Every change travels in `english-rewrite-return-*.json` with its before value. Across
all rounds the reviewer attested 207 changes and refused 15. It held further rows whose changes it had
attested, for faults elsewhere in the row. Its commonest grounds were rewording nobody asked for and a
line number one off where a clause runs across two lines.

**STILL HELD (3), with the latest finding on each row in the hold file (`latestUnderR1023`):**
`ENG-022-GK-11` (two drafters each found no honest key: "each time" holds at one site of the three a
whole-text item needs; a fix is a new question, not a repair); `ENG-018-RB-02` (a walk cites lines 63
to 64 for a clause beginning on line 62); `ENG-026-AL-03` (an execution calls Grandad's stated reason
"the real reason", which the passage leaves open).

**WHAT THE PASS FOUND.**
1. **12 of the 183 holds were already fixed on the store.** The earlier retag pass had corrected the
   tag a hold named, and the hold file still listed the old fault. Those rows landed unchanged once the
   reviewer re-read them. A hold reason describes the row on the day it was written, not the row now.
2. **R57 again, inside this pass's own tooling.** The rewrite packets hid `_`-prefixed stem keys (as
   `export-english-packets` does), so a drafter could not name them. A rebuild replaced the stem

3. **A person's approval marker on machine text.** ENG-001-WIW-10's hint carried
   `hintAuthoredBy: Annie`. Rewriting the text while the marker stayed would have served agent words

6. **Gate-forced rewording of option values the holds did not name.** The appropriateness screen refuses

## R1025 — The maths answer-rank shortcut, and a door total that hid it inside templates (2026-11-20)

**THE SHORTCUT.** On maths-01 (179 LIVE rows, seven types, four options), option ORDER is shuffled per
child, but VALUE rank is not. Across the 161 rows whose options compare in one unit, the key was the
second-smallest on 69 (43%) and the largest on 13 (8%). "Never the biggest, usually second-smallest"
beat 25% by a wide margin. The cause is in the diagnosis itself: the commonest mistakes (rounding without
compensating, a step dropped, subtracting the wrong way) land just either side of the key. Roundness was
checked as a second tell and is clean: on 0 rows is the key the only non-round option.

**THE REPAIR, under R1021**, in three rounds (proposer, independent reviewer, `land-proposals
--from-live`). The rule: a distractor is replaced only if its tag occurs at least 10 times on the door,
with a value that tag's mistake really produces. Any re-tag keeps the value. **41 rows changed** (37
values, 4 re-tag only). The reviewer attested 143 changes and refused 14. **Door ranks 29/69/50/13 →
41/50/42/28** (smallest/second-smallest/second-largest/largest; target 28–52 each). Replacing rounded
distractors also removed several that were the key rounded (60 on a key of 62, £7.00 on £6.85, £5.00
on £4.75), the "nearly right" answers a marker might accept.

**THE FINDING THAT MATTERS: A DOOR TOTAL CAN BE FAIR WHILE EVERY TEMPLATE IS A GIFT.** The five mock
papers repeat each template (MCnn-<slot>). Round 1 met its door-level target, and the reviewer then
found it had made the key the SMALLEST on 12 of 13 "how much change" rows. It had moved the
shortcut, not removed it. The door total could not see this. **An instrument that measures a
population can be satisfied by moving the fault into a sub-population it does not measure.** That is
R595's shape (a subset indistinguishable from the whole), arriving through a repair. So
`measure-maths-key-rank.ts` now FLAGS any template or stem shape of 3+ rows where one rank holds three
quarters or more, and exits non-zero while any is flagged. Round 3 cleared seven groups (CALC-02,
CALC-04, CALC-08, GEOM-01, MEAS-04, MEAS-07, a rectangle shape). The "how much change" rows now spread
7/4/2/0.

**STILL FLAGGED (5 templates), with why:**
- **NPV-01**, value of a digit, second-largest 5 of 5. The only real mistakes are face value and one
  column either way, so the key sits second-largest BY CONSTRUCTION. It needs a different distractor
  kind or a different template.
- **FDP-04**, second-largest 5 of 5, and **MEAS-01**, one-price change, smallest 4 of 5. The only honest
  below-key mistakes have no library entry ("bridging to the pound"), or land exactly on the key rounded.
- **FDP-02** and **NPV-07** (4 of 5). The proposed values were refused: 280000 for "hundreds in 2,800",
  and a fitted 36 that would also have left "less than 12" as a tell. They need different values.

**THREE LIBRARY ENTRIES WOULD UNLOCK REAL DIAGNOSES** that are currently mis-tagged or unrepairable:
"halved instead of quartered" (MC04-FDP-02/07/08 carry it as #78 with no percentage present);
"used the angle on the line as an angle of the triangle" (MC05-GEOM-06's 10°, MC02-GEOM-06's 45°);
"bridging to the pound" (MEAS-01). Re-tags this pass fixed every #63 used where no carry is involved
(→ #61) and #12 used on an addition (→ #69).

**ALSO NOTED.** 324 LIVE maths distractors still have no execution (staff-facing). The lander writes one on
every row it touches. MC02-GEOM-03's stem says "46 degrees" in words, which is not house notation, and
the notation gate did not report it.

## R1027 — The value-of-the-digit shortcut closed, and two "templates" that were never templates (David, 2026-11-20)

**THE INSTRUCTION.** David: *"Yes, do NPV-01."* "In the number 4,652, what is the value of the digit
6?" ran on all five papers with the same wrong answers: face value 6, one column right 60, one column
left 6000. So the key was second-largest on 5 of 5, by construction.

**THE ENTRY.** `maths-114-read-from-the-digit-to-the-end`: the child gives 652 for the 6 in 4,652, taking
the digit and everything after it as its value (the 6 starts the spoken chunk "six hundred and
fifty-two"). Drafted by one agent and attested by another through `land-new-entries`. The reviewer was
told the entry existed to break a pattern, which is a motive to fit, and judged it real because the
value comes from one fixed rule applied identically on every row, not chosen row by row. Neither
agent could cite a published frequency, and the entry's note says so. It is distinct from maths-61
(a digit followed by zeros) and maths-62 (the bare digit). Its carriers are the five whole-number rows
only: on decimal rows the move has no single value.

**THE ROWS.** MC03-NPV-01 and MC05-NPV-01 take 283 and 473 in place of 20 and 40. Those were maths-61,
which occurs 26 times on the door and stays on each row's 2000/4000 option. 6 changes attested, 2 rows
signed. NPV-01 drops from 5 of 5 to 3 of 5 at one rank. **Door ranks 40/52/41/28.**

**THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG ABOUT TWO SLOTS.** `measure-maths-key-rank` treated every paper slot
(MCnn-<slot>) as a template. FDP-04 holds five DIFFERENT questions (glasses, adding fractions ×2, a sale
price, a fraction as a decimal), and NPV-07 holds three kinds (hundreds in a number ×2, the largest
decimal, rounding ×2). A child meets the stem, never the slot number, so a rank shared across a mixed
slot is no shortcut. Two rounds of proposers and the reviewer spent effort on a pattern that did not
exist; the reviewer twice called FDP-04 "structural" before the cause was named. Both slots are now
DECLARED mixed in the script, with their kinds written out, and printed on every run. The stem-shape
grouping still screens their rows. Baseline (R149) before and after: exactly those two groups moved
from flagged to declared, and nothing else moved. **Within-template: 0 flagged.** The two pairs inside
NPV-07 (both rounding rows, both hundreds rows) share a rank, and at 2 rows they are below the
3-row floor. A third paper would make them a real group.

note at 1,800 characters. maths-113's note had already lost most of the reviewer's half (2,929 → 1,800),
which was the overlap finding the note was extended to carry. The cut is removed and the note restored

## R1028 — English answer tells: the key is the one with a comma (2026-11-20)

**THE QUESTION.** David: *"do the English measurement."* After vr-08, vr-16 and maths-01, the same
question for the 345 LIVE English comprehension rows: does a surface feature pick the key without
reading? `scripts/agent-review/measure-english-tells.ts` tests each candidate tell. A tell either picks
one option (a unique extreme) or none, and its hits are set against chance (Σ 1/k over the rows where it
picks). Option order is shuffled per child, so position is not a tell.

**WHAT IT FOUND.**
- **The only option with a comma is the key on 38 of 66 rows (58%, chance 24%, ×2.4)**: retrieval
  18 of 27, inference 15 of 23. **The only two-part option** (", and" / "while" / "but") is the key on
  20 of 39 (×2.1), and 11 of 15 in retrieval. Together they point at the key on 45 rows. The rows were
  read before this was believed: keys are written as fuller, qualified, two-claim statements ("A
  sprain, and no bones broken"; "his looks, and … very rich"); distractors as short single claims.
- **Retrieval: the option sharing most words with the cited lines** is the key on 40 of 81 (49%, ×2.0).
  Matching words to the lines is part of retrieval, but distractors that never reuse the window's
  words make word-matching enough on its own.
- **Inference: the longest option by words** is the key on 35 of 78 (45%, ×1.8).
- **No strong door-wide tell** from length alone (×1.2–1.4), hedges (35 picks), absolutes (5), or
  overlap with the stem or the whole passage (all at or below chance).
- **Two distractors restate the stem** and can be ruled out without reading: ENG-028-PR-09 ("The traffic
  under the boards has changed.") and ENG-007-LP-06.

**THE REPAIR, NOT YET DONE.** This is a DISTRACTOR-writing fault, as in maths. The fix is on the wrong
answers: give some of them the key's shape (two claims, a comma, words lifted from the cited lines
with the wrong element, which `en-within-span-wrong-element` already names), and stop writing every key
as the fuller statement. It is English item text, so under R1023 it runs drafter → independent
reviewer → `land-proposals --from-live`, and every change travels back to Cowork in the return
changeset. The measure is the acceptance test: no tell above ×1.5 on 30+ picks door-wide, and none
on 10+ picks within a type.

## R1029 — The English answer tells repaired, and what the repair taught the measure (David, 2026-11-20)

**THE INSTRUCTION.** David, on R1028: *"Yes, repair them."*

**THE REPAIR.** Two rounds under R1021/R1023: four drafters by passage group, independent reviewers, and
`land-proposals --from-live`, so only rows that land leave service. **105 LIVE English rows changed**;
141 changes attested and 15 refused. Every change is in the return changeset to Cowork, with its before
value (`english-rewrite-return`, now 314 rows / 801 field changes across R1023–R1029). The method: on each
row, one DISTRACTOR takes the key's surface shape (a comma, two claims, its length, words from the cited
lines), aiming for a tie. No key was reworded except ENG-001-WIW-06, which was rebuilt and signed.

**RESULT, measured on the live store** (345 comprehension rows):

| tell | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| only option with a comma | 38 of 66, x2.38 | 5 of 35, x0.60 |
| only two-part option | 20 of 39, x2.14 | 5 of 27, x0.77 |
| longest (words) | x1.38 (inference x1.84) | x0.54 |
| most words shared with the cited lines, retrieval | 40 of 81, x2.02 | under x1.5 |
| key in the closest near-twin pair | 21 of 22 (retrieval 17 of 17) | 3 of 5, x1.20 |
| distractors restating the stem | 2 rows | 0 |

**WHAT THE REPAIR TAUGHT THE MEASURE. Three faults were found only by running it on a repair.**
1. **A one-sided target lets a repair FLIP a tell rather than remove it.** Round 1 as drafted met "nothing
   above x1.5" while making the comma option the key on 0 of 30 rows: "never the comma" is a tell too.
   The target is now two-sided for SURFACE tells (x0.5–1.5). It stays one-sided for CONTENT tells
   (overlap with the lines, passage or stem), because ruling out an option the text does not support is
   reading. The ORIGINAL authoring already had that (an option sharing no words with the cited lines
   was the retrieval key 1 time in 77).
2. **A tie-based repair manufactures CONVERGENCE.** Giving a distractor the key's words makes a near-twin
   pair, and "the answer is one of the two nearly identical options" halves the choice. The door-C
   reviewer named this before any measure could. It is now a tell (chance 2/k, the pair must be unique
   and share half its content words). Round 1 had raised it from 14/14 to 17/17 in retrieval; round 2
   broke it.
3. **Two distractors written to beat the measure were refused on sight**: an emphatic "does save" to win a
   stemmed word count, and a lifted phrase to win overlap. A measure that drafters iterate against
   becomes a target. The reviewer reading the row as a child is the guard, and the 15 refusals are
   where it acted.

**BALANCE BY WITHHOLDING, NOT AUTHORING.** Where landing every signed row would push a surface tell below
x0.5, the fewest signed rows were WITHHELD and left LIVE as already reviewed (13 in round 1, 4 in round
2; lists in `tells/withheld-for-balance.json` and `tells/r2/withheld-for-balance.json`). A withheld row
is a correct row that keeps the key as the unique comma or longest option, at the rate chance would
give. Their signed proposals stay on file.

**STILL OUTSIDE THE BAND, NAMED.**
- Inference "longest (words)" x0.44 and "only two-part" x0.43 (1 of 10): mild elimination tells.
  Ruling the longest option out takes a guess from 25% to about 30%.
- Three technique tells (shortest x0.10, only-without-comma, only one-part). These were in the original
  authoring; a technique key ("the writer shows X by Y") is structurally the fullest option.
- Rows held with a reviewer's fix on file (LP-04, LP-15, BB-01, CR-08, HD-11, RR-04, TM-09) stay LIVE as
  they were.
- The door-B reviewer asked whether visible near-twin pairs below the 0.5 threshold (AGG-04 at 0.40,
  LW-05 at 0.43) should count. That is a threshold ruling, not a row fault.

## R1030 — The orderable VR doors: the generator's wrong answers give the key away (2026-11-20)

**THE QUESTION.** David: *"do the number VR check."* This is R1025's maths question asked of every VR door
whose options can be ordered: numbers by value, single letters by alphabet position.
`scripts/agent-review/measure-vr-key-rank.ts`.

**WHAT IT FOUND (LIVE practice rows):**
| door | key rank (0 = smallest) | the shortcut |
|---|---|---|
| vr-14 letter connections | rank 2 on **25 of 25** | always the second-latest letter; and "H" is a distractor on every row shown, so it is never the answer |
| vr-11 number series | 3 options: middle on **12 of 12**; 4 options: smallest on **13 of 13** | every distractor is larger than the key |
| vr-07 letters for numbers | ranks 2–3 on **0 of 25** | the key is always one of the two smallest |
| vr-09 letter series | ranks 0–1 on 23 of 25 | the key is almost always one of the two earliest letters |
| vr-18 related numbers | middle on 14 of 25 | milder |
| vr-17 complete the sum | largest on 0 of 25 | milder |
| vr-19 word-number codes | 10/10/5 | within reason |

The flag rule needs 20 rows per option count, so it missed vr-11's two perfect splits. Read the
table, not the ✗ count.

**THE CAUSE IS THE GENERATOR, NOT A ROW.** The distractors are DERIVED in code
(`buildDerivedVrDistractors`), and every derivation lands on one side of the key. vr-11 uses
off-by-one (+1), step applied twice, and sum of the last two, all above the key. vr-14 uses ±1 and a
direction error that lands on a fixed letter. vr-07's operation slip and dropped term produce larger
totals. Generating to diagnosis made each mistake PREDICTABLE IN DIRECTION, which is the house rule's
warning about predictable distractor types, arriving through value instead of type.

**THE REPAIR IS NOT DONE.** The fix is in the generator: choose derivations that fall on both sides
(off-by-one in either direction, a wrong-direction step, under-counted terms), so each door's key-rank
spread is near uniform. Because these rows are LIVE and reviewed, R62 applies: `content:generate`
refuses to rewrite reviewed rows, so a generator change means re-deriving each door, re-reviewing,
re-signing and republishing under R1021. Measure each door with this script before and after.

**OUTCOME OF THE GENERATOR REPAIR (David: *"Fix the VR generator"*, 2026-11-20).**

*What landed.* **vr-11** (12 rows, all signed): distractors are now chosen among every value the tags
genuinely produce, least-used rank first. Before → after: middle of 3 on 12/12 → 6/6 middle/largest;
smallest of 4 on 13/13 → 7/6 smallest/second-smallest. The generator and the LIVE rows agree on 25/25.

*What the builder is.* `buildSpreadVrDistractors` (core): a value can be offered only if a tag produces it,
so the gate is unchanged. It never offers a `forbidden` value (one printed in the stem, or a letter that
wraps past A or Z). Then it scores, in order: least-used rank, the key not the middle of a run, the most
distinct mistakes, least churn. `buildDerivedVrDistractors` gained the same optional `forbidden`, default
none. Every door that passes nothing re-derives exactly as before, so R62's guard is undisturbed.
`propose-from-generator.ts` turns a generator change into a reviewable proposal (R62's "take the change
to review", made a tool), with executions written FROM the operands. The reviewer refused the generic
vr-07 value-slip template ("for one of the letters") because a sentence that fits every row checks
nothing (R569).

*What did NOT land, and why. Each is a design call, not a tuning problem.*
- **vr-14**: the real shortcut was never rank. Both step-size values (key ± 1) are always offered, so
  **the key is the middle of three consecutive letters on 25 of 25 rows**, before and after any
  rank fix. A third genuine mistake was proposed and REFUSED by the independent reviewer: "applied the
  step twice" is a SERIES mistake, not an analogy one, and the code comment showed the value had come
  before the story. Backward questions (the reviewer's alternative) spread the rank but not the
  run. Needs: a real third mistake, or one step-size value per row (three options would raise a guess
  to 33%), or a ruling.
- **vr-07**: rank-first piled value-slip into 44 of 75 seats, all one side of the key, a new tell of its
  own; variety-first left the key among the two smallest. It also offered code values printed in the
  stem. The fix is in the QUESTIONS: an expression whose last term is sometimes "+" lets term-dropped land
  on either side. Generator left as LIVE.
- **vr-09**: 5 LIVE rows offer the last letter shown as "one short", and 2 offer a wrapped "direction"
  letter (Y from B), both of which Annie's rule excludes. Excluding them leaves 15 rows without three
  honest distractors (on a step-1 series, step-repeat and off-by-one collide), and the key can then only
  sit in the middle two. Needs new genuine mistakes or series that start away from the alphabet's ends.
- **vr-11 and vr-09 keep an adjacency tell**: an off-by-one distractor makes the key one of the only two
  options one apart (vr-11: 23 of 25). That is inherent to offering off-by-one at all, and is
  pre-existing.

*A fault in the landing door, found by the guard.* `land-proposals` wrote option values as TEXT. Since
R1021, vr-17 (25 rows), vr-18 (18) and vr-11 (12) held a numeric key beside "17", "21". The lander now
keeps the stored type. `normalise-option-value-types.ts` converted all 55 rows: it asserted every
option reads identically, acted only where the latest machine signature covered the row, and re-signed
with a method saying nothing a child sees changed.

*The measure grew too.* `measure-vr-key-rank.ts` now reports "key is the middle of a run" and "key in the
only adjacent pair". The first version measured rank only and called vr-14 a rank problem. It was a run
problem all along (R595: a measure can be satisfied while the fault sits where it does not look).

**ROUNDS 2–3: vr-07, vr-09 and vr-14 redesigned and landed (David: *"All three"*, 2026-11-20).** 64 rebuilds
over three review rounds. Round 2 refused all 67 rebuilds, and every refusal was right; round 3 attested
and signed all 64.

*The designs, as landed:*
- **vr-14**: THREE options (step-direction and ONE step-size value), so there is no run of three around
  the key. FOUR SHAPES are cycled evenly: forward or backward question (the reviewer's suggestion,
  after refusing an invented mistake) times near miss one long or one short. Steps 2–4 only: on a step of
  1 the near miss is the printed stem letter. Rejected if the key, the stem letter or any distractor is
  printed in the pair, or the stem letter IS a pair letter.
- **vr-09**: THREE options and FOUR SHAPES (step-repeat or direction, times off-by-one ±1). Steps 2–4,
  nothing wraps, nothing printed, and 25 distinct series (round 2 had 7).
- **vr-07**: four options, one of each mistake. Four-term expressions alternate the minus between the end
  and the middle, so term-dropped lands on both sides. Tier 1 keeps "P + Q − R": in "P − Q + R" every
  neighbouring pair has opposite signs, so a neighbour swap always cancels to a printed value (measured).
  The key is never a printed code value, no running total or option is negative, and walk scripts and
  executions name the swap.

*Result, simple rules a child could learn, LIVE:*

| door | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| vr-14 | middle of the run, 25/25 (certain) | best rule 52%, chance 33%; the one-in-two floor |
| vr-09 | two earliest, 23/25 | best rule 48% |
| vr-07 | two smallest, 25/25 | best simple rule 36%, chance 25% |
| vr-11 | smallest 13/13, middle 12/12 | landed in round 1 |

**THE ONE-IN-TWO FLOOR IS THE HONEST LIMIT, NAMED.** An off-by-one distractor sits next to the key by
definition, so a child who learns "the answer is one of the two neighbouring letters" halves the choice.
That is in the mistake itself, not in how it is placed. Balancing the four shapes guarantees no rule
beats it. vr-07 has a subtler version: a child who reads WHERE the minus sign is narrows to two ranks
(64%, against the 50% such a rule gets on random keys). The reviewer signed on that basis, and the way out
(two value-slips on some rows) has its own cost.

**WHAT THE REVIEW TAUGHT THE BUILDER.** Round 1 balanced the key's RANK and lost which SIDE the near
miss fell on, so "the outer letter of the pair, else the middle" found the key on 25/25 (vr-09) and 22/25
(vr-14). **Balancing one statistic moves the tell into the statistic next to it.** That is the third
time today (English commas to near-twins, maths door totals to templates, VR rank to side), and the
answer each time was to balance the SHAPE of the whole option set, not one number about it.

*Process faults, fixed:*
- Every rebuilt row's walk script was stale; the gate caught only the vr-09 rows where an old letter
  vanished. Walk scripts are now written from the row, and "the letter X" stops bare A and I reading as
  words.
- Taking all 25 rows of vr-09 and vr-14 out of service emptied both cases, and `publish-door --ready`
  then refused. Both were republished in full (25/25 each) minutes later, on dev only. `land-proposals
  --from-live` now refuses a landing that would empty a case unless `--allow-empty-pool` is passed.
- A refused option delete rolls back the whole door's transaction, not just the row (comment
  corrected); it fails safe.

*Not gated, but now prevented by the generator:* negative options, negative running totals, a question
that answers itself, and a key that is the only printed option. The gates do not catch these, and a
hand-authored row could still carry them.

The generator and the LIVE rows agree on all four doors (25/25 unchanged each).

## R1031 — The machine reviewer is calibrated against a person, blind (David, 2026-11-22)

**WHY.** Since R1021 the machine reviewer `rev-agent-01` is the latest signer on **761 of 1,176 LIVE
rows** (ENGLISH 336, VR 346, MATHS 79). Annie (`rev-0001`) is latest on 176 by signature, 9 more by
capital-`Item` signature, 204 by the older APPROVED event and 25 (ENG-003) by her return ruling; 1 is
the dev-only `zz-e2e-fixture-item`. Nobody had measured how often a person would sign what the machine
signs, so every figure since R1021 rests on a judgement whose error rate is unknown.

**THE SAMPLE** (`scripts/agent-review/export-calibration-sample.ts`, seed `calibration-01`, digest
`ebda446551d602e2`): 40 cards. **32 machine-SIGNED LIVE rows** (English 13, VR 13 = one each from 13
of 15 types, maths 6 = one per type) and **8 whole-row rebuilds the machine HELD** (English 4, VR 4,
from 105 held rebuilds). The held cards exist so her sign rate is not the only number. Without them,
nothing tests whether the machine's refusals are right as well.

**BLINDNESS IS ASSERTED, NOT HOPED FOR.**
- Nothing on a card says which kind it is.
- A screen with a carried fixture checks every card for reviewer ids, verdict words, door names and
  item ids. It found 0 leaks.
- Options are shuffled per card, because rebuilds list the key first.
- Hint and walk script must appear at the same rate on both kinds within a district. That check is
  why **VR walk scripts are outside this sample**: a held VR rebuild carries none, so showing them on
  signed VR cards only would tell her which they are.
- No maths card is held, because a held maths rebuild carries no hint either.
- `key.json` says which card is which. It is never delivered.

**DELIVERED** as `~/Downloads/11+/from-cluecrew/calibration-cards-ebda446551d602e2.html`, a single offline page. She records Sign, Hold or Refuse, where the fault is, and a reason, then downloads a return quoting the digest.

**THE SCORE** (`score-calibration.ts`):
- Two numbers: signed → she signs (the false-accept side, the one 761 rows rest on); held → she holds
  or refuses (false-refuse, a cost in speed, not in safety).
- Each comes with a Wilson 95% interval. At n = 32 a bare percentage claims more than it knows.
- A partial return is scored on decided cards only, and the undecided count is printed beside every
  rate.
- A return is matched by digest, never by name.

**WHAT FOLLOWS FROM IT is David's to rule once the return is in.** The proposal:
- If she would sign about 30 of 32 or more, the machine signature stands, with periodic samples.
- If any district shows two or more refusals, re-review that district's machine-signed rows by a
  person.
- Read every disagreement whatever the rate, because a disagreement names a fault class the gates and
  the machine share.

**THE FIRST RETURN, 2026-11-22. Annie is no longer reviewing (David: "no more annie"), so the sample
was read by a second machine reviewer.** It was briefed only with the cards, the reviewer briefs and
CLAUDE.md, and barred from the key, the review files and the database. **This measures agreement
between two machines, not whether a person would sign.** Both learned one standard from the same
documents and can share blind spots, so their agreement is NOT evidence of quality. Their
disagreements ARE evidence: at least one of the two is wrong on each.

- Machine-signed: the second reviewer signs **23 of 32 (72%, 95% CI 55–84%)**. By district: English
  8 of 13, maths 4 of 6, VR 11 of 13. It holds 8 and refuses 1.
- Machine-held: it also holds **3 of 8**. It signs the other 5.

## R1032 — A sentence with a gap is the question: the 16-word cap applies to it (David, 2026-11-22)

**THE RULING.** Asked whether vr-06's gap sentence should keep its exemption from the 16-word cap,
David: *"whatever is best practice."* Best practice is that the cap protects what the child must read
to answer. So: **a `stem.sentence` containing a gap marker (`___`) is the question and keeps the stem
role and its cap. Only a gapless carrier sentence takes the word-card role.** The gapless carrier is
vr-04's, which only picks the sense. The August exemption (`12f52c8`) was ruled for vr-04 and swept
vr-06 in under "one field, one rule". The line is drawn on the CONTENT (is there a gap?), not on a
list of question types, so a new gap-sentence type is capped without anyone remembering to add it.

**INSTRUMENT CHANGE, BASELINED (R149).** `checkItemChildFacing`, before and after, over 1,227 items:
- blocked went from 12 to 15;
- newly failing: exactly `bank-vr-06-missing-word-23`, `-35` and `-40`, each a sentence-length fault;
- 0 newly passing and 0 changed;
- no vr-04 row moved.

The test that asserted the old behaviour now asserts the new one, and a within-cap case is added.

**THE THREE ROWS** were split into two sentences each, with the gap, key, options, tags and
executions unchanged. A drafting agent proposed the splits; a separate reviewer counted every
sentence itself, then attested and signed them. They landed `--from-live` and were republished, so
vr-06 has 40 of 40 LIVE. Re-diff against the baseline: blocked is back to 12, with 0 newly failing.

**FOUND ALONGSIDE, NOT ACTED ON: vr-06 IS NOT THE GL QUESTION TYPE ITS PROMPT DESCRIBES.**
- The prompt says "Three letters that make a word are missing". GL's missing three-letter-word type
  is built on that rule: the three missing letters are themselves a word (MO___ + USE = MOUSE), and
  a child uses it as a strategy.
- Of 40 LIVE keys, only about 9 are three-letter words a child knows: OUT, TON, ASH, PET, FOR, BIN,
  SIN, FUR, FEE.
- About 11 more are dictionary oddities: USH, BAS, GAR, PER, DON, BUR, OSE, LAR, OLE, SOL, DOC.
- 20 are not words at all, for example EAD, PLA, CLE, SPO and DEF.
- So the bank practises "complete the word in the sentence", a cloze-spelling skill, not the GL
  type. Annie signed these rows under the same prompt, so this was the design, not a slip.
- Making it GL-faithful means rebuilding about 31 rows: a new target word whose missing letters
  spell a known three-letter word, with three-letter-word distractors.
- That is a type-design decision and is left to David.

## R1033 — A Cowork-authored row returns whatever its door is called (2026-11-22)

**THE FAULT.** `land-proposals.ts` decided whether a door carries changes back to the authoring store
by the door's NAME (`english-rewrite/*`). "Cowork authors, the DB holds" covers every Cowork-authored
item, so **7 Cowork-authored VR rows landed with no return**:
- `bank-vr-04-closest-meaning-30` (vr-04, R1021);
- `bank-vr-06-missing-word-15` and `-17` (vr-06, R1021);
- `bank-vr-06-missing-word-36` (calibration-fix/vr);
- `bank-vr-06-missing-word-23`, `-35` and `-40` (calibration-fix/vr-06-cap).

Found while preparing the vr-06 rebuild, which would have made it 40 rows.

**THE FIX.** The lander now returns by AUTHORSHIP: any landed row whose `authoredBy` is
`ai-draft:cowork*` goes into the door's `changeset.json`. A generated row in the same door (vr-04 `gen-*`)
does not, because Cowork holds no copy of it. `export-agent-review-return.ts` delivers every changeset
outside `english-rewrite/` as the `agent-review-return` family, finding doors by walking for
`changeset.json` (R57), never from a list. All 7 rows were backfilled. Each door's packet has only
one version, written before landing, so it is the true before state; after is the DB now. Each row is
marked `backfilled` with that provenance. Delivered: 7 rows, 8 field changes.

**NOT COVERED, STATED.** Maths rows are `authoredBy: maths staging import` or `amended maths source`,
not Cowork, so they do not return. Whether maths has an authoring store that should receive them is
unexamined.

## R1034 — Cowork is retired: the database is the only content store (David, 2026-11-22)

**THE RULING.** David: *"not using cowork anymore you need to manage it all."* Cowork is no longer
an authoring store, and Annie is no longer reviewing (R1031). **This repository and its database
author, review, hold and serve all content.** Agents draft. A separate agent reviews and signs as
`rev-agent-01`, never under a person's name (R94/R1021). The DB is authoritative for every field.

**WHAT IT SUPERSEDES.**
- "ONE DIRECTION ONLY FOR AUTHORED ITEM CONTENT: COWORK AUTHORS, THE DB HOLDS" (CLAUDE.md, R23-era).
  There is no other side to drift from. Edits are made here, through the gated doors.
- "LIBRARY TEXT: THE DB AUTHORS, COWORK PROPOSES TRANSFORMS." The DB authors library text, and
  nobody else proposes.
- The return leg (R88, R579, R588, R1023 condition 5, R1033). Nothing is owed back. The CI step
  `check:return-leg` is removed. `check:return-sequence`, `check:manifest-diff`,
  `check:arrival-confirmed`, `export:pilot`/`import:pilot` and the outbound folder
  `~/Downloads/11+/from-cluecrew` are retired with it. The scripts stay as history.

**WHAT IT KEEPS.** Each door's `changeset.json` (field, before, after) is still written. It is the
in-repo audit of what an agent changed. It now exists for this repo's own history and is no longer a
delivery, so the lander no longer delivers returns. Every gate stays. Every signing rule stays. The
reviewed-content guard (R62) stays. The fault it guards against was never about Cowork.

**WHAT IT COSTS, STATED.** The two-store arrangement held a check that is now gone: a second party
read the content with a different method. Nothing replaces that except the separate reviewing agent
and the blind calibration sample (R1031). On that sample, the second machine reviewer disagreed on 9
of 32 machine-signed rows, and every factual claim it made was confirmed. Machine review is the only
review now, so periodic blind calibration between independent agents is the standing check.

## R1035 — vr-06 Missing Word rebuilt to the GL rule (David, 2026-11-22)

**THE RULING.** David: *"Yes, rebuild them."* The GL missing three-letter-word question rests on one
rule: the three missing letters are a word by themselves. Of the 40 LIVE keys, only about 9 were

## R1039 — the content snapshot: CI reads the real store (David: "Yes, build the snapshot", 2026-11-22)

**BUILT.** `scripts/content-snapshot.ts` (`pnpm snapshot:export | snapshot:restore | check:snapshot`).
The snapshot holds 14 tables of content and provenance, 45,652 rows (11 MB):
- QuestionType, Region, Case, Word, Misconception, Item, ItemOption and ItemOptionTag;
- Reviewer, AttributionEvent, FamilyBankSignature and NvrTemplateSignature;
- ContentWriteLog and AdminAuditLog.

That set is closed under foreign keys, and no family, child, session, billing or webhook table is
exported. The format is one COPY-text TSV per table, with columns named and rows ordered by primary
key under the C collation. The manifest has no clock, so re-exporting unchanged content is
byte-identical and `git diff` on the snapshot is the content diff.

**Restore refuses three things:**
- any non-empty target table (it never merges into a store);
- a migration mismatch;
- a file whose digest differs from the manifest (a hand edit).

Restore loads in one transaction with triggers off, so the write log keeps dev's history and not
45,000 rows of "restore wrote this". It then re-reads the DATABASE and compares it table by table
with the files (R60 question 3).

**THE ROUND TRIP IS NOT FRESHNESS, AND IT SAYS SO ON EVERY RUN.** In CI, a matching `check` proves
the restore was faithful. Only a run against dev proves the committed snapshot is current, and CI
has no dev.

**MEASURED** in a throwaway worktree against fresh en_US databases, with the restore step after the
migration drift check:
- Restore: 45,652 of 45,652 rows faithful, digest `bb940792ce412fbc`.
- CI went from 33 of 73 failing to 30 of 74.
- 11 steps that failed now pass:
  - signed-family fingerprints and bank content;
  - verdict refusals;
  - serving path;
  - shipped clusters;
  - cloze gaps;
  - error-spot preview;
  - authority shape;
  - lint and the scripts typecheck, fixed under R1038.
- 7 steps FAIL FOR THE FIRST TIME because they now read real content. That is the snapshot working,
  not a regression:
  - **Seed:** the free-tier floor refuses because `case-maths-01` exists (since 2026-08-29) and no
    Maths case is listed free. The seed has refused against the real store since that day; nobody
    ran it. Which Maths case is free is a pricing decision for David.
  - **Generate:** `content:generate` would cut 10 words from the APPROVED `vr02-surface-link`
    childHint, and the R213 guard refuses. The generator's copy of library text has drifted from the
    store.
  - **db-content:** 15 SERVING faults, including three maths stems over the 16-word cap
    (MC04-CALC-08, MC05-CALC-08, MC05-STATS-01).
  - **every-string-field:** 153 faults.
  - **option-positions:** en-spag-punct-spot (56%) and en-spag-spelling-spot (67%) serve the key in
    one position.
  - **verify:solutions:** 187 of 187 maths items fail. This is its FIRST population ever (R61).
    Every row failing points at the instrument before the content (R599); not yet read.
  - **register:** this entry closes it.

**HELD: THE SNAPSHOT IS NOT COMMITTED.** The GitHub repository is PUBLIC. Committing the snapshot
would publish the whole item bank, the signatures, and a personal email address that appears 4,351
times in AttributionEvent. The code is committed. `packages/db/snapshot/` is gitignored until David
rules, and the CI restore step is held with it. The options:
- make the repository private, then commit the snapshot as is;
- encrypt the snapshot with a key held as a CI secret, which loses the readable diff;
- keep it out of git and have CI fetch it with a secret.

**ENCRYPTED, NOT HELD** (David, 2026-11-22: "Encrypt it instead"). The repository stays public. The
snapshot is in git as `packages/db/snapshot.enc`, 1.3 MB: AES-256-GCM over the gzipped tables, with
the manifest digest as authenticated data. Beside it is `packages/db/snapshot.manifest.json`, which
is plain and holds tables, columns, row counts and digests, with no names and no addresses. A content
change therefore shows in review as a changed count and digest, not as readable text: that is the
diff this choice gives up.
- The key is `SNAPSHOT_KEY`, in the root `.env` (gitignored) and as a GitHub Actions secret, set on
  2026-11-22. It was never printed.
- GCM needs a fresh IV every time, so `snapshot.enc` is rewritten only when the digest changes.
  Re-exporting unchanged content leaves it byte-identical (verified).
- Export decrypts what it just wrote and compares every table before it returns.
- Restore always decrypts the COMMITTED file and never the local TSVs, so it loads what CI loads.
- Measured on a fresh migrated database:
  - no key: refused, 0 rows written;
  - wrong key: refused on authentication, 0 rows written;
  - real key: 45,652 of 45,652 rows faithful;
  - a second restore into the loaded database: refused.
- **Limits:**
  - Pull requests from forks get no secrets, so they cannot restore, and the step fails rather than
    skips.
  - If the key is lost, the file cannot be read. The dev database is the source, so re-export with a
    new key and reset the secret.
  - Each content change adds about 1.3 MB to the git history.

## R1040 — the seven checks CI could finally see (David: "Fix the 7 new failures", 2026-11-22)

Loading the real store (R1039) turned seven CI steps red for the first time. Each one is now
resolved. Three were instrument faults, three were content, and one needed a ruling. Two of the
rulings below are David's own words.

**1. GENERATE: the generator overwrote approved library text on every run.** `generate-content.ts`
upserted its own July copy of 45 VR library entries, both `description` and `childHint`, each time
it ran. On 2026-11-22, 30 of those 45 differed from the store, and every one was approved, by Annie
or by rev-agent-01. The only reason no approved hint was ever lost is that the generator had not
run against dev since those approvals. The first CI run that tried it replaced three entries before
R213's no-cut guard stopped it on the fourth. That guard catches cuts only, so a longer old wording
would have gone in silently. **Fixed:** the generator now creates missing entries and never updates
existing ones (`update: {}`). The DB authors library text (R1034).

**2. SEED: the free-tier floor and the Maths case.** RULING (David): **"Keep Maths paid."**
`case-maths-01` is the only Maths case and was built paid. The floor of two free cases per district
(capped at the number of cases) would have made it free, giving away the whole district. The seed
had refused against the real store since 2026-08-29, and nobody had run it. **Fixed:** MATHS is
added to `FLOOR_EXEMPT_DISTRICTS` with the reason, and the exemption is printed on every seed run.
Revisit it when Maths has a second case.

**3. check:db-content: 15 SERVING faults → 0.**
- **Instrument (7):**
  - The check never passed the reviewer's clearance record to the gate, unlike publish-door,
    gate-baseline and check-gate-silence. That left two positions cleared under R1005 failing for
    ever.
  - It gated the two case doorplates as `narrative`, when R689 moved them to `doorplate` (no word
    cap). The role is now chosen from the fact that a record exists at
    `content/case-faces/<id>.json`.
  - Before 15 faults, after 8, and the diff by name is exactly those 7 rows (R149).
- **Content (8), landed through `ci-fix/content-01` and its round 2:**
  - three maths stems over the 16-word cap, each split in two;
  - three vr-10 walk scripts naming words not on the card;
  - two VR rows whose KEY was "pot". A flagged key routes every time (R1005), so the keys became
    "jug" and "vase".
  - The drafter also found a walk on gen-vr-03-related-words-10 written for a different item. The
    gate's `wordOptionsNamedNotOnCard` cannot see a walk that is entirely about another item. That is
    an open instrument gap.

**4. check:every-string-field: 20 undeclared paths (R720).** The 153 punctuation notes are
staff-field reports and never failed the check; only the undeclared paths did. Each path was
declared from a fact:
- child: `stem.code.A/I/T` (the vr-19 card), `stem.wordWithGap` (rendered by plain-item and
  stowaway), and `options[].content.value[]` (vr-02 pairs). These are notation-bearing.
- staff: `banListException.*` and `sendHistory.*`. No file under apps/web or packages/ui names
  either root.

**5. check:option-positions: two unshuffled banks.** en-spag-punct-spot (A held 56%) and
en-spag-spelling-spot (A held 67%) serve their segments in order, so the position IS where the error
sits. Seven items were rebuilt to move the error. One round-2 rebuild was held, a 30-word sentence
cut to 23. Both banks now read A2 B2 C2 D2 N1 and A2 B2 C2 D1 N2.

**6. verify:solutions: 187 of 187.** RULING (David): **"Add them, reviewed."** The Maths district
went LIVE without the `solution` expression its spec requires (BUILD-DISTRICT-MATHS §5). R61's
declaration said "remove this the moment a maths item reaches the database"; 187 did on 2026-08-29,
and the declaration stood for three months because CI could not see them.
- **Blind drafting.** The drafter saw the question text and the key's UNIT, never its value.
- **Result:** 177 expressions matched their keys and 10 keys are not a single number (6
  coordinates, 3 clock times or durations, 1 named choice). rev-agent-01 attested all 187 after
  reading every row. The 177 have landed (`land-solutions.ts`, which writes `solution` only). The 10
  are declared in `content/maths-noncomputable-keys.json`, and the gate prints them on every run and
  fails if one ever reads as a number. The gate now uses requirePopulation.
- **ZERO MISMATCHES WAS INVESTIGATED, NOT ACCEPTED (R173).** A key check cannot see a wrong answer
  that EQUALS the key. Screening every option against the computed value found one:
  - **MC05-MEAS-03 offered "£4.30" and "£4.3".** The tag `maths-31` (writing £3.5 for £3.50) puts
    the slip in the ANSWER there, so that option was a second correct answer. On its other carrier,
    MC04-MEAS-04, the slip sits in the working and gives a genuinely different amount.
  - The fix went through two review rounds. Round 1 was refused: a stale tag on C, and a
    £3.30/£4.30/£5.30 run with the key in the middle. Round 2: £13.30 (maths-13) and C retagged
    maths-69.
- **THE PARSER MISREAD THREE KEY SHAPES.** `optionNumericValue` read "5/8" as 5, "4:15 pm" as 4 and
  "1 h 30 min" as 1, the leading digits every time. A fraction key would have matched any expression
  computing its numerator. It now reads fractions and mixed numbers by value and refuses times,
  coordinates and two-quantity values. The stale-declaration guard caught the last of these on its
  first run.
- **REPLAYS STAY OFF.** The worked-example replay on a miss is built from this same expression and
  prints the raw trace, for example "18 * 145 makes 2610.", with no £, no commas, fractions as
  decimals, and an em dash in its template. None of that passes a gate. No child had ever seen it
  only because nothing had an expression. `orchestrator.ts` now replays only when an item's
  explanation NAMES a template, which no item does yet. Fixing the replay text is its own task.

**7. check:register:** this entry.

**Also:**
- The three agent-review landers (land-proposals, publish-door, land-library) and land-solutions now
  re-export the content snapshot as their final `--apply` step.
- Noted, not fixed:
  - MC04-NPV-06 and MC05-NPV-06 are temperature answers given as bare numbers with a hyphen for the
    minus sign, which breaks house notation; the notation gate does not see it.
  - gen-vr-10-word-connections-11's "little" carries the tag vr03-same-topic, but it is a synonym of
    the first pair's answer.

**Second CI pass: two more things the real store exposed.**
- **The generator no longer describes 13 VR types.** Once the library overwrite was fixed,
  `content:generate` reached its item loop. There the reviewed-content guard (R62) refused 22 vr-03
  rows. Measured across all 19 generated types, the derivation would revert **292 reviewed LIVE
  rows** in 13 types and writes 0 rows anywhere. Those rows were rewritten by rulings (R1035–R1037
  and this entry), and the July tables were never updated. Those 13 types join `BANK_OWNED_TYPES`,
  which the generator and `check:generator-agreement` both read. The 6 types where the derivation
  still reproduces every stored row (vr-01, 07, 09, 12, 14, 15) stay generator-owned, so a code

## R1042 — superseded values leave the field they supersede: the migration R358 deferred

**2026-11-23, carried out from the session working on CI (R1041).** R358 found old wordings stored
INSIDE the field they replaced, so anything walking the container reads them as live. It skipped them
in the gate, reported them, and deferred the move. The ruled target is Cowork's: the history goes in a
`_superseded` SIBLING outside the container.

**The population was larger than the check said, and in a place it did not look.** By 2026-11-23,
`check:superseded-inside-field` reported only top-level keys of `stem` and `explanation`. Read at
every depth, and in option `content` too (the gate's own rule, `isSuperseded`), the population was
**216 items, all LIVE, 592 instances, 29 shapes**. That includes 116 options carrying
`content._previousValue` and 14 carrying `content._previousMisconceptionId`, plus
`stem.quotes[n]._previousText`. None of those were visible. Same fault as R595: a subset of a real
population, indistinguishable from it because nothing showed what was excluded.

**Storage: a sibling column, `superseded`, on `Item` and `ItemOption`** (migration
`20261123120000_superseded_outside_field`). The shape is `{ version: 1, entries: [{ container, path,
key, value }] }`: every value verbatim, with the exact path and key it sat under. Two alternatives were
rejected:
- **AttributionEvent provenance.** An event records an ACT, with an actor and a time, and most of
  these values carry neither. R358's August 36 pre-date every changeset, so writing them as events
  would invent the act (R98, R94).
- **Door changesets.** They hold the R1037 rounds only, and they live in files, not the store.

The column holds the history; `field-dispositions.ts` declares it RETENTION by name
(`isSupersededColumn`), so `check:every-string-field` reads it as before-images (R715) and not as prose.

**The migration classifies before writing (R62)** (`scripts/move-superseded-outside-field.ts`;
helpers in `scripts/lib/superseded.ts`, which the check also calls, so the two cannot disagree). For
each row it asserts all of the following before any write:
- the lifted entries restore to the stored container exactly;
- the retention-excluded and canonical-order hashes are unchanged;
- no `_`-key survives the lift.

It also classifies every stored `subjectHash` on the affected items, trying every option order (R936).
The 361 hashes split three ways:
- **158 reproduce over the excluded projection.** The move cannot touch them.
- **171 reproduce under no projection today (UNKNOWN).** The move cannot change that either: after
  the move a row's included projection equals its excluded one, and these hashes already fail to
  match it. That is 119 SIGNED (all carrying the canonical-order spec), 32 APPROVED, 18 AMENDED and
  2 UNATTRIBUTED. Most predate a later amendment, but they were not investigated here.
- **32 were taken over the retention-INCLUDED projection, on 31 items.** These would stop reproducing.
  26 were the item's only reproducing signature: 25 `gen-vr-19-word-number-codes` rows plus
  `MC01-FDP-03`. The other 6 were approvals on 5 maths rows that also carry a safe signature.

**Those 31 went through a reviewed door, not a silent void.** The script writes
`content/agent-review/superseded-move/packet.json` with before, after, what moves out and the hashes
that stop reproducing. A separate agent then reviewed it as `rev-agent-01`
(`SUPERSEDED-MOVE-REVIEWER.md`): structure checked by its own script, every code and calculation
recomputed, every row read as a child. It returned **28 SIGN and 3 HOLD**. Only a SIGN over the
packet's pre-image digest lets a row move. The new signature is over the canonical-order subject,
recorded through `recordSignature`.

**THE THREE HOLDS ARE A LIVE CONTENT FAULT THE MIGRATION SURFACED, NOT CAUSED.**
`gen-vr-19-word-number-codes-03`, `-13` and `-23` ask a child to encode **SPAS**, a British
playground slur (a variant of "spaz"). They are LIVE, and `scan:vocab` does not know the word.
- **They were not moved.** Moving them would stop their pin reproducing with nothing signed in its
  place.
- **They are frozen in `check:superseded-inside-field` by id and exact count.** Any new instance
  fails. A change to a frozen count fails. A freeze that no longer matches its row fails as stale.
- **Replacing the word is a reviewed authoring task**, and so is any decision to pull them from
  serving. The word also belongs in the vocabulary scanner. Open.

**Applied.** 213 items moved, with 580 entries now outside the containers (462 from stem and
explanation, 116 options). Each moved item carries an AMENDED event (`migration:superseded-outside-field`),
and 28 new SIGNED events were recorded by `rev-agent-01`. Verified afterwards:
- every hash that reproduced before still reproduces (143 SIGNED, 11 APPROVED, 4 AMENDED);
- the 29 included-projection pins on moved rows no longer reproduce, as predicted, and each of
  those items carries a new reproducing signature.

`check:outside-writes`, `signing-doors`, `authority-shape`, `db-content`, `every-string-field`,
`source-quotes`, `walkscript-reach`, `declared-unread`, `db-invariants`, `migration-replay` and
`derived-writes` all pass. The snapshot was re-exported, and its delta is exactly this change: 241
events and 329 write-log rows.

**Instance count: 0 outside the 3 held rows.** `check:superseded-inside-field` now FAILS, and runs in
CI after `check:every-string-field`. `SWEEP-FIX.md` points drafters at the column. The gate's
`isSuperseded` skip stays as defence in depth.

**Open:** the three SPAS rows (above). There are also 50 moved LIVE items with no reproducing SIGNED
hash under any declared subject. That was already true before the move and is unchanged by it, but
nothing has read it as a population yet.

## R1048 — the SPAS three: the word replaced, the rows re-signed, the hold lifted (David: "Replace the word in the three SPAS items", 2026-11-23)

**The word is the family's, so it changed in the derivation first.** `gen-vr-19-word-number-codes-03`,
`-13` and `-23` were the third slot of `wordNumberCodes` (generate-content.ts), which cycles ten words
over 25 rows. Changing only the rows would have made `content:generate` fail on them under R62, or
rewrite them back. **SPAS → SITS**, chosen under the family's own constraints:
- it uses only the coded letters A I P S T;
- it repeats a letter, so `vr19-shared-letter-miss` is a real act;
- it codes to a non-palindrome, so key, reverse and slip are three distinct values;
- it is vocab tier 1 like SPAS, so the family's tier ladder does not move. PITTA was the first
  candidate and would have gone to tier 3;
- it passes the appropriateness screen (v3-2026-11-23).

SITS is also the first word in the family to use T, so each row's T digit (3, 1, 2) now matters.
`regenerate-vr19.ts`, a historical script, gets the same list so the two derivations agree.

**Through a reviewed door** (`scripts/agent-review/replace-vr19-spas.ts`, `content/agent-review/vr19-spas/`).
- The lander takes stem and option values from `wordNumberCodes` itself (R429).
- The drafter wrote the six executions in the family's house form.
- A separate agent, as `rev-agent-01`, encoded every row itself: 9739/9379/9730, 9719/9179/9710 and
  9729/9279/9720. It **attested 6 of 6 executions and signed 3 of 3 rows**.
- The lander refuses on a moved pre-image, on a missing verdict, or on any blocking child-facing fault.
- After landing, `classifyDerivedWrites` over all 25 rows reports **25 reviewed-and-unchanged, 0
  blocked**, so `content:generate` stays a no-op.

**History stays outside the container (R1042).** The August `_previousPrompt`/`_previousValue` keys
moved into `superseded`, and the SPAS wording joined them there, stamped with this ruling and date.
The replaced executions are verbatim in each AMENDED event's note.

**The hold lifted (R1043).** All three moved from `SERVING_HOLDS` to `LIFTED_HOLDS`, never removed
silently. VR SERVABLE went from 615 back to 618. `check:superseded-inside-field` has no frozen rows
left: 0 instances, 604 entries in the column.

**Checks.** `check:db-content` passes. It failed exactly these three rows under R1044, and now
reports all 1660 serving rows pass. Also passing: `serving-path`, `every-string-field`,
`outside-writes`, `signing-doors`, `authority-shape`, `vr-distractors`, `generator-agreement`,
`db-invariants`, `snapshot`, `derived-writes` and 797 core tests.

**A NUMBER COLLISION, RECORDED AND NOT REWRITTEN.** This door's six events (3 AMENDED and 3 SIGNED on
the three rows) carry "R1047" in their `method`. The vault session took R1047 concurrently for
its seven-card redraft, and both landed before either reached the register. Those events belong
to THIS entry. They are not rewritten, because an attribution record is evidence (R65). The
reviewed `packet.json` and `BRIEF.md` also say R1047 and are left byte-for-byte as reviewed.
The lesson is R178's: a ruling number is looked up at the moment of writing. Two sessions read
the same last heading.

**The snapshot committed with this entry also carries the vault session's seven landed redrafts**
(14 events and 7 write-log rows on `Word`), because it is a picture of the one store. Their register
entry and scripts are theirs to commit.

## R1049 — the dependency audit, first run against real CI in months (David: "Yes, patch it", 2026-11-23)

The audit step had been skipped behind failing steps, so its first local run against the real setup
found 20 high or critical advisories, 3 of them **unauthenticated remote code execution in Next.js
15.5.22**.
- **Next.js:** floor raised to `^15.5.29`, the latest 15.5 patch (2026-11-03), which carries every
  fix from 15.5.28. `pnpm install` had left the lockfile on 15.5.22 while the manifest said
  `^15.5.29`, and `--frozen-lockfile` did not notice. Only `pnpm add next@^15.5.29` moved the
  resolved version, which is why the lockfile entry is now checked by eye.
- **Patch-level transitive fixes**, under the existing override rule (2026-08-08: override, never
  ignore, a patch that lands cleanly): sharp ≥0.35.5, brace-expansion (three lines), js-yaml ≥4.3.2,
  source-map-js ≥1.2.2, vite ≥7.3.7, effect ≥3.22.1.
- **Measured:** audit at 2 critical and 2 high, all needing a major version (tinypool via vitest 4,
  deepmerge-ts via Prisma, zod 3→4). Typecheck is clean, core 797 and web 41 tests pass, and
  `pnpm build` compiles on 15.5.29.

## R1050 — hollow takes its ratified tier; transparent's would move a LIVE item, so it waits (David: "Apply the ratified tiers to hollow and transparent", 2026-11-23)

On 2026-08-02 David ratified two superseded vault cards' tier moves on corpus evidence: hollow
1 → 2 and transparent 5 → 3. Each card's supersedeNote records the move, yet both rows still held
the old tier.

**Why they reverted.** The write log starts on 2026-08-16. From then on, every seed run wrote both
rows with no column changes, so the old tiers were already back by then. The seed (`seedWords`)
upserts every field of `content/words/words.json` over the store unconditionally, and that file
still carried tier 1 and tier 5. The cause falls before the log can see (R62's boundary), but the
seed is the only routine writer of those values. So **a tier fix must land in the store AND in
words.json**, or the next seed undoes it. `scripts/apply-ratified-vault-tier.ts` writes both
together and refuses unless the card's own note records a ratified move.

**hollow: applied.** Store and words.json are both at tier 2, with one AMENDED event
(actor `ruling:david`).
- hollow is a VOCAB_BANK card (bank rarity 1, both halves). The guard holds (`VOCAB_GUARD_OK`
  true → true), and `vocabTier` gives the same item tiers at rarity 1 or 2. So the family's output
  is unchanged.
- The bank's hardcoded rarity 1 now differs from the vault's 2, with identical output. It is left
  alone because the bank is a signed family.
- LIVE items: bank-vr-04-closest-meaning-07 has an authored tier, and gen-vr-04-closest-meaning-07
  derives T2 → T2 (the key "empty" already sets it).

**transparent: REFUSED by the door, so it needs a decision.** The generator derives item difficulty
from words.json: `vocabTierOfSet([headword, key])`, read through `packages/db/prisma/difficulty.ts`.
With transparent at 3, LIVE gen-vr-04-closest-meaning-38 ("clear") would derive **T3 instead of
T5**. That is a change to a reviewed item, which the reviewed-content guard would fail in CI. The
vault tier and the item tier are one decision: apply both, with the item re-tiered through review,
or neither.

**Found on the way, and not fixed here.** All 120 seed words' `definitionChild` in the store differ
from words.json. The August house-style rewrite went into the store, never into the file. Any seed
run, CI included, would rewrite them: 117 of them LIVE, and hollow's whole replacement card back to
the 2026-08-02 card it superseded. It is the R62 class on Word, the table with no reviewed-content
guard. It is a separate fix: either make `seedWords` create-only, or guard it with
`classifyDerivedWrites`'s shape.

**Number collision.** The event and the supersedeNote written for hollow say "R1048". That number
was free when the script ran and was taken by another session before this entry. Recorded here,
not rewritten.

**zod 3 -> 4 and vitest 3 -> 5** (David: "upgrade zod to v4", "upgrade vitest and prisma too", 2026-11-23).
- **zod 4.6.7** clears the memory-exhaustion advisory. That one mattered at runtime: zod parses
  request bodies in 11 API routes, and no request-size cap was found. The one break the typechecker
  reported was `z.record` with a single argument, so 16 call sites now pass an explicit
  `z.string()` key (zod 3's implicit default), changed by a bracket-counting rewrite that leaves
  two-argument calls alone.
- **The zod checks still bite.** Errors are read through `.error.issues`, which zod 4 keeps. The
  same 78 content files validate, the pilot-exclusion canary is still rejected, and a malformed
  word file and a malformed case file are refused.
- **vitest 5.1.1 and @vitest/coverage-v8 5.1.1** drop tinypool, which carried the 2 critical
  advisories. The coverage gate was proved live: with a 100.1% line threshold it fails on all four
  gated files, and it passes at 90%.
- **Measured:** core 797 and web 41 tests pass, typecheck and lint are clean, `pnpm build` passes,
  and the audit is down to deepmerge-ts (high, under Prisma), which the Prisma 7 upgrade clears.
- **CORRECTION, the same day.** "Typecheck clean" above was true of the zod step and NOT re-run
  after the vitest bump. Vitest 3 had been supplying `@types/node` to packages/core by accident; vitest
  5 does not, so `3be5916` left core's typecheck failing (node:fs, process, console). Core now declares
  `@types/node` itself, pinned at the version packages/db uses. All four packages typecheck.

## R1051 — the word-door e2e test asserted a proxy; it now asserts the reviewed act (2026-11-23)

Reported by the product-build session. `apps/web/e2e/word-draft-door.spec.ts` "every imported vault
card is DRAFT and names its author" failed on a database restored from a snapshot holding the R1045
and R1047 publications. It asserted that no `ai-draft:cowork-okafor-v1` card is ever LIVE.

**Ruling: the test was stale, not the door.** The spec's header and the CHECK
`word_live_needs_reviewer`, added in the same 2026-08-02 change, both set up a REVIEW door for
imported cards, and a door exists to be passed through. "Never LIVE" described the state on the day
nothing had been reviewed. It was a proxy for the rule: nothing an agent drafted reaches a child
unless a reviewer approved it.

**The first rewrite was REFUSED by rev-agent-01, and rightly** (eight holes). It demanded evidence only
for a `reviewer:` value, so any human-looking name passed on the bare field. That is R94 and R203: a
name in a field asserts the review that the record is supposed to prove. Its self-review check
compared strings from two different naming schemes and could never fire. It also screened by two
author prefixes, so a mislabelled card escaped both the CHECK and the test, and it printed no
population. The reviewer's findings are in `content/agent-review/vault/review-door-test-R1051.json`.

**The test now (`servingDoorFaults`), after a second refusal.** Round 2 found three more holes, all
closed. (1) A non-`reviewer:` value was accepted over ANY approval, so `reviewedBy: "Annie"` over a
rev-agent-01 approval passed. That is a machine verdict wearing a person's name, R94 itself. (2)
Fixtures were excluded by the `zz-e2e-` PREFIX, which any writer could pick. (3) `seed` passed
unchecked, and the CHECK exempts it too. Over every LIVE card except this spec's two fixtures
(excluded by id), 176 today:
- `seed` is checked against the IDS the seed writes: the ids in `content/words/words.json` plus its
  fixture card `zz-e2e-fixture-word`. 118 cards today. It checks ids only, not content: a `seed` card
  whose text has drifted from the file still passes, which is the seed's own guard to fix (R1050);
- `ai-draft:` and `agent:` are agent-authored (58 today). Any other author, null included, fails;
- an agent-authored card needs `reviewedBy: reviewer:<id>` AND an APPROVED event under that same
  Reviewer row. The event must come from an actor with no AUTHORED or AMENDED event on the card, and
  must be no earlier than the card's last edit, so the approval covers the version that serves;
- or the card is a NAMED exception, keyed by id, carrying its sign-off digest in `reviewNotes`, and
  cited here.

The population is printed, and an empty one fails (R60). A second test runs eight canaries inside a
rolled-back transaction and asserts each one is caught:
- a bare human name;
- a machine reviewer with no event;
- a self-approval;
- an undeclared author;
- a person's name over a machine approval;
- an approval older than the last edit;
- a false `seed` label;
- the exception's digest removed.

All three DB-only tests were run with Playwright (no web server) and pass. In round 1, before this
entry existed, the main test failed on exactly the missing citation.

**The one declared exception: `gave-a-disgust`.** Published 2026-08-22 by
`scripts/run-idiom-containment.ts` on Annie's ninety-ninth return (sha256 `cb80fc2f…`, in the card's
reviewNotes). That was before landers wrote attribution events, so its review exists as that
signed return and not as an event.

**Raised, not fixed:** Annie's Reviewer row (`rev-0001`) still has `heldUntil` null, though R1031
ended her reviewing on 2026-11-22. Until that is corrected, no check can test that an approver held
the role at the time. The content-hash pin is also not done. A recorded edit after an approval
is caught, by event order. What a pin would add: catching an edit written with NO event, and an
edit in the same millisecond as its approval (one landing writes both, so ties pass by design).
